cirneco-cons-ampd2-study-2024.name: Murgiano et al. (2024) - Frameshift Variant in AMPD2 in Cirneco dell'Etna Dogs with Retinopathy and Tremors (Genes)
cirneco-cons-ampd2-study-2024.note: Peer-reviewed study (Genes 2024;15(2):238, PMID: 38397227, PMCID: PMC10887799) identifying a 1-bp frameshift deletion in exon 15 of AMPD2 on CFA6 (g.42,698,170delC / c.2131delG / p.D711Mfs12Stop) associated with Cirneco oculo-neurological syndrome (CONS) in two male littermates and three related carriers.

nsdtr-club-usa-health-statement.note: US parent-club health statement outlining required CHIC screenings (hip dysplasia evaluation, ACVO eye exam, and prcd-PRA DNA test) and optional screenings (elbow, cardiac, patellar, thyroid, CEA, JADD, CP1, CLPS, CDDY, CLAM, and CDMC).

nsdtr-immune-mediated-disease-patterns-2.name: Disease Patterns and Incidence of Immune-Mediated Disease in Insured Swedish Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retrievers
nsdtr-immune-mediated-disease-patterns-2.note: Bremer HD, Vilson Å, Bonnett BN, Hansson-Hamlin H (Veterinary Record 2015;177(3):74). Epidemiological cohort study of 2,890 insured Swedish Tollers (2002–2007) reporting elevated relative risk and incidence rates for SRMA (20 per 10,000 DYAR; RR 12) and IMRD (6.8 per 10,000 DYAR; RR 18), higher lymphoma risk, and lower ear and heart disease rates compared with other breeds.

nsdtr-immune-mediated-health-survey-2024.name: In Sickness and Health - A Questionnaire-Based Study of Immune-Mediated Diseases and Neoplasia in Swedish Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retrievers
nsdtr-immune-mediated-health-survey-2024.note: Nilsson K et al. / Hansson-Hamlin H (Acta Veterinaria Scandinavica 2024;66:39). Questionnaire study of 935 living and 177 deceased Swedish Tollers reporting living lifetime prevalence of 3.0% for IMRD and 3.5% for SRMA, owner-reported neoplasia of any type in 14% of living dogs (mammary 22%, mast cell 15%), and neoplasia as cause of death in 38.4% of deceased dogs.

nsdtr-resf1-jadd-study-2026.name: A Variant in RESF1 Is Associated with Addison's Disease and Multiple Autoimmune Syndrome in Young Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retrievers
nsdtr-resf1-jadd-study-2026.note: Brown EA, Cullen JN et al. / Bannasch DL (Scientific Reports 2026;16:13194). Identifies an autosomal recessive missense variant in RESF1 (Chr27:29,736,795, c.3170C>T, p.Pro1057Leu) associated with juvenile-onset Addison's disease (~75% penetrance by 1 year, median onset 5 months) and multiple autoimmune syndrome (41.7%–70.8% concurrent immune disorders; median survival 2.0 years).

uc-davis-vgl-jadd-nsdtr.name: UC Davis Veterinary Genetics Laboratory - Juvenile Addison's Disease in Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retrievers
uc-davis-vgl-jadd-nsdtr.note: UC Davis VGL test page for the RESF1 c.3170C>T (p.Pro1057Leu) juvenile Addison's disease (JADD) variant, documenting autosomal recessive inheritance with incomplete (~75.9%) penetrance, ~20%–23% carrier frequency, concurrent ocular/immunologic comorbidities, and breeding guidance.

wikimedia-bloodhound-black-and-tan-canar.note: Photograph of a male black-and-tan Bloodhound by Canarian, captured 2013-09-21 (per Summary and SONY DSLR-A350 EXIF metadata) and uploaded 2013-10-23 (630x442, licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0).

hokkaido-association-of-north-america-ab.name: Hokkaido Association of North America - About Hokkaido
hokkaido-association-of-north-america-ab.note: National breed club overview covering temperament, appearance, coat colours, grooming, house manners, vocalization, pica, and potty training.

hokkaido-association-of-north-america-hi.name: Hokkaido Association of North America - Hokkaido History
hokkaido-association-of-north-america-hi.note: National breed club history covering Ainu origins, Thomas Blakiston (1869), the 1902 Hakkōda Mountains army rescue, the 1937 Natural Monument designation, DOKENHO (1954), and Otōsan.

hokkaido-association-of-north-america-he.name: Hokkaido Association of North America - Hokkaido Health
hokkaido-association-of-north-america-he.note: National breed club health statement detailing mandatory and optional pre-breeding clearances, Collie eye anomaly (CEA), heart murmurs, hip dysplasia, idiopathic seizures, anxiety, psychogenic polydipsia, and pica.

united-kennel-club-hokkaido-breed-standa.name: United Kennel Club - Hokkaido (Ainu) Breed Standard
united-kennel-club-hokkaido-breed-standa.note: Official UKC breed standard for the Hokkaido (recognized as Ainu in 1996, renamed Hokkaido in 2008; Northern Breed Group).

hokkaido-cea-nhej1-study.name: Veterinary Ophthalmology - Collie Eye Anomaly in Hokkaido Dogs: Case Study
hokkaido-cea-nhej1-study.note: Peer-reviewed study by Mizukami et al. (Vet Ophthalmol 2012;15(2):128-132; DOI: 10.1111/j.1463-5224.2011.00950.x) identifying the intronic 7.8-kb NHEJ1 deletion in Hokkaido dogs.

hokkaido-cea-mdr1-selection-study.name: Veterinary Record - Investigation of Parallel and Simultaneous Selection for Collie Eye Anomaly and Ivermectin Toxicosis
hokkaido-cea-mdr1-selection-study.note: Peer-reviewed study by Mizukami et al. (Vet Rec 2014;175(7):174; DOI: 10.1136/vr.102015) confirming a 0.667 mutant allele frequency for the NHEJ1 Collie eye anomaly deletion (12/18 carriers, 6/18 affected) and 0% frequency for the MDR1/ABCB1 defect in tested Hokkaido dogs.

fci-grand-anglo-francais-tricolore-stand.name: FCI - Grand Anglo-Français Tricolore Standard No. 322
fci-grand-anglo-francais-tricolore-stand.note: Official FCI English breed standard for Grand Anglo-Français Tricolore (Great Anglo-French Tricolour Hound, Standard No. 322, published 1996-06-18; official valid standard dated 1983-01-27).

fci-grand-anglo-francais-tricolore-nomen.name: FCI - Grand Anglo-Français Tricolore Breed Nomenclature (No. 322)
fci-grand-anglo-francais-tricolore-nomen.note: Official FCI nomenclature entry (No. 322) confirming definitive recognition on 1983-01-27, Group 6 Section 1.1 classification, working-trial requirement, and official multilingual breed names (Great Anglo-French Tricolour Hound, Grand Anglo-Français Tricolore, Großer Anglo-Französischer Dreifarbiger Laufhund, Gran Sabueso Anglo-Francés Tricolor).

venerie-grand-anglo-francais-tricolore.name: Société de Vénerie - Races : Le Grand Anglo-Français Tricolore (Standard FCI N° 322)
venerie-grand-anglo-francais-tricolore.note: Full French text of FCI Standard No. 322 (valid standard 27.01.1983) published by the Société de Vénerie, along with French pack-hound kennel, disease-prevention, and working guidance.

chien-com-grand-anglo-francais-tricolore.name: Chien.com - Grand Anglo-Français Tricolore
chien-com-grand-anglo-francais-tricolore.note: Secondary French breed profile noting Poitevin, Gascon Saintongeois, and English Foxhound ancestry and reporting secondary height (62–72 cm males, 60–68 cm females) and weight (29–30 kg) estimates.

wikimedia-grand-anglo-francais-tricolore.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Grand anglo francais tricol.jpg
wikimedia-grand-anglo-francais-tricolore.note: Wikimedia Commons file page for photograph by Alephalpha (captured 2006-10-22, uploaded 2008-10-21, 1200x800 px), dual-licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0 and GFDL 1.2+.

wikimedia-largeanglofrench-tricolore1-ca.note: Wikimedia Commons file page for photograph by Canarian (captured 2022-04-24, uploaded 2022-04-27, 2045x1772 px), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0.

italian-greyhound-club-of-america-about.name: Italian Greyhound Club of America - About the Italian Greyhound
italian-greyhound-club-of-america-about.note: National breed club guide covering temperament, exercise, grooming (daily tooth brushing, 1–3x weekly nail grinding), puppy/adult feeding schedules, house-training, and jump/fracture safety.

italian-greyhound-club-of-america-histor.name: Italian Greyhound Club of America - Italian Greyhound Breed History
italian-greyhound-club-of-america-histor.note: National breed club history covering ancient Mediterranean origins, Renaissance nobility and artists, royal owners, 1886 AKC registration, and post-WWII European repopulation.

italian-greyhound-club-of-america-health.name: Italian Greyhound Club of America - Italian Greyhound Health
italian-greyhound-club-of-america-health.note: Official IGCA Health Testing Recommendations (also published at https://www.akc.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Health-Statement-Italian-Greyhound-Club-of-America-2026-Final.pdf).

the-italian-greyhound-club-uk-breed-stan.name: The Italian Greyhound Club (UK) - Official Breed Standard
the-italian-greyhound-club-uk-breed-stan.note: Official UK breed standard under the auspices of The Kennel Club specifying ideal height 32–38 cm (12.5–15 in), ideal weight 3.6–4.5 kg (8–10 lbs), and accepted colours.

uc-davis-vgl-italian-greyhound-health-pa.name: UC Davis Veterinary Genetics Laboratory - Italian Greyhound Health Panel (FEH, PCAG, PRA-IG1)
uc-davis-vgl-italian-greyhound-health-pa.note: UC Davis VGL documentation for FEH (https://vgl.ucdavis.edu/test/feh-ig), PCAG (https://vgl.ucdavis.edu/test/pcag-susceptibility-ig), and PRA-IG1 (https://vgl.ucdavis.edu/test/pra-susceptibility-ig).

italian-greyhound-feh-enam-study.name: Animal Genetics - Simple Recessive Mutation in ENAM Is Associated with Amelogenesis Imperfecta in Italian Greyhounds
italian-greyhound-feh-enam-study.note: Peer-reviewed study by Gandolfi et al. (Anim Genet 2013;44(5):569-578; DOI: 10.1111/age.12043) identifying the 5-bp deletion in exon 10 of ENAM causing familial enamel hypoplasia (14% affected, 30% carriers).

italian-greyhound-autoimmune-diversity-s.name: Canine Genetics and Epidemiology - A Search for Genetic Diversity Among Italian Greyhounds from Continental Europe and the USA and the Effect of Inbreeding on Susceptibility to Autoimmune Disease
italian-greyhound-autoimmune-diversity-s.note: Peer-reviewed study by Pedersen et al. (Canine Genet Epidemiol 2015;2:17; DOI: 10.1186/s40575-015-0030-9; PMID: 26526059) analyzing genetic bottlenecks, DLA class I/II homozygosity, and multiple autoimmune diseases in Italian Greyhounds.

fci-grand-anglo-francais-blanc-et-orange.name: FCI - Grand Anglo-Français Blanc et Orange Standard No. 324
fci-grand-anglo-francais-blanc-et-orange.note: Official FCI English breed standard for Grand Anglo-Français Blanc et Orange (Great Anglo-French White and Orange Hound, Standard No. 324; current official valid standard dated 2023-08-01, English publication 2023-10-06; original valid standard 1983-01-27).

fci-grand-anglo-francais-blanc-et-orange.name: FCI - Grand Anglo-Français Blanc et Orange Breed Nomenclature (No. 324)
fci-grand-anglo-francais-blanc-et-orange.note: Official FCI nomenclature entry (No. 324) confirming definitive recognition on 1983-01-27, Group 6 Section 1.1 classification, working-trial requirement, current valid standard date (2023-08-01), and official multilingual breed names (Great Anglo-French White & Orange Hound, Grand Anglo-Français Blanc & Orange, Großer Anglo-Französischer Weiß-Oranger Laufhund, Gran Sabueso Anglo-Francés Blanco y Naranja).

ukc-great-anglo-francais-white-and-orang.name: United Kennel Club - Great Anglo-Français White and Orange Hound Breed Standard
ukc-great-anglo-francais-white-and-orang.note: Official UKC breed standard (recognized in 2006, Scenthound Group) specifying complete scissors bite, black or orange-brown nose, 23.5–27.5 inch height at withers, coat and colour rules, and disqualifications (cryptorchidism, viciousness or extreme shyness, albinism).

worldlydogs-grand-anglo-francais-blanc-e.name: Worldly Dogs - Grand Anglo-Français Blanc et Orange
worldlydogs-grand-anglo-francais-blanc-e.note: Secondary breed overview consulted cautiously for historical context and traditional pack-hunting background.

wikimedia-grand-anglo-francais-blanc-et-.note: Wikimedia Commons file page for photograph by Alephalpha (captured 2006-10-22, uploaded 2008-10-23, 640x480 px), dual-licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0 and GFDL 1.2+.

fci-tornjak-official-standard.name: FCI - Tornjak Official Breed Standard No. 355
fci-tornjak-official-standard.note: Official FCI Standard No. 355 (dated 2017-11-23; original valid standard published 2017-11-07) for the Tornjak (Bosnian and Herzegovinian – Croatian Shepherd Dog), covering origin, historical summary (1067 and 1374 records; 1972 recovery; 1978 purebred breeding), utilization, Group 2 Section 2.2 classification, temperament, conformation proportions (length exceeding height by no more than 8%, 1:1 skull-to-muzzle ratio, ~120° shoulder angle), coat, colour, height (males 65–70 cm, females 60–65 cm, ±2 cm tolerance), and disqualifying faults.

fci-tornjak-nomenclature.name: FCI - Tornjak Breed Nomenclature
fci-tornjak-nomenclature.note: Official FCI nomenclature entry No. 355 confirming multilingual breed names, origin in Bosnia and Herzegovina and Croatia, Group 2 Section 2.2 (Molossian type, Mountain type) classification without working trial, provisional acceptance on 2007-06-01, and definitive acceptance on 2017-11-07.

american-kennel-club-tornjak.name: American Kennel Club - Tornjak Breed Profile
american-kennel-club-tornjak.note: Official AKC breed profile (recorded in the Foundation Stock Service since May 2012 with Working Group designation) providing height (23–28 inches), weight (62–110 pounds), life expectancy (12–14 years), historical registration under the name Kanis Montanus and etymology from 'tor' (livestock enclosure), temperament, grooming, exercise, training, and nutrition guidance.

ukc-tornjak-official-standard.name: United Kennel Club - Tornjak Breed Standard
ukc-tornjak-official-standard.note: Official UKC breed standard (recognized 2011-08-18; revised 2017-05-01) classifying the Tornjak in the Guardian Dog Group and specifying history, character, conformation, coat, colour, height (males 25.5–27.5 in, females 23.5–25.5 in, ±0.75 in tolerance), eliminating faults, and disqualifications.

tornjak-club-north-america-breed-profile.name: Tornjak Club of North America - About the Breed
tornjak-club-north-america-breed-profile.note: North American breed-club profile detailing the Tornjak's Balkan mountain origins, livestock-guardian temperament, average height (23–28 in), average weight (60–120 lbs), and lifespan (12–14 years).

tornjak-club-north-america-health-concer.name: Tornjak Club of North America - Health Concerns
tornjak-club-north-america-health-concer.note: Breed-club health guidance on gastric dilatation-volvulus (GDV / bloat, including resting after meals, feeding smaller frequent meals, and avoiding elevated food bowls) and hip and elbow dysplasia (pre-breeding joint screening, controlled puppy growth, and weight management).

tornjak-hip-dysplasia-monitoring-study-2.name: Results of Radiological Hip Dysplasia Monitoring in Tornjak Breed
tornjak-hip-dysplasia-monitoring-study-2.note: Peer-reviewed retrospective study (Vrbanac et al., Veterinarski arhiv 2022;92(5):599–607, DOI: 10.24099/vet.arhiv.1409) of 735 Tornjak hip radiographs evaluated from 2001 to 2016 (median age 18 months), finding 74.97% healthy (grades A/B) and 25.03% dysplastic (grades C/D/E) overall (76.86% healthy and 23.14% dysplastic in 523 dogs under 24 months) and a significant reduction in severe grade E hip dysplasia over the 15-year period.
tornjak-hip-dysplasia-monitoring-study-2.publisher: Faculty of Veterinary Medicine, University of Zagreb (Veterinarski arhiv)

tornjak-hip-dysplasia-biomarker-study-20.name: Breed-Specific Evaluation of Serum Biochemical Markers in Canine Hip Dysplasia Observed in a Tornjak Dog Population
tornjak-hip-dysplasia-biomarker-study-20.note: Peer-reviewed study (Alilovic et al., Am J Vet Res 2023;84(11):ajvr.23.07.0170, PMID: 37699541) evaluating serum hyaluronic acid (HA), procollagen II C-terminal propeptide (PIICP), and matrix metallopeptidase 9 (MMP9) activity across 99 adult Tornjaks in Bosnia and Herzegovina (51 non-dysplastic grades A/B vs. 48 dysplastic grades C/D/E).
tornjak-hip-dysplasia-biomarker-study-20.publisher: American Veterinary Medical Association (American Journal of Veterinary Research)

wikimedia-tornjak-and-puppy-tomasz-wasko.note: Wikimedia Commons file page for 'File:Tornjak and puppy.jpg', photographed by Tomasz Waśko (uploader TomaszVasco) on 2023-05-20 and uploaded on 2023-05-26 under CC BY-SA 4.0 (4966 × 3311 px).

wikimedia-tornjak-female-canarian.note: Wikimedia Commons file page for 'File:Bosnian and Herzegovinian - Croatian Shepherd Dog aka Tornjak.jpg', photographed by Canarian on 2008-10-31 and uploaded on 2013-01-20 under CC BY-SA 3.0 (495 × 408 px).

skg-schweizer-laufhund.name: Schweizer Laufhund — Rasseporträt (mit dem Schweizerischen Laufhundeclub SLC)
skg-schweizer-laufhund.note: Official Swiss Kennel Club breed portrait co-authored with the Schweizerischer Laufhundeclub (SLC), documenting height (47–59 cm), weight (18–23 kg), history, working styles, temperament, exercise, and health/ear care.

schweizerischer-laufhundeclub-zuchtregle.name: Zuchtreglement des Schweizerischen Laufhunde-Clubs (ZR-SLC-2021)
schweizerischer-laufhundeclub-zuchtregle.note: Official breeding regulations of the Swiss breed club (approved by the SKG Central Committee on 2021-04-28), covering mandatory breeding inspection (Ankörung) at 15+ months, minimum breeding age (18 months), and conformation/behavioural requirements.

united-kennel-club-swiss-hound-breed-sta.name: Swiss Hound — Official UKC Breed Standard
united-kennel-club-swiss-hound-breed-sta.note: Official UKC breed standard (Scenthound Group, recognized January 1, 2006), confirming height (19–23 in / 49–59 cm males, 18.5–22.5 in / 47–57 cm females), four varieties, and coat colours.

russian-toy-club-of-america-breed-standa.name: Russian Toy Club of America — Official AKC Breed Standard
russian-toy-club-of-america-breed-standa.publisher: Russian Toy Club of America (RTCA) / American Kennel Club (AKC)
russian-toy-club-of-america-breed-standa.note: Official AKC breed standard (approved July 14, 2017; effective June 27, 2018), specifying height (8–11 in; disqualifying <7 in or >12 in), weight (up to 6.5 lbs; disqualifying <2 lbs), coat length (1–3 in, full ear fringe after 3 years), and accepted colours.

russian-toy-club-of-america-breed-histor.name: Russian Toy Club of America — Breed History
russian-toy-club-of-america-breed-histor.note: Official parent-club history documenting the 1716–1725 preserved specimen at the Zoological Museum in St. Petersburg, the 1958 long-coated progenitor Chiki, the 1966 standard, and the 1988 unification of the two varieties.

russian-toy-club-of-america-faq.name: Russian Toy Club of America — Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)
russian-toy-club-of-america-faq.note: Official parent-club FAQ covering appearance, coat colour eye/nose pigment rules, minimal shedding, puppy coat drop between 5 and 12 months, full coat/fringe maturation at 2–3 years, and harness safety.

russian-toy-club-of-america-health-and-g.name: Russian Toy Club of America — Health & Genetics Committee
russian-toy-club-of-america-health-and-g.note: Official RTCA Health & Genetics page listing core OFA screenings (Patellar Luxation, Ophthalmology Exam, Basic Cardiology Exam), optional OFA screenings (Legg-Calvé-Perthes, Hip Dysplasia, Elbow Dysplasia, Paired Serum Bile Acid), and Cornell Biobank sample collection for PRA and Legg-Calvé-Perthes.

russian-toy-club-of-america-performance.name: Russian Toy Club of America — Performance & Nose Work
russian-toy-club-of-america-performance.note: Official RTCA performance overview documenting participation in agility, obedience, rally, lure coursing, trick training, and nose work.

united-kennel-club-russkiy-toy-breed-sta.name: United Kennel Club — Russkiy Toy Breed Standard
united-kennel-club-russkiy-toy-breed-sta.note: Official UKC breed standard (recognized 2008, revised February 1, 2018; Companion Dog Group), specifying height 8–11 in (preferred 10 in), weight up to 6 lbs (preferred 5 lbs; eliminating fault <3 lbs or >6 lbs; disqualifying <2 lbs), and all 11 coat colours.

fci-bullmastiff-official-standard.name: FCI - Bullmastiff Official Breed Standard No. 157
fci-bullmastiff-official-standard.note: Official FCI Standard No. 157 (header dated 06.10.2026; official valid standard published 08.09.2026) covering Great Britain origin, Group 2 Section 2.1 classification without working trial, utilization, historical summary, temperament, head proportions (1:3 muzzle-to-head ratio, level/pincer or slightly undershot bite, non-pendulous flews), conformation, coat, colour (brindle, fawn, or red with essential black muzzle and slight white chest mark permissible), height (males 64–69 cm, females 61–66 cm), and weight (males 50–59 kg, females 41–50 kg).

american-kennel-club-bullmastiff.name: American Kennel Club - Bullmastiff
american-kennel-club-bullmastiff.note: Official AKC breed profile covering height (males 25–27 in, females 24–26 in; male average 26 in), weight (males 110–130 lbs, females 100–120 lbs; male average 120 lbs), life expectancy (7–9 years), 'The Gamekeeper's Night Dog' nickname, 1860 English origins, 1933/1934 AKC recognition, grooming, exercise, training, nutrition (several small puppy meals, two adult meals daily, post-meal rest), and recommended health tests (hip, elbow, cardiac, ophthalmologist, and thyroid evaluations).

royal-kennel-club-bullmastiff-standard.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Bullmastiff Breed Standard
royal-kennel-club-bullmastiff-standard.note: Official UK breed standard (last updated 1 August 2025) specifying Working Group classification, conformation, temperament, coat, colour, height (dogs 64–69 cm / 25–27 in, bitches 61–66 cm / 24–26 in), and weight (dogs 50–59 kg / 110–130 lbs, bitches 41–50 kg / 90–110 lbs).

royal-kennel-club-bullmastiff-profile.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Bullmastiff Breed Profile
royal-kennel-club-bullmastiff-profile.note: Official UK breed profile detailing 19th-century gamekeeper history, brindle nighttime camouflage, breed characteristics (large house, large garden, weekly grooming, under 10 years lifespan, >2 hours daily exercise listing), Breed Watch Category 2 status, short-muzzle/facial-fold care, and Good Practice pre-breeding schemes (elbow, eye, and hip testing).

american-bullmastiff-association-health-.name: American Bullmastiff Association - Health Statement
american-bullmastiff-association-health-.note: Official parent-club health statement recommending pre-breeding screening for hip dysplasia, elbow dysplasia, autoimmune thyroiditis / hypothyroidism, ophthalmic disorders, and cardiac disease.

american-bullmastiff-association-common-.name: American Bullmastiff Association - Common Diseases and Conditions
american-bullmastiff-association-common-.note: Parent-club health reference covering high pain tolerance, allergies, bloat (GDV), cancer (hemangiosarcoma, lymphoma/lymphosarcoma, mast cell tumors, osteosarcoma, mammary tumors), cardiac disorders (valvular murmurs, sub-aortic stenosis [SAS], cardiomyopathy), eye disorders (entropion, autosomal dominant PRA, retinal dysplasia), hypothyroidism, kidney/urinary disease (chronic renal failure, cystinuria, glomerulonephritis, renal amyloidosis, juvenile renal dysplasia), and orthopedic conditions (hip/elbow dysplasia, cruciate ligament rupture, HOD, OCD, and panosteitis).

petmd-bullmastiff-health-and-care.name: PetMD - Bullmastiff Dog Breed Health and Care
petmd-bullmastiff-health-and-care.note: Veterinary-authored breed guide (by Michelle Diener, DVM; reviewed by Molly Price, DVM; updated 15 April 2025) covering 7–9 year lifespan, dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM), subaortic valvular stenosis (SAS), entropion, progressive retinal atrophy (PRA), hip/elbow dysplasia, lymphoma, bloat/GDV and prophylactic gastropexy, feeding (2–3 meals/day at floor level, slow-feeder bowls, 1-hour rest before/after meals), moderate drooling and daily jowl wiping, allergy-related ear care, training, and fenced-yard/housing guidance.

merck-veterinary-manual-gastric-dilatati.name: Merck Veterinary Manual - Gastric Dilatation and Volvulus in Small Animals
merck-veterinary-manual-gastric-dilatati.note: Peer-reviewed veterinary reference (by Kevin P. Winkler, DVM, DACVS; reviewed August 2025) detailing GDV pathophysiology, risk factors, clinical signs, emergency stabilization and derotation, and preventive measures (multiple small meals, exercise restriction around meals, reducing mealtime stress, avoiding elevated bowls, and prophylactic gastropexy).

wikimedia-bullmastiff-desaix83.note: Wikimedia Commons file page for 'File:Bullmastiff.jpg' (589 × 509 px, CC BY-SA 3.0), uploaded on 2015-03-17 by Desaix83 as a white-background derivative of 'File:Bullmastiff edited.JPG' (originally photographed by Fausto Moreno on 2006-10-07).

fci-bucovina-shepherd-dog-official-stand.name: FCI - Romanian Bucovina Shepherd Official Breed Standard No. 357
fci-bucovina-shepherd-dog-official-stand.note: Official FCI Standard No. 357 (valid standard dated 20 August 2023; English version published 1 September 2023) covering Romanian Carpathian/Bucovina transhumance origin, Group 2 Section 2.2 classification without working trial, utilization, temperament, head proportions (1:1 skull-to-muzzle ratio, 16–18 cm male / 15–17 cm female skull width, scissor or level bite), conformation, dark ash-grey skin, double coat (6–9 cm body hair, neck mane, limb fringes/culottes), classical pied and solid colours (brindle patches rejected), height (males 68–78 cm, ideal 71–75 cm; females 64–72 cm, ideal 66–68 cm; ±4 cm tolerance), weight in proportion to height, and faults/disqualifications.

fci-bucovina-shepherd-dog-nomenclature.name: FCI - Romanian Bucovina Shepherd Nomenclature No. 357
fci-bucovina-shepherd-dog-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature page for Ciobănesc Românesc de Bucovina (No. 357), confirming Romania origin, Group 2 Section 2.2 (Molossian type, Mountain type) classification without working trial, provisional acceptance on 2009-03-26, definitive acceptance on 2019-04-29, official valid standard date 2023-08-20, and multilingual standard publication on 2023-09-01.

uc-davis-canine-hip-dysplasia.name: UC Davis School of Veterinary Medicine - Canine Hip Dysplasia
uc-davis-canine-hip-dysplasia.publisher: University of California, Davis, School of Veterinary Medicine
uc-davis-canine-hip-dysplasia.note: Veterinary reference (by John Gardiner, 24 April 2019) covering multifactorial genetics of canine hip dysplasia, caloric intake and growth rate management, lean body condition, and pre-breeding radiographic evaluation.

avma-pet-dental-care.name: AVMA — Pet Dental Care
avma-pet-dental-care.note: Clinical veterinary guidance on home dental prophylaxis and professional oral examinations for domestic canines.

wikimedia-bucovina-shepherd-canarian-201.note: Wikimedia Commons file page for 'File:Bucovina Shepherd.jpg' (2343 × 1791 px, CC BY-SA 4.0), photographed by Canarian on 2019-09-07 (Sony DSLR-A350 EXIF) and uploaded on 2019-09-09.

american-kennel-club-boykin-spaniel-offi.name: American Kennel Club - Official Standard for the Boykin Spaniel

royal-kennel-club-hovawart-profile.name: The Royal Kennel Club — Hovawart Breed Profile
royal-kennel-club-hovawart-profile.note: UK kennel-club breed profile confirming Working Group placement, Breed Watch Category 1 status, 1936 German Kennel Club recognition, exercise guideline (>2 hours/day), grooming (>once/week), shedding, lifespan (>10 years), and Best Practice BVA/KC Hip Dysplasia Scheme screening.

hovawart-club-of-great-britain-breed-int.name: Hovawart Club of Great Britain — Breed Introduction
hovawart-club-of-great-britain-breed-int.note: UK breed-club introduction detailing Harz, Black Forest and Odenwald origins, Kurt König's post-WWI reconstruction, 1947 postwar club formation, 1980 UK arrival and 1982 UK club founding, all three colours occurring in a single litter, 2-year maturation, height (63–70 cm / 58–65 cm) and weight (30–40 kg / 25–35 kg).

hovawart-club-of-great-britain-health.name: Hovawart Club of Great Britain — Health & Breeding Code of Ethics
hovawart-club-of-great-britain-health.note: UK breed-club health page and Code of Ethics (Clauses 15.3–15.5) requiring pre-breeding hip scoring (maximum individual BVA score 20, maximum combined parent score 25; UK breed median 8–9), thyroid testing within 2 years of mating (Total T4, Free T4, cTSH, and TgAA; tested halfway between seasons in bitches and >=30–45 days post-vaccination), and Degenerative Myelopathy (SOD1) DNA testing to avoid producing homozygous DM/DM offspring, plus GDV/bloat awareness.

hovawart-club-of-great-britain-care.name: Hovawart Club of Great Britain — Care and Grooming
hovawart-club-of-great-britain-care.note: UK breed-club care guide covering long-pin slicker and rotating-tooth comb brushing, mat-prone zones (behind ears, elbow feathers, rear-leg feathering), optional ear/foot hair trimming to reduce grass seeds and mud, growth-spurt nutrition, controlled puppy exercise, scent work, and weekly puppy veterinary weighing visits.

hovawart-club-of-north-america-faq.name: Hovawart Club of North America — Frequently Asked Questions
hovawart-club-of-north-america-faq.note: North American parent-club FAQ covering suitability for first-time owners, space needs, defensive vs. aggressive guarding instincts, 10–14 year lifespan, <5% hip dysplasia rate, and HCNA breeding requirements (two Very Good/Excellent conformation ratings, temperament test at >=20 months, OFA Good or Excellent hips at >=24 months, annual eye exam, full thyroid panel, and Breeding Director approval for genetic diversity).

societe-centrale-canine-braque-francais-.name: Société Centrale Canine – Braque Français, Type Gascogne

united-kennel-club-braque-francais-de-gr.name: United Kennel Club – Braque Francais de Grande Taille Breed Standard

american-kennel-club-american-english-co.name: American Kennel Club — American English Coonhound
american-kennel-club-american-english-co.note: Official AKC breed profile; provides height (24–26 in male, 23–25 in female), weight (45–65 lbs), lifespan (11–12 years), coat and colour information, working history, temperament, grooming, nutrition, and health guidance.

american-kennel-club-american-english-co.name: Regulations for AKC Coonhound Bench Shows, Field Trials, Nite Hunts and Water Races — History and Official Standard for the American English Coonhound
american-kennel-club-american-english-co.note: AKC Coonhound Regulations (amended to October 2021) and History & Standards for Coonhound Breeds (Pages 60–63: American English Coonhound history and official standard, approved April 2009, effective 1 January 2010).

united-kennel-club-english-coonhound-sta.name: United Kennel Club — English Coonhound Official Breed Standard
united-kennel-club-english-coonhound-sta.note: Official UKC English Coonhound breed standard (revised 1 January 2016); documents 1905 registration as English Fox & Coonhound, 1945/1946 Walker and Bluetick separations, height limits (22–27 in males, 21–25 in females), permitted coat colours (including white and lemon), and disqualifications.

american-kennel-club-american-english-co.name: American Kennel Club — American English Coonhound History: Why Most Call Them 'English Dogs'
american-kennel-club-american-english-co.note: AKC breed-history feature by Denise Flaim (updated 16 February 2024) covering British foxhound ancestry, 'English dogs' terminology, 'barking up the wrong tree' origin, bear/cougar baying, 1920s Leafy Oak winner 'Bones', and ticking distinctions from the Bluetick and Treeing Walker Coonhounds.

wikimedia-american-english-coonhound-pet.name: Wikimedia Commons — File:American English Coonhound.jpg
wikimedia-american-english-coonhound-pet.publisher: Wikimedia Commons; original author Pets Adviser
wikimedia-american-english-coonhound-pet.note: Wikimedia Commons file page for American_English_Coonhound.jpg: photographed 9 February 2012 by Pets Adviser at the Westminster Kennel Club Meet the New Breeds event, uploaded 2 July 2013 by Ltshears via Flickr upload bot, 3888 × 2592 px, licensed under CC BY 2.0 (includes author request to link to petsadviser.com).

akc-english-setter-profile.name: American Kennel Club — English Setter
akc-english-setter-profile.note: Breed profile covering measurements (males 25–27 in / 65–80 lb; females 23–25 in / 45–55 lb), 12-year life expectancy, care, grooming, exercise, nutrition, and recommended health tests.

english-setter-association-breed-standar.name: English Setter Association (UK) — Breed Standard
english-setter-association-breed-standar.note: Reproduces the UK Kennel Club breed standard (published August, amended November 2002); specifies height of 65–69 cm (25.5–27 in) for dogs and 61–65 cm (24–25.5 in) for bitches.

english-setter-association-health.name: English Setter Association (UK) — Health
english-setter-association-health.note: UK breed-club health overview covering hip dysplasia, atopic dermatitis, hypothyroidism, congenital deafness (BAER testing), and DNA testing for PRA-rcd4 and NCL.

pubmed-english-setter-congenital-deafnes.name: Congenital sensorineural deafness in English setters in the United Kingdom: prevalence and association with phenotype and sex
pubmed-english-setter-congenital-deafnes.note: Peer-reviewed study (Vet Rec 2020;186(17):e13, Epub 2019-10-29) of 447 UK English Setter puppies from complete litters undergoing BAER testing (2000–2018), reporting 3.6% unilateral and 0.9% bilateral congenital sensorineural deafness (4.5% total).

akc-english-setter-history.name: American Kennel Club — English Setter History: From Net Hunter to Dual-Purpose Show Dog
akc-english-setter-history.note: Historical overview covering 14th-century net-hunting origins, John Caius's 1570 account, Edward Laverack's 1825 line ('Ponto' and 'Old Moll'), R. Purcell Llewellin's field setter line, and 1878 charter recognition.

schweizerische-kynologische-gesellschaft.name: Schweizerische Kynologische Gesellschaft (SKG) & Gesellschaft Weisse Schäferhunde Schweiz (GWS) – Weisser Schweizer Schäferhund Rasseportrait

fci-pyrenean-mastiff-nomenclature.name: FCI Breeds Nomenclature — Mastín del Pirineo (92)
fci-pyrenean-mastiff-nomenclature.note: Official FCI nomenclature entry for Standard No. 92 (Group 2, Section 2.2 Molossoid breeds, Mountain type); documents definitive FCI acceptance on 13 November 1954 and official standard publication on 26 May 1982.

uk-kennel-club-pyrenean-mastiff-standard.name: The Royal Kennel Club — Pyrenean Mastiff (Imp) Breed Information & Interim Standard
uk-kennel-club-pyrenean-mastiff-standard.note: Official UK Kennel Club breed profile and interim standard overview (Working Group, Imported Breed Register since 2001); documents historical name 'Navarra Mastiff', Aragon/Navarre origin, spiked collar history, ideal heights of 81 cm (32 in) for males and 73.5 cm (29 in) for females, and exercise/living space requirements.

akc-pyrenean-mastiff-profile.name: American Kennel Club — Pyrenean Mastiff
akc-pyrenean-mastiff-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile; reports height (30–31 in males, 28–30 in females), weight (120–190 lbs / 54.4–86.2 kg), life expectancy (10–12 years), very low prey drive, puppy diet duration (18 months for females, 24 months for males), and recommended health tests.

pmaa-pyrenean-mastiff-standard.name: Pyrenean Mastiff Association of America — Breed Standard & History
pmaa-pyrenean-mastiff-standard.note: AKC parent club breed history and standard; documents 1970s breed rescue in Aragon by Rafael Malo Alcrudo (30 foundation dogs from ~100 survivors, 1977 CMPE founding), 1996 US introduction, minimum heights of 30 in (dogs) and 28 in (bitches) with no upper limit, 9:10 proportion, and accepted patch colours including brindle, agouti, sable, and badger.

pmaa-pyrenean-mastiff-health.name: Pyrenean Mastiff Association of America — Health Conditions
pmaa-pyrenean-mastiff-health.note: Detailed parent-club health epidemiology covering international hip and elbow dysplasia screening data (Finland n=291, Spain n=82, US/Canada n=81), Finnish Kennel Club cardiac mortality records (1990–2025: 46 cardiac deaths = 6.25%, mean age 6y 10m; last 15 yrs = 6.61%, mean age 5y 10m), degenerative myelopathy, eye conditions (iris-to-iris PPM, entropion, ectropion, distichiasis/trichiasis), and spine conditions (spondylosis, LTV).

petmd-pyrenean-mastiff-health.name: PetMD — Pyrenean Mastiff Dog Breed Health and Care
petmd-pyrenean-mastiff-health.note: Veterinary breed guide reviewed by Barri J. Morrison, DVM (featuring interviews with PMAA president Karina Whittington and board member Crystal Kaiser); verifies 120–190 lb adult weight, 8–12 year lifespan, DM, hip/elbow dysplasia, osteosarcoma, bloat/GDV precautions, feeding frequency (3 meals/day for puppies until ~2 years, 2 meals/day for adults), and grooming schedule.

akc-tibetan-terrier-standard.name: American Kennel Club — Official Standard of the Tibetan Terrier
akc-tibetan-terrier-standard.note: Official AKC breed standard approved 10 March 1987; specifies square proportions, large flat round snowshoe feet, fall of hair over eyes, double coat, any colour/combination with black nose and dark eye rims, average male height 15–16 inches (14–17 inches acceptable, females slightly smaller), and weight 18–30 pounds (14–30 pounds across 14–16 inch heights).

ttca-tibetan-terrier-health-testing.name: Tibetan Terrier Club of America — Health Testing Recommendations
ttca-tibetan-terrier-health-testing.note: Parent-club breeding health recommendations covering hip evaluation, ACVO eye examination, DNA testing for NCL (ATP13A2), PLL (ADAMTS17), PRA3 (FAM161A), and RCD4 PRA (C2orf71), BAER hearing evaluation, and patellar luxation assessment. Note: TTCA has migrated active web operations to https://ttca-online.org/.

ttca-tibetan-terrier-health.name: Tibetan Terrier Club of America — Breed Health Overview
ttca-tibetan-terrier-health.note: Parent-club overview of longevity (12–16 years) and hereditary ocular, orthopedic, neurological, auditory, and endocrine conditions.

wikimedia-tibetan-terrier-acid-pix.note: Photograph by Acid Pix, captured 15 October 2012 (Canon EOS 7D) and uploaded 13 November 2012 via Flickr upload bot by Ltshears (2,402 × 1,601 px), licensed under CC BY 2.0.

federation-cynologique-internationale-fc.name: Fédération Cynologique Internationale (FCI) – Staffordshire Bull Terrier
federation-cynologique-internationale-fc.note: FCI Standard No. 76 for the Staffordshire Bull Terrier (Group 3, Section 3).

staffordshire-bull-terrier-club-of-ameri.name: Staffordshire Bull Terrier Club of America – Health and CHIC Requirements
staffordshire-bull-terrier-club-of-ameri.note: Official national parent club health testing guidelines, CHIC criteria, and hereditary disease statements.
staffordshire-bull-terrier-club-of-ameri.publisher: Staffordshire Bull Terrier Club of America

pegram-2020-staffordshire-bull-terrier-v.name: Pegram et al. (2020) – Staffordshire Bull Terriers in the UK: Their Disorders and Demographics in VetCompass
pegram-2020-staffordshire-bull-terrier-v.note: Epidemiological cohort study of 1,304 confirmed Staffordshire Bull Terriers evaluating disorder prevalence, longevity, and behavioral odds in primary-care veterinary clinics.

ukc-black-mouth-cur-breed-standard.name: United Kennel Club — Official Breed Standard: Black Mouth Cur
ukc-black-mouth-cur-breed-standard.note: Official UKC breed standard (recognised 1 November 1998, Scenthound Group) specifying history, working characteristics, conformation, dark oral mucosa pigment, webbed feet, accepted coat colours and dilute traits, and minimum mature height (18 in male / 16 in female) and weight (40 lb male / 35 lb female).

continental-kennel-club-black-mouth-cur.name: Continental Kennel Club — Black Mouth Cur Dog Breed Information
continental-kennel-club-black-mouth-cur.note: Kennel-club breed profile and standard detailing alternate names (American BlackMouth Cur, Ladner Cur, Ladner BlackMouth Cur, Southern Cur, Yellow Black Mouth Cur, BMC), group (Pastoral and Stock Dog Breeds), lifespan (12–16 years), height (18–26 in male, 16–24 in female), weight (40–60 lb male, 35–55 lb female), and 4:5 to 1:1 muzzle-to-skull ratio.

fci-deutsch-stichelhaar-standard.name: Fédération Cynologique Internationale — FCI-Standard N° 232: Deutsch Stichelhaar
fci-deutsch-stichelhaar-standard.note: Official English-language FCI breed standard (valid standard dated 29 November 2001, published 13 March 2008). Covers German origin, 1888 Hans von Kadisch historical proof, 1892 Club Stichelhaar / 1976 Verein Deutsch Stichelhaar history, 4 cm stiff bristly coat, brown/roan colours, male (60–70 cm) and female (58–68 cm) withers height, and disqualifying faults.

vdh-deutsch-stichelhaar-profile.name: Verband für das Deutsche Hundewesen (VDH) — Rasselexikon: Deutsch Stichelhaar
vdh-deutsch-stichelhaar-profile.note: German national kennel club breed profile covering height (60–70 cm males, 58–68 cm females), coat, temperament, and working history.

american-kennel-club-slovensky-cuvac.note: Official AKC breed profile and Foundation Stock Service standard criteria (recorded in FSS since February 2009).

klub-chovatelov-slovenskych-cuvacov-zdra.name: Klub chovateľov slovenských čuvačov – Dysplázia bedrových kĺbov (DBK)
klub-chovatelov-slovenskych-cuvacov-zdra.note: Official national breed club health regulations governing mandatory pre-breeding hip dysplasia screening (RTG DBK) and breeding limits.

fci-tyrolean-hound-official-standard.name: FCI — Tyrolean Hound (Tiroler Bracke) Official Breed Standard No. 68
fci-tyrolean-hound-official-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 68 (dated 18 June 1996; valid standard published 10 October 1995). Verifies Austrian origin, Emperor Maximilian I (~1500) lead-hound history, 1860 pure breeding, 1896 standard, 1908 recognition, 1994 deletion of the short-legged variety, conformation, 42-tooth scissor bite, red and black-and-tan colour varieties, and withers height (44–50 cm males, 42–48 cm females).

fci-tyrolean-hound-nomenclature.name: FCI — Tiroler Bracke (68) Breed Nomenclature
fci-tyrolean-hound-nomenclature.note: Official FCI nomenclature entry for Breed No. 68 confirming multilingual names (Tyrolean Hound, Brachet Tyrolien, Tiroler Bracke, Sabueso del Tirol), Group 6 Section 1.2 classification, working trial requirement, and definitive recognition on 8 October 1954.

klub-tirolerbracke-profile.name: Klub Tirolerbracke (Österreich) — Die Tirolerbracke Rasseprofil
klub-tirolerbracke-profile.note: Official Austrian parent club breed standard and profile detailing origin, solo vocal trailing and blood-tracking use, conformation, and calm, child-friendly household character when integrated into the hunter's family.

tiroler-jaegerverband-tyrolean-hound.name: Tiroler Jägerverband — Jagdhunde in Tirol: Tiroler Bracke
tiroler-jaegerverband-tyrolean-hound.note: Official Tyrolean Hunters' Association overview of Alpine hunting dogs and tracking stations (Nachsuchestationen), confirming the Tyrolean Hound's height (44–50 cm males, 42–48 cm females), coat, and role in vocal trailing and blood tracking.

fci-bernese-mountain-dog-standard.name: FCI — Bernese Mountain Dog (Berner Sennenhund, Dürrbächler) Official Breed Standard No. 45
fci-bernese-mountain-dog-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 45 (dated 5 May 2003; official valid standard published 25 March 2003). Used to verify Swiss origin in the Canton of Bern and Dürrbach near Riggisberg, historical exhibitions (1902, 1904, 1907, 1910 Burgdorf show with 107 dogs) and 1907 founding of the Schweizerischer Dürrbach-Klub, 9:10 height-to-length and 2:1 height-to-chest-depth proportions, close-fitting lips, jet-black tricolour coat pattern, height ranges (64–70 cm male with 66–68 cm ideal; 58–66 cm female with 60–63 cm ideal), and disqualifying faults.

american-kennel-club-bernese-mountain-do.name: American Kennel Club — Bernese Mountain Dog Breed Information
american-kennel-club-bernese-mountain-do.note: Official AKC breed profile used to verify published adult weight ranges in pounds (80–115 lb for males; 70–95 lb for females), 7–10 year life expectancy, 1937 AKC recognition, 1892 foundation work by Franz Schertenleib, high shedding and grooming requirements, minimum 30 minutes of daily moderate exercise, and family temperament traits.

bernese-mountain-dog-club-america-recomm.name: Bernese Mountain Dog Club of America — Recommended Testing
bernese-mountain-dog-club-america-recomm.publisher: Bernese Mountain Dog Club of America (BMDCA)
bernese-mountain-dog-club-america-recomm.note: National parent breed club testing guidelines specifying minimum recommended health screenings: hip and elbow radiographic evaluations, ophthalmologist eye exam, cardiac exam, degenerative myelopathy DNA testing (both SOD1A and SOD1B mutations), plus at least one optional test among von Willebrand disease Type I DNA testing, thyroid panel, or histiocytic sarcoma genetic risk testing, shared via OFA/CHIC and the Berner-Garde database.

fci-brittany-spaniel-standard.name: FCI — Brittany Spaniel (Épagneul Breton), Standard No. 95
fci-brittany-spaniel-standard.note: Official FCI Standard No. 95 (English translation published 05.05.2003; official valid standard dated 25.03.2003). Verifies French origin in central Brittany, 1907 Nantes draft and 7 June 1908 Loudéac ratification, Group 7 Section 1.2 classification, square proportions, natural tailless/short-tailed trait, allowed bicolour/roan/tricolour coats, and sex-specific heights at withers (males 48–51 cm ±1 cm tolerance; females 47–50 cm ±1 cm tolerance).

american-kennel-club-brittany-standard.name: American Kennel Club — Official Standard for the Brittany
american-kennel-club-brittany-standard.note: Official AKC breed standard (approved April 10, 1990; effective May 31, 1990). Verifies height (17.5–20.5 inches with disqualification outside those bounds), weight (30–40 pounds), tight dry lips with heavy penalty for drooling or flews, tailless to 4-inch tail length, fine loose skin that rolls with briars, allowed orange-and-white, liver-and-white, and liver tricolour patterns, and disqualification of black nose or black in the coat.

american-kennel-club-brittany-profile.name: American Kennel Club — Brittany Dog Breed Information
american-kennel-club-brittany-profile.note: AKC breed profile verifying Sporting Group membership, height (17.5–20.5 in), weight (30–40 lb), life expectancy (12–14 years), trait ratings (moderate shedding, low drooling, high energy, high trainability), grooming, exercise, training, nutrition, and historical dates (1931 US introduction, 1934 AKC recognition, and September 1, 1982 official name change from Brittany Spaniel to Brittany).

american-brittany-club-health-testing.name: American Brittany Club — ABC Breeder Recommendations for Health Checks
american-brittany-club-health-testing.note: Official parent-club health statement specifying CHIC health screening requirements for Brittanys: (1) OFA or PennHIP hip evaluation, (2) annual eye examination by a boarded ACVO ophthalmologist from 2 to 8 years of age, and (3) one elective evaluation submitted to OFA from cardiac, elbow dysplasia, patellar luxation, or thyroid testing.

fci-great-dane-standard.name: FCI — Great Dane (Deutsche Dogge), Standard No. 235
fci-great-dane-standard.note: FCI Standard No. 235 (English version dated 02.10.2024; official valid standard published 21.08.2024). Verifies German origin, Group 2 Section 2.1 classification, 1878 Berlin committee and 1880 standard history, withers height (80–90 cm males, 72–84 cm females), and three breeding colour groups (Fawn/Brindle, Harlequin/Merle/Black including Mantle and Plattenhunde, and Blue).

american-kennel-club-great-dane-profile.name: American Kennel Club — Great Dane Breed Profile
american-kennel-club-great-dane-profile.note: AKC breed profile verifying published whole-number weight ranges (140–175 lb for males, 110–140 lb for females), height ranges (30–32 in males, 28–30 in females), life expectancy (7–10 years), historical French and German names, grooming and exercise guidance, and recommended health evaluations.

american-kennel-club-great-dane-lifespan.name: American Kennel Club — Great Dane Life Span and Health Issues
american-kennel-club-great-dane-lifespan.note: Health and longevity article (updated July 27, 2020) discussing typical lifespan (8–10 years, with some dogs living 6–7 years and rare individuals reaching 12), gastric dilatation-volvulus (bloat), dilated cardiomyopathy, orthopaedic disorders (hip dysplasia, osteoarthritis, osteochondrosis, hypertrophic osteodystrophy), and autoimmune thyroiditis.

great-dane-club-america-health-research.name: Great Dane Club of America — Health and Research
great-dane-club-america-health-research.note: Parent breed club health and surgical resource detailing gastric dilatation-volvulus and prophylactic gastropexy, dilated cardiomyopathy, hip dysplasia, autoimmune thyroiditis and Addison's disease, cataracts and entropion, osteosarcoma and lymphoma, cervical spondylomyelopathy (Wobbler syndrome), hypertrophic osteodystrophy and panosteitis, giant-breed surgical protocols, and baseline plus repeat health screenings (hips, echocardiogram, thyroid, eyes).

great-dane-club-america-owner-guide.name: Great Dane Club of America — Is a Great Dane for You?
great-dane-club-america-owner-guide.note: Parent breed club owner suitability and responsible-breeding guide covering space, transport, veterinary costs, supervision around young children, leash and fencing requirements, delaying jogging until after two years of age, and pre-breeding health testing.

rassezuchtverein-der-kromfohrlaender.note: Original German national breed club founded in 1955 by breed founder Ilse Schleifenbaum; establishes health screening regulations (Körung), breeding guidelines, and the University of Kassel DNA blood bank.

fci-gascon-saintongeois-standard.name: FCI Standard No. 21 — Gascon Saintongeois
fci-gascon-saintongeois-standard.note: Official FCI Standard No. 21 (English version published 08.08.2023; official valid standard published 01.08.2023; FCI definitive acceptance 10.08.1963, https://fci.be/en/nomenclature/GASCON-SAINTONGEOIS-21.html). Verifies French origin, Group 6 classification (Section 1.1 Large-sized scenthounds for Grand; Section 1.2 Medium-sized scenthounds for Petit, both with working trial), 19th- and 20th-century history, hunting utilization, temperament, conformation, coat and colour (including pale tan points and the dead-leaf roebuck mark), and withers height ranges (Grand: 65–72 cm males, 62–68 cm females; Petit: 56–62 cm males, 54–59 cm females, ±1 cm tolerance).

royal-canin-gascon-saintongeois.name: Royal Canin — Gascon Saintongeois
royal-canin-gascon-saintongeois.note: Veterinary-nutritionist brand breed profile (also published in English at https://www.royalcanin.com/us/dogs/breeds/gascon-saintongeois) used to verify typical life expectancy (12–14 years), temperament descriptors (determined, calm, loving, obedient), minimal grooming needs, and high exercise requirements.

american-kennel-club-coton-de-tulear-off.note: Official AKC breed standard for the Coton de Tulear (approved September 11, 2013; effective October 1, 2013).

the-royal-kennel-club-coton-de-tulear-br.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Coton De Tulear Breed Standard
the-royal-kennel-club-coton-de-tulear-br.note: Official UK Royal Kennel Club breed standard for the Coton de Tulear in the Toy Group (heights 25–30 cm for dogs, 22–27 cm for bitches).

united-kennel-club-coton-de-tulear-breed.name: United Kennel Club - Coton de Tulear Breed Standard
united-kennel-club-coton-de-tulear-breed.note: Official UKC breed standard for the Coton de Tulear in the Companion Dog Group (recognized January 1, 1996; revised July 1, 2007).

usactc-history-of-the-coton-de-tulear.name: United States of America Coton de Tulear Club - History of the Coton de Tulear
usactc-history-of-the-coton-de-tulear.publisher: United States of America Coton de Tulear Club
usactc-history-of-the-coton-de-tulear.note: Official AKC parent club history, origin in Toliara (formerly Tuléar), temperament, vocalizations, 15–19 year lifespan, and 9–14 month coat-transition grooming guidance.

coton-de-tulear-bnat-grm1-study.name: Journal of Veterinary Internal Medicine - A Truncated Retrotransposon Disrupts the GRM1 Coding Sequence in Coton de Tulear Dogs with Bandera's Neonatal Ataxia
coton-de-tulear-bnat-grm1-study.note: Peer-reviewed study by Zeng et al. (J Vet Intern Med 2011;25(2):267-272, PMID 21281350) identifying the exon 8 GRM1 retrotransposon insertion causing autosomal recessive Bandera's neonatal cerebellar ataxia in Coton de Tulear dogs.

coton-de-tulear-cmr2-best1-study.name: UC Davis Veterinary Genetics Laboratory - Canine Multifocal Retinopathy 2 (CMR2)
coton-de-tulear-cmr2-best1-study.note: Veterinary genetics reference documenting the autosomal recessive BEST1 c.482G>A mutation causing Canine Multifocal Retinopathy 2 (CMR2) in the Coton de Tulear (citing Guziewicz et al., 2007, Invest Ophthalmol Vis Sci 48(5):1959-67).

coton-de-tulear-ph-agxt-study.name: Animal Genetics - Primary Hyperoxaluria in Coton de Tulear
coton-de-tulear-ph-agxt-study.note: Peer-reviewed study by Vidgren et al. (Anim Genet 2012;43(3):356-361, PMID 22486513) identifying the autosomal recessive AGXT c.996G>A (p.Gly102Ser) mutation causing fatal neonatal primary hyperoxaluria in Coton de Tulear puppies.

fci-alpine-dachsbracke-standard.name: FCI Standard No. 254 — Alpenländische Dachsbracke (Alpine Dachsbracke)
fci-alpine-dachsbracke-standard.note: Official English translation (18 June 1996) of FCI Standard No. 254 (valid standard published 10 October 1995) for the Alpine Dachsbracke, covering Austrian origin, Group 6 Section 2 leash-scenthound classification, 1881/1885 Crown Prince Rudolf history, 1932/1975/1991 recognition milestones, 2:3 and 9:10 proportions, 42-tooth dentition, coat colours (Hirschrot and black with Vieräugl markings), and 34–42 cm height range.

fci-parson-russell-terrier-standard.name: FCI — Parson Russell Terrier Standard No. 339
fci-parson-russell-terrier-standard.note: Official FCI Standard No. 339 for the Parson Russell Terrier (Terrier du Révérend Russell), specifying Great Britain origin, Group 3 Section 1 classification, ideal heights of 36 cm for males and 33 cm for females, spannable chest, and smooth/broken/rough white or predominantly white coat.

akc-parson-russell-terrier-standard.name: American Kennel Club — Official Parson Russell Terrier Standard
akc-parson-russell-terrier-standard.note: Official AKC breed standard (approved July 13, 2004; effective September 29, 2004) specifying ideal heights of 14 inches for males and 13 inches for females, height disqualifications under 12 inches or over 15 inches, working weight of 13–17 pounds, and chest spanning procedure.

american-kennel-club-parson-russell-terr.name: American Kennel Club — Parson Russell Terrier
american-kennel-club-parson-russell-terr.note: AKC breed overview documenting 14 in (male) / 13 in (female) height, 12–15 in range, 13–17 lb weight, 13–15 year life expectancy, grooming, exercise, training, and national breed club health testing recommendations.

parson-russell-terrier-association-ameri.name: Parson Russell Terrier Association of America — Breed Guide
parson-russell-terrier-association-ameri.publisher: Parson Russell Terrier Association of America
parson-russell-terrier-association-ameri.note: Parent-club guide covering history, exercise, grooming, safe containment, and health screening.

american-kennel-club-parson-russell-terr.name: American Kennel Club — Breed-Specific DNA Testing Recommendations
american-kennel-club-parson-russell-terr.note: Lists Parson Russell Terrier DNA tests including Primary Lens Luxation (PLL), Late Onset Ataxia (LOA, CAPN1 gene), Spinocerebellar Ataxia (SCA, KCNJ10 gene), and Amelogenesis Imperfecta (Parson Russell Terrier Type).

fci-cirneco-dell-etna-nomenclature.note: Official FCI nomenclature entry for Cirneco dell'Etna (No. 199), documenting definitive recognition on 1956-03-09, official multilingual names, and working-trial status.

enci-cirneco-dell-etna-profile.name: Ente Nazionale della Cinofilia Italiana (ENCI) - Cirneco dell'Etna
enci-cirneco-dell-etna-profile.note: Official Italian Kennel Club (ENCI) breed profile, historical monograph (Migneco 1932, Baroness Agata Paternò Castello, Solaro 1939 standard, 1951 Catania club, Ch. Aetnensis Pupa 1952, ferret partnership), and Selected Breeding (Riproduzione Selezionata) requirements including HD A/B hip grading.

the-royal-kennel-club-cirneco-dell-etna-.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Cirneco Dell'Etna Breed Standard
the-royal-kennel-club-cirneco-dell-etna-.note: Official UK breed standard in the Hound Group specifying ideal height of 46–50 cm (18¼–19½ in) for dogs and 44–48 cm (17¼–19 in) for bitches, 2.5 cm (1 in) body coat, and colour rules.

united-kennel-club-cirneco-dell-etna-sta.name: United Kennel Club (UKC) - Cirneco dell'Etna Breed Standard
united-kennel-club-cirneco-dell-etna-sta.note: Official UKC breed standard in the Sighthound & Pariah Dog Group (recognized 2006, revised 2009-07-01).

cirneco-dell-etna-club-of-america-about.name: Cirneco dell'Etna Club of America - About CdECA
cirneco-dell-etna-club-of-america-about.note: Official parent-club history documenting the founding of CdECA on 1997-06-15 in Houston, establishment of the North American studbook in June 1998, ASFA lure-coursing recognition, and full AKC Hound Group recognition on 2015-01-01.

cirneco-dell-etna-club-of-america-sport.name: Cirneco dell'Etna Club of America - Sport & ENCI Work Standard
cirneco-dell-etna-club-of-america-sport.note: Parent-club guide to Cirneco field work, lure coursing, conformation, and the English translation of the ENCI Working Standard and Field Trial Regulations on wild rabbit.

cirneco-dell-etna-club-of-america-rescue.name: Cirneco dell'Etna Club of America - Rescue & Adoption Guidance
cirneco-dell-etna-club-of-america-rescue.note: Parent-club rescue and owner guidance covering North American population numbers, prey drive toward cats and squirrels, fenced running requirements, off-leash safety, and indoor blanket-burrowing habits.

cirneco-genomic-variability-cortellari-2.name: Cortellari et al. (2021) - Genomic variability of Cirneco dell'Etna and the genetic distance with other dog breeds (Italian Journal of Animal Science)
cirneco-genomic-variability-cortellari-2.note: Peer-reviewed genomic study (Ital J Anim Sci 2021;20(1):304–314) analyzing 230K SNP arrays in self-coloured fawn and tan-and-white Cirnechi, establishing genetic closeness to Kelb tal-Fenek and Segugio Italiano, ROH inbreeding (FROH 0.195 vs 0.100), and MITF white-spotting selection.
cirneco-genomic-variability-cortellari-2.publisher: Italian Journal of Animal Science (Taylor & Francis)

cirneco-leishmania-immune-response-2024.name: Martínez-Sáez et al. (2024) - Adaptive and innate immune response of Leishmania infantum infection in Cirneco dell'Etna dog breed
cirneco-leishmania-immune-response-2024.note: Peer-reviewed veterinary immunology study (Comp Immunol Microbiol Infect Dis 2024;113:102232, PMID: 39217909) investigating Th1 and Th17 cytokine responses to endemic Leishmania infantum infection in Cirneco dell'Etna dogs.
cirneco-leishmania-immune-response-2024.publisher: Comparative Immunology, Microbiology and Infectious Diseases / PubMed

fci-german-shepherd-dog-standard.name: FCI - German Shepherd Dog (Deutscher Schäferhund) Official Standard No. 166
fci-german-shepherd-dog-standard.note: Official FCI Standard No. 166 (dated 11 August 2010, published in English 23 December 2010) verifying German origin, Group 1 Section 1 classification with working trial, 1899 SV foundation in Frankfurt/Main and Augsburg from central and southern German herding dogs, balanced steady character, 60-65 cm (30-40 kg) male and 55-60 cm (22-32 kg) female size ranges, double coat and long double coat varieties (both with undercoat), accepted black with reddish-brown/brown/yellow-to-light-grey markings, solid black, and grey with darker shading, and disqualification of white coat or coats lacking an undercoat.

american-kennel-club-german-shepherd-dog.name: American Kennel Club - German Shepherd Dog
american-kennel-club-german-shepherd-dog.note: AKC breed profile verifying 1908 AKC recognition, Herding Group placement, 24-26 in (65-90 lb) male and 22-24 in (50-70 lb) female size ranges, 12-14 year life expectancy, trait ratings, double-coat shedding and grooming needs, exercise and training guidance, and recommended hip, elbow, and temperament evaluations.

vcahospitals-german-shepherd.name: VCA Animal Hospitals - German Shepherd
vcahospitals-german-shepherd.note: Veterinary breed reference verifying general physical traits, double-coat shedding, exercise and training needs, home environment considerations, and breed-associated conditions across life stages including hip and elbow dysplasia, osteochondritis dissecans, panosteitis, exocrine pancreatic insufficiency, epilepsy, allergic dermatitis, perianal fistula, pannus, degenerative myelopathy, degenerative joint disease, and lymphoma.

german-shepherd-dog-club-of-america-heal.name: German Shepherd Dog Club of America - Health & Genetics
german-shepherd-dog-club-of-america-heal.publisher: German Shepherd Dog Club of America
german-shepherd-dog-club-of-america-heal.note: Parent club health and genetics page verifying CHIC certification requirements (OFA hip dysplasia evaluation, OFA elbow dysplasia evaluation, and GSDCA temperament evaluation) and Health Award of Merit criteria (adding OFA cardiac, OFA thyroid, and degenerative myelopathy DNA testing), plus resources on bloat (GDV), fibrotic myopathy, and hemangiosarcoma.

fci-drentsche-patrijshond-standard.name: FCI Standard No. 224 — Drentsche Patrijshond (Drentsche Partridge Dog)
fci-drentsche-patrijshond-standard.note: Official international breed standard specifying classification (Group 7, Section 1.2, with working trial), Dutch origin in Drenthe (16th-century Spioenen roots, 1943 recognition, 1948 club founding), proportions, circular tail motion when scenting, coat, white-and-brown colour patterns, withers height (58–63 cm males, 55–60 cm females), and weight (30–35 kg males, 25–31 kg females).

drentsche-patrijshond-club-health-screen.name: Vereniging 'De Drentsche Patrijshond' — Gezondheidsonderzoeken & Gezondheid
drentsche-patrijshond-club-health-screen.note: Dutch parent breed club health and breeding programme documentation covering mandatory ophthalmic (ECVO), hip dysplasia (HD), and elbow dysplasia (ED) evaluations as well as breed guidance on idiopathic epilepsy and von Willebrand disease type 1.

united-kennel-club-drentsche-patrijshond.name: United Kennel Club — Drentsche Patrijshond Breed Standard
united-kennel-club-drentsche-patrijshond.note: UKC Gun Dog Group breed standard confirming 16th-century Dutch origin from Spanish/French Spioenen, anatomy, coat, colour, and imperial height range (23–25 in males, 21.5–23.5 in females).

fci-stabijhoun-standard.name: FCI Standard No. 222 — Stabijhoun (Frisian Pointer)
fci-stabijhoun-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 222 (valid standard dated 2014-11-03, published 2015-05-29) specifying classification (Group 7 Pointing Dogs, Section 1.2 Continental Pointing Dogs, Spaniel type, with working trial), Frisian forest history, 1938 purification and 1942 recognition, 1947 NVSW founding, ideal withers height (50–53 cm males, 48–50 cm females, ±2 cm tolerance), weight (22–27 kg males, 18–23 kg females), coat structure, and accepted black-and-white or brown-and-white pied/roan colours (with tan markings/tricolour disqualifying).

american-kennel-club-stabyhoun.name: American Kennel Club — Stabyhoun Dog Breed Information
american-kennel-club-stabyhoun.note: AKC Foundation Stock Service breed profile documenting height (19–21 inches), weight (40–60 pounds), life expectancy (13–15 years), family/child/dog compatibility ratings, shedding and grooming needs, daily exercise requirement (~1 hour/day), barking and drooling ratings, and health screening priorities (epilepsy, hip and elbow dysplasia, patent ductus arteriosus, and cerebral dysfunction).

stabyhoun-association-of-america-about-b.name: Ameri-Can Stabyhoun Association (ASA) — About the Breed & Health of the Stabyhoun
stabyhoun-association-of-america-about-b.note: North American breed club health and breed overview documenting population incidence and mandatory breeding policies for hip dysplasia (HD), elbow dysplasia (ED), idiopathic epilepsy (~1%), steroid-responsive meningitis-arteritis (SRMA, ~0.5%), patent ductus arteriosus (PDA, ~0.7%), cerebral dysfunction (CD, mandatory DNA test since April 2015), and von Willebrand Disease Type I (vWD-I).

united-kennel-club-stabyhoun-standard.name: United Kennel Club — Official Stabyhoun Breed Standard
united-kennel-club-stabyhoun-standard.note: Official UKC Gun Dog Group breed standard (recognized 2006, updated April 1, 2009) detailing Frisian history, utility as an all-around hunting, cart-pulling, and mole-catching farm dog, tight non-pendulous lips without dewlap, ideal height (21 inches males, 19.5 inches females), weight (45–55 pounds males, 35–45 pounds females), and coat colours.

licg-stabijhoun.name: Landelijk InformatieCentrum Gezelschapsdieren (LICG) — Huisdierenbijsluiter Stabijhoun
licg-stabijhoun.note: Dutch national companion-animal veterinary advisory covering Frisian origins, height (50–53 cm males, 48–50 cm females), weight (22–27 kg males, 18–23 kg females), average lifespan (~13 years), coat care, exercise, socialization, alone-time tolerance when gradually trained, and Utrecht University priority hereditary conditions (patent ductus arteriosus, idiopathic epilepsy, cerebral dysfunction, von Willebrand disease type 1, hip dysplasia, and elbow dysplasia).

nsdtr-club-usa-health-overview.note: US parent-club health and genetics overview detailing required CHIC tests (hip evaluation, annual ACVO eye exam, prcd-PRA DNA test) and recommended screenings (elbow, cardiac, patellar, thyroid, CEA, JADD, CP1, CLPS, CDDY, CLAM, and CDMC).

uc-davis-vgl-nsdtr-health-panel.name: UC Davis Veterinary Genetics Laboratory - Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retriever Health Panel

uc-davis-vgl-clam-nsdtr.name: UC Davis Veterinary Genetics Laboratory - Cardiac Laminopathy (CLAM) in Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retrievers

american-kennel-club-nsdtr-history.name: American Kennel Club - Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retriever History: Behind the 'Little River Duck Dog'
american-kennel-club-nsdtr-history.note: Detailed AKC historical article documenting Mi'kmaq and red-fox tolling traditions, Little River Harbour origins, Kooikerhondje and St. John's Water Dog connections, 1945 Canadian registration of 15 dogs, Sue Van Sloun's 1978 US imports, 1984 US club founding, and 2003 AKC recognition as the 150th breed.

fci-lowchen-standard.name: FCI Standard No. 233 — Löwchen (Little Lion Dog / Petit Chien Lion)
fci-lowchen-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 233 specifying origin (France), classification (Group 9 Companion and Toy Dogs, Section 1.3 Bichons and related breeds, without working trial), historical summary (13th-century Amiens Cathedral carvings, 15th-century tapestries, court of Burgundy, Buffon, Linnaeus, 18 November 1947 French breed club founding), square proportions, silky wavy single coat, obligatory Lion Clip for exhibition, all permitted coat colours and combinations, height (26–32 cm at the withers, ±1 cm tolerance), and approximate weight (6 kg).

american-kennel-club-lowchen.name: American Kennel Club — Löwchen Dog Breed Information
american-kennel-club-lowchen.note: AKC Non-Sporting Group breed profile documenting height summary (12–14 inches), weight summary (15 pounds), life expectancy (13–15 years), temperament ratings, low shedding and drooling levels, grooming, exercise, training, nutrition, and recommended parent-club health evaluations (Patella Evaluation, Hip Evaluation, Ophthalmologist Evaluation).

lowchen-club-of-america-breed-health.name: The Löwchen Club of America — Löwchen Dog Breed Health Testing
lowchen-club-of-america-breed-health.note: Official U.S. parent breed club health testing page specifying OFA Canine Health Information Center (CHIC) recommended screenings: ACVO Eye Exam, Hip Dysplasia evaluation, and Patellar Luxation evaluation.

lowchen-club-of-america-about-breed.name: The Löwchen Club of America — Get to Know the Little Lion Dog
lowchen-club-of-america-about-breed.note: Official U.S. parent breed club guide by Jennie Chen, PhD covering non-shedding dual-textured single coat, colour shifts with maturity, typical pound weight range (10–17 lb), athleticism in agility/obedience/rally/flyball/barn hunt, problem-solving intelligence, vocal habits, adolescent coat change around one year of age, and companion vs. show grooming.

fci-collie-rough-nomenclature.name: FCI Breeds Nomenclature — Collie Rough (156)
fci-collie-rough-nomenclature.note: Official FCI nomenclature entry for Collie Rough (Standard No. 156), documenting Group 1 (Sheepdogs and Cattledogs, except Swiss Cattledogs), Section 1 (Sheepdogs), country of origin (Great Britain), definitive recognition date (1955-04-13), official valid standard date (2026-09-08), English standard publication date (2026-10-06), multilingual breed names, and exemption from working-trial requirements.

fci-collie-rough-standard-2012.name: FCI Standard No. 156 — Collie (Rough)
fci-collie-rough-standard-2012.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 156 for the Collie (Rough) (2012 edition and 2026-09-08 / 2026-10-06 valid standard revision at the same canonical URL), specifying Scottish herding origins, oblique almond-shaped dark eyes, semi-erect ears tipping forward over the top third, harsh straight outer coat with dense furry undercoat, three accepted colours (Sable, Tricolour, Blue Merle) with typical white markings, and withers height of 56–61 cm for males and 51–56 cm for females.

american-kennel-club-collie.name: American Kennel Club — Collie Dog Breed Information
american-kennel-club-collie.note: Official AKC Herding Group breed profile detailing height (24–26 in male, 22–24 in female), weight (60–75 lb male, 50–65 lb female), life expectancy (12–14 years), Scottish Highland and Lowland history, Queen Victoria's Balmoral kennel, 1885 AKC recognition, 1886 Collie Club of America founding, coat care, exercise, multi-meal bloat-reduction feeding advice, and recommended health tests.

collie-club-of-america-health.name: Collie Club of America — Collie Health
collie-club-of-america-health.note: Official U.S. parent club health overview summarising Collie CHIC Breed Survey results, general breed hardiness (typical 10–14 year lifespan, average 12 years), specialist veterinary ophthalmologist puppy eye checks at 5–6 weeks for Collie Eye Anomaly (CEA), and MDR1 medication sensitivity precautions.

collie-club-of-america-breeder-health.name: Collie Club of America — Questions To Ask A Breeder (Breeder Health Testing)
collie-club-of-america-breeder-health.note: Official Collie Club of America breeder health testing guide (incorporating the Breeder Health Testing FAQ) listing recommended parent and puppy evaluations: Collie Eye Anomaly (CEA), MDR1, PRA-rcd2, Hip evaluation (OFA, PennHIP, or equivalent), Dermatomyositis (DMS), Degenerative Myelopathy (DM), and pre-placement puppy ophthalmic examination.

american-bloodhound-club-breed-history-s.name: American Bloodhound Club - Breed History & Official AKC Standard

american-bloodhound-club-faq.name: American Bloodhound Club - Frequently Asked Questions about Bloodhounds
american-bloodhound-club-faq.note: US parent-club FAQ covering activity needs, apartment unsuitability, height/weight (including 120–130+ lb individuals), colour shades, drooling, baying, non-guarding watchdog nature, supervision with children under 5, pack sociability, digging, 5–6 ft physical fencing, and why electronic/invisible fences fail.

bloodhound-club-uk-breed-standard.name: The Bloodhound Club (UK) - Official UK Kennel Club Breed Standard
bloodhound-club-uk-breed-standard.note: Complete text of the UK Kennel Club Bloodhound breed standard hosted by The Bloodhound Club, detailing head length (≥30 cm / 12 in in dogs, ≥28 cm / 11 in in bitches), unimpeded eyesight, scissor bite, colours, height (63–69 cm / 25–27 in dogs, 58–63 cm / 23–25 in bitches; ideal 66 cm / 61 cm), and weight (41–50 kg / 90–110 lbs dogs, 36–45.5 kg / 80–100 lbs bitches).

bloodhound-club-uk-considering-a-bloodho.name: The Bloodhound Club (UK) - Considering A Bloodhound, What You Should Know
bloodhound-club-uk-considering-a-bloodho.note: UK parent-club buyer and owner guide covering KC/BVA hip, elbow, eye, heart, and DM testing, 10.00% average COI, scent-driven temperament, 15-foot slobber throws, minimum 2 hours of daily exercise, counter-surfing height, gastric torsion, ear cleaning, and reduced entropion incidence.

bloodhound-club-uk-breed-history.name: The Bloodhound Club (UK) - The History of the Bloodhound
bloodhound-club-uk-breed-history.note: UK parent-club historical account documenting British records from c. 1300, St. Hubert's Abbey origins, Scottish border 'sleuth hound' tracking of cattle reivers, Robert Boyle's 17th-century 7-mile trailing trial, Sir Walter Scott and Landseer depictions, and WWII population bottleneck.

royal-canin-fr-grand-anglo-francais-tric.name: Royal Canin France - Grand anglo-français tricolore
royal-canin-fr-grand-anglo-francais-tric.note: French breed profile noting 1978 official recognition, minimal grooming needs, outdoor living requirements, high exercise demands, and a secondary lifespan estimate of 12–14 years.

ach-dysplasia-screening-list.note: Official Romanian Kennel Club (AChR) breeding regulation table (adopted 17 February 2016) listing Ciobănesc Românesc de Bucovina (No. 357, Group II) for radiographic hip dysplasia (HD, minimum age 12 months, accepted breeding grade up to C) and elbow dysplasia (ED, minimum age 12 months, accepted breeding grade up to 1) evaluation.

ach-dysplasia-info.name: Asociația Chinologică Română - Informații Examen Displazie
ach-dysplasia-info.note: Official Romanian Kennel Club (AChR) hip and elbow dysplasia evaluation protocol detailing GRSK-accredited radiographic scoring recognized by the FCI Scientific Commission and International Elbow Working Group (IEWG).

ach-selection-regulation-romanian-shephe.name: Asociația Chinologică Română - Regulament de Selecție pentru Ciobăneștii Românești
ach-selection-regulation-romanian-shephe.note: Official AChR breeding-selection regulation (adopted 20 August 2008, effective 21 August 2008) requiring all Romanian Shepherd breeding stock (minimum age 15 months, microchipped) to pass a two-judge selection examination (ADR) covering body measurements, coat/undercoat, pigmentation, complete dentition/bite, calm balanced character, gait, and any requested medical/radiographic certificates prior to Romanian Stud Book (COR) litter registration.

ach-romanian-shepherd-breeds-2025-commun.name: Asociația Chinologică Română - Comunicat Oficial privind Rasele de Ciobănești Românești (2025)
ach-romanian-shepherd-breeds-2025-commun.note: Official AChR press release (No. 881/29.10.2025) reporting Romanian Stud Book (COR) registration totals for 2020–2024 (5,668 Romanian shepherd dogs total, led by 1,984 Ciobănesc Românesc de Bucovina registrations) and confirming 2009 provisional and 2019 definitive FCI recognition.

romfilatelia-romanian-dog-breeds-2019.name: Romfilatelia - Dog Breeds Postage Stamps Issue (Romanian Shepherd Breeds)
romfilatelia-romanian-dog-breeds-2019.publisher: Romfilatelia (Romanian Post Philatelic Authority, with AChR and Grigore Antipa National Museum)
romfilatelia-romanian-dog-breeds-2019.note: Official 22 February 2019 Romanian postage stamp issue (prepared with the Romanian Kennel Club and Grigore Antipa National Museum of Natural History) featuring the Romanian Bucovina Shepherd Dog on the Lei 8.50 stamp.

wisdom-panel-romanian-bucovina-shepherd-.name: Wisdom Panel - Romanian Bucovina Shepherd Dog
wisdom-panel-romanian-bucovina-shepherd-.note: Veterinary-reviewed breed profile (reviewed 12 July 2023 by Dr. Casey Knox, DVM) documenting traditional names ('Dulău' and 'Căpău'), transhumance flock guarding against wolves, bears, and lynx, the traditional wooden 'jujău' neck dangle required on free-ranging working dogs in Romania, 1982 AChR standard and 2019 recognition, and secondary weight (110–198 lb) and lifespan (12–14 yr) estimates.

fci-afghan-hound-standard.name: FCI - Afghan Hound Breed Standard (Standard No. 228)
fci-afghan-hound-standard.note: Official FCI standard PDF for the Afghan Hound (Standard No. 228, Group 10 Sighthounds, Section 1 Long-haired or fringed Sighthounds; origin Afghanistan, patronage Great Britain; male height 68-74 cm, female height 63-69 cm).

american-kennel-club-afghan-hound-standa.name: American Kennel Club - Official Standard for the Afghan Hound
american-kennel-club-afghan-hound-standa.note: Official AKC breed standard PDF approved September 14, 1948, specifying height for dogs (27 inches +/- 1 inch) and bitches (25 inches +/- 1 inch), and approximate weights of 60 lb for dogs and 50 lb for bitches.

american-kennel-club-afghan-hound.name: American Kennel Club - Afghan Hound Breed Profile
american-kennel-club-afghan-hound.note: AKC breed overview covering Hound Group assignment, 12-18 year life expectancy, coat care, exercise requirements, and recommended health evaluations.

afghan-hound-club-of-america-health.name: Afghan Hound Club of America - Health Testing and CHIC
afghan-hound-club-of-america-health.note: Parent breed club health-screening guidance listing hip dysplasia evaluation, board-certified ophthalmologist examination, and autoimmune thyroiditis testing.

wikimedia-afghan-hound-jurriaan-schulman.note: Wikimedia Commons image file page for a reddish-coated Afghan Hound photographed by Jurriaan Schulman under CC BY-SA 3.0.

wikimedia-afghan-hound-bryan-ungard.note: Wikimedia Commons image file page for an Afghan Hound photographed outdoors by Bryan Ungard on 2007-12-16 and uploaded on 2011-08-03 under CC BY-SA 2.0.

fci-chow-chow-standard.name: FCI - Chow Chow Breed Standard (Standard No. 205)
fci-chow-chow-standard.note: Official FCI Standard No. 205 (Group 5 Spitz and primitive types, Section 5 Asian Spitz and related breeds; origin China, patronage Great Britain; wither height 48-56 cm for males and 46-51 cm for females; whole-coloured black, red, blue, fawn, cream, or white).

american-kennel-club-chow-chow.name: American Kennel Club - Chow Chow
american-kennel-club-chow-chow.note: AKC breed profile and official standard link covering Non-Sporting Group assignment, 17-20 inch height, 45-70 lb weight range, 8-12 year life expectancy, coat colours, grooming, exercise needs, and recommended health evaluations.

chow-chow-health-screening-chic.name: Chow Health - OFA-CHIC Health Testing Requirements
chow-chow-health-screening-chic.note: Breed-specific health screening guidance covering veterinary ophthalmologist eye examination, hip dysplasia evaluation, elbow dysplasia evaluation, patellar luxation evaluation, and autoimmune thyroiditis panel, with cardiac evaluation listed as optional.
