wikimedia-chow-chow-olga-filonenko.note: Wikimedia Commons file page identifying Olga Filonenko as author under CC BY-SA 2.0 licensing.

boykin-spaniel-society-breed-standard.name: The Boykin Spaniel Society - Official Boykin Spaniel Breed Standard
boykin-spaniel-society-breed-standard.note: Official breed standard of The Boykin Spaniel Society (founded 1977; studbook established 1979), specifying height (15.5–18 in dogs, 14–16.5 in bitches), weight (30–40 lbs dogs, 25–35 lbs bitches), coat varieties (including short straight coat without feathering for warm-weather hunting), and working retriever/flusher characteristics.

boykin-spaniel-society-preferred-breeder.name: The Boykin Spaniel Society - Preferred Breeder Program Booklet (Revision 5)
boykin-spaniel-society-preferred-breeder.note: Official Boykin Spaniel Society Preferred Breeder Program requirements (Revision 5, June 2023), mandating OFA Fair-or-better hip evaluations, Normal cardiac, patellar, and ophthalmic certifications, and DNA testing for EIC, DM, and CEA with at least one parent tested Clear per condition.

boykin-spaniel-society-faq.name: The Boykin Spaniel Society - Frequently Asked Questions & Health Overview
boykin-spaniel-society-faq.note: Official Boykin Spaniel Society FAQ covering companion and hunting suitability, skin allergies in certain bloodlines, hip dysplasia, juvenile cataracts, pulmonic stenosis (congenital cardiac screening), patellar luxation, EIC, CEA, and DM inheritance tables.

boykin-spaniel-club-faq.name: Boykin Spaniel Club and Breeders Association of America - Breed FAQs
boykin-spaniel-club-faq.publisher: Boykin Spaniel Club and Breeders Association of America
boykin-spaniel-club-faq.note: AKC parent club FAQ detailing upland and waterfowl hunting versatility, high daily energy, sociability with children and other dogs, and moderate alert barking.

uc-davis-vgl-boykin-spaniel-health-panel.name: UC Davis Veterinary Genetics Laboratory - Boykin Spaniel Health Panel
uc-davis-vgl-boykin-spaniel-health-panel.note: Veterinary genetics laboratory breed health panel for the Boykin Spaniel covering Chondrodystrophy (CDDY/IVDD — FGF4-12) and Chondrodysplasia (CDPA — FGF4-18), Collie Eye Anomaly (CEA — NHEJ1), Degenerative Myelopathy (DM — SOD1), Exercise-Induced Collapse (EIC — DNM1), and Progressive Rod-Cone Degeneration (PRA-prcd — PRCD).

boykin-spaniel-eic-dnm1-study-2011.name: Minor et al. (2011) - Presence and Impact of the Exercise-Induced Collapse Associated DNM1 Mutation in Labrador Retrievers and Other Breeds
boykin-spaniel-eic-dnm1-study-2011.note: Peer-reviewed genetic survey (Vet J 2011;189(2):214–219, PMID: 21782486, DOI: 10.1016/j.tvjl.2011.06.022) confirming the DNM1 c.767G>T mutation and clinical exercise-induced collapse phenotype in Boykin Spaniels.

canine-fgf4-ivdd-batcher-2019.name: Batcher et al. (2019) - Phenotypic Effects of FGF4 Retrogenes on Intervertebral Disc Disease in Dogs
canine-fgf4-ivdd-batcher-2019.note: Peer-reviewed study (Genes 2019;10(6):435, PMCID: PMC6627552, DOI: 10.3390/genes10060435) demonstrating that the chromosome 12 FGF4 retrogene insertion (12-FGF4RG / CDDY) acts dominantly to cause premature intervertebral disc calcification and elevated risk of Hansen Type I disc herniation in segregating breeds including the Boykin Spaniel.

petmd-boykin-spaniel-health-care.name: PetMD - Boykin Spaniel Dog Breed Health and Care
petmd-boykin-spaniel-health-care.note: Veterinary breed care guide covering Boykin Spaniel exercise needs (at least 60 minutes daily), weekly brushing, monthly bathing limit, summer coat trimming for swimmers, post-swim ear flushing, and inherited health screening.

wikimedia-boykin-spaniel-flatscaster.note: Wikimedia Commons file page for 'File:Boykin spaniel.jpg' (2592 × 1944 px), photographed by Flatscaster on 2006-04-29 (Canon PowerShot S2 IS EXIF), originally uploaded to English Wikipedia on 2006-08-09 and transferred to Commons on 2008-02-15 under a public-domain dedication.

wikimedia-boykin-spaniel-april-jet.note: Wikimedia Commons file page for 'File:Boykin Spaniel April Jet.jpg' (1024 × 683 px, CC BY-SA 2.0), photographed by jetsonphoto on 2011-04-07 and uploaded to Commons on 2012-02-18.

fci-airedale-terrier-standard.name: FCI - Airedale Terrier Breed Standard
fci-airedale-terrier-standard.note: FCI Standard No. 7 (Group 3 Terriers, Section 1 Large and medium-sized Terriers; origin Great Britain; wither height 58-61 cm for males and 56-59 cm for females; hard, dense, wiry coat with dark saddle and tan furnishings).

american-kennel-club-airedale-terrier.name: American Kennel Club - Airedale Terrier
american-kennel-club-airedale-terrier.note: Breed profile covering Terrier Group classification, 50-70 lb weight range, 11-14 year life expectancy, traits, exercise needs, and recommended health evaluations.

airedale-terrier-club-america-health-sta.name: Airedale Terrier Club of America - Health Statement
airedale-terrier-club-america-health-sta.note: Parent breed club health statement covering hip, cardiac, and renal disease screening requirements, with eye, thyroid, and elbow evaluations designated as optional screenings.

wikimedia-airedale-terrier-ioan-bodean.note: Photograph of an Airedale Terrier outdoors by Ioan Bodean under CC BY-SA 2.0.

wikimedia-airedale-young-milkomede.note: Photograph of a young Airedale Terrier by Milkomède under CC BY-SA 4.0.

fci-artois-hound-nomenclature.name: FCI - Chien d'Artois (Artois Hound) Nomenclature No. 28
fci-artois-hound-nomenclature.note: Official FCI nomenclature entry No. 28 confirming France origin, Group 6 Section 1.2 (Medium-sized Scent Hounds) classification subject to a working trial, definitive acceptance on 1963-10-18, official valid standard date 1996-07-24, and multilingual names (Chien d'Artois, Artois Hound, Sabueso Artesiano).

societe-centrale-canine-chien-dartois-pr.name: Société Centrale Canine — Chien d'Artois Breed Profile
societe-centrale-canine-chien-dartois-pr.note: Official French national kennel-club breed profile covering general appearance, height (53–58 cm), weight (28–30 kg), coat, history, pack behaviour (entering the pack from 6 months of age, firm yet gentle 'iron hand in a velvet glove' guidance), unsuitability for urban living or being tied up, and puppy/adult nutrition (growing until 1 year of age on two substantial meals per day).

societe-centrale-canine-chien-dartois-hi.name: Société Centrale Canine — Le chien d'Artois : l'histoire
societe-centrale-canine-chien-dartois-hi.note: In-depth historical dossier (published 5 December 2022, updated 4 November 2025) documenting 1394 and 1410 Burgundian Ducal account mentions, the 1431 Paris coronation stag hunt before Henry VI, Louis XIII's 1608–1610 journals, 1609 Croÿ gift, Sélincourt (1683), Le Couteulx de Canteleu (1890), Ernest Levoir's Rallye-Scardon (c. 1888–1918), Auguste and Albert Mallart (1854–1932), the 1930 suppression of 'Briquet', and the 1970s reconstruction by André Audréchy ('du Parc à Biches'), Joseph Mancini, and Josette Pilat ('La Meute Saint-Louis' / 'Piqu'Artois Saint-Louis').

societe-centrale-canine-chien-dartois-ch.name: Société Centrale Canine — Le chien d'Artois : le caractère et la fonctionnalité
societe-centrale-canine-chien-dartois-ch.note: Official SCC working and temperament dossier (published 5 December 2022, updated 4 November 2025) detailing cold-trail 'rapprocheur' ability (up to 6-hour-old trails), vocalization ('meowing' whimpers on cold scent before giving full voice), puppy initiation at 4–5 months, pack peacefulness (including same-sex dogs), affectionate and quiet demeanour off-duty, TAN/brevet de chasse working trials, and current usage (~75% on wild boar, plus hare and roe deer).

royal-canin-fr-chien-dartois.name: Royal Canin France — Chien d'Artois
royal-canin-fr-chien-dartois.note: French breed guide listing average life expectancy (10–13 years), temperament traits (affectionate, confident, gentle, calm, intelligent, loyal), moderate grooming needs, high exercise needs, and early training.

woopets-chien-dartois.name: Woopets — Chien d'Artois : caractère, santé, alimentation, prix et entretien
woopets-chien-dartois.note: French breed guide reporting height (53–58 cm), weight (28–30 kg), secondary lifespan estimate (12–14 years), litter size (4–8 puppies), low drooling, moderate shedding, weekly brushing (1–2x/week), post-outing ear/pad/coat inspection, and twice-daily long exercise.

wikimedia-artois-puppy-pmarlow.note: Wikimedia Commons file page for 'File:Artois puppy.jpg' (350 × 282 px), released into the public domain worldwide by author P.Marlow at English Wikipedia on 2007-06-13 and transferred to Wikimedia Commons on 2011-05-08.

fci-dobermann-standard.name: FCI - Dobermann Breed Standard No. 143
fci-dobermann-standard.note: Official FCI Standard No. 143 (Group 2 Pinscher and Schnauzer type, Section 1 Pinschers, with working trial; origin Germany; male wither height 68-72 cm, weight about 40-45 kg; female wither height 63-68 cm, weight about 32-35 kg; recognized colors black or brown with rust-red markings).

american-kennel-club-doberman-pinscher.name: American Kennel Club - Doberman Pinscher
american-kennel-club-doberman-pinscher.note: Breed profile covering Working Group classification, 24-28 inch height, 60-100 lb weight, 10-12 year life expectancy, four recognized colors (black, red, blue, fawn with rust markings), temperament, grooming, and health screenings.

american-kennel-club-working-group-healt.name: American Kennel Club - Working Group Health Testing Requirements
american-kennel-club-working-group-healt.note: Official parent-club health testing requirements for the Working Group, listing hip evaluation, cardiac evaluation, ophthalmologist evaluation, autoimmune thyroiditis panel, and von Willebrand disease DNA testing for the Doberman Pinscher.

doberman-pinscher-club-america-health-st.name: Doberman Pinscher Club of America - Health Statement
doberman-pinscher-club-america-health-st.note: Parent breed club health statement covering dilated cardiomyopathy (echocardiogram and annual Holter monitoring), autoimmune thyroiditis, von Willebrand disease, liver disease (chronic hepatitis), cervical vertebral instability (Wobbler syndrome), hip dysplasia, and eye examinations.

fci-welsh-terrier-nomenclature.name: FCI - Welsh Terrier Breed Information
fci-welsh-terrier-nomenclature.note: FCI breed nomenclature lists Welsh Terrier as Standard No. 78, Group 3, with Great Britain as its country of origin. The current nomenclature page records the official valid standard date as 08 September 2026.

royal-kennel-club-welsh-terrier-standard.note: Official breed standard covering coat texture, colour, height not exceeding 39 cm, weight 9-9.5 kg, and working movement.

american-kennel-club-welsh-terrier.name: American Kennel Club - Welsh Terrier
american-kennel-club-welsh-terrier.note: Breed profile covering history, height (about 15 inches), average weight (20 pounds), 12-15 year lifespan, colours, grooming, exercise, and health screening.

welsh-terrier-club-america-health-statem.name: Welsh Terrier Club of America - Health Statement
welsh-terrier-club-america-health-statem.note: Parent breed club health statement approved 17 August 2016, recommending Primary Lens Luxation (PLL) DNA testing for breeding stock.

vcahospitals-welsh-terrier.name: VCA Animal Hospitals - Welsh Terrier
vcahospitals-welsh-terrier.note: Veterinary clinical overview covering grooming, exercise needs, temperament, and health considerations (glaucoma, lens luxation, allergies, and orthopedic conditions).

fci-finnish-hound-official-standard.note: Official English-language FCI Standard No. 51 (Group 6 Scent hounds and related breeds, Section 1.2 Medium-sized Hounds; origin Finland; male height 55-61 cm, female height 52-58 cm; tricolour with black mantle, rich tan markings and white patches).

finnish-kennel-club-finnish-hound.name: Finnish Kennel Club — Finnish Hound
finnish-kennel-club-finnish-hound.note: Breed overview by the Finnish Kennel Club (Suomen Kennelliitto) covering history, working purpose for hunting hare and fox, temperament, and hip-index breeding goals.

united-kennel-club-finnish-hound-standar.name: United Kennel Club — Finnish Hound Breed Standard
united-kennel-club-finnish-hound-standar.note: UKC Scenthound breed standard covering general appearance, rectangular body proportions, harsh double coat, and hunting characteristics.

zoetis-finnish-hound-profile.name: Zoetis Petcare — Finnish Hound Breed Profile
zoetis-finnish-hound-profile.note: Veterinary clinical profile providing typical lifespan and health guidance.

wikimedia-finnish-hound-canarian-2021.note: Photograph of a Finnish Hound by Canarian, dated 2021-08-01, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0.

fci-old-danish-pointing-dog-nomenclature.name: FCI - Gammel Dansk Hønsehund (Old Danish Pointing Dog) Nomenclature No. 281
fci-old-danish-pointing-dog-nomenclature.note: Official FCI nomenclature entry No. 281 confirming Denmark origin, Group 7 Section 1.1 (Continental Pointing Dogs, 'Braque' type) subject to a working trial, definitive acceptance on 1969-04-02, valid standard date 1998-01-08, and official multilingual names (Gammel Dansk Hønsehund, Old Danish Pointing Dog, Chien d'arrêt danois ancestral, Altdänischer Vorstehhund, Antiguo Perro de Muestra Danés).

fci-old-danish-pointing-dog-judges-compe.name: FCI & Klubben for Gamle Danske Hønsehunde — Judges' Compendium for the Old Danish Pointer (FCI Standard No. 281)
fci-old-danish-pointing-dog-judges-compe.publisher: Fédération Cynologique Internationale / Klubben for Gamle Danske Hønsehunde
fci-old-danish-pointing-dog-judges-compe.note: Official FCI breed-specific education compendium (March 2026) providing detailed illustrated commentary on FCI Standard No. 281, including complete 42-tooth dentition (20 upper, 22 lower), puppy-to-adult eye colour darkening, ear length (leaving just over the outer third of the muzzle free), throat dewlap hallmark, 50%/50% chest depth, 110°/125°/135° angulation, and faults/disqualifications.

danish-kennel-club-old-danish-pointing-d.name: Dansk Kennel Klub (DKK) — Gammel Dansk Hønsehund Breed Profile & Breeding Requirements
danish-kennel-club-old-danish-pointing-d.note: Official Danish Kennel Club breed profile and mandatory pre-breeding studbook regulations ('Avlskrav': mandatory pre-mating HD status A or B, or HD C only if mated to HD A; mandatory pre-mating rcd4/PRA DNA test status; documented normal testicles; and Basis+ GDH breeding permit introduced 1 September 2017).

danish-breed-club-breeding-approval.name: Klubben for Gamle Danske Hønsehunde — Hvad skal der til for at få sin hund avlsgodkendt?
danish-breed-club-breeding-approval.note: Official Danish breed-club 5-point breeding approval checklist: (1) minimum 'Good' show rating at ≥15 months of age, (2) official DKK hip dysplasia grading A, B, or C, (3) DNA status for congenital myasthenic syndrome ('muskeltræthed'), (4) hunting evaluation ('jagtlig vurdering') for both sexes, and (5) DNA test status for PRA.

old-danish-pointing-dog-pra-c17h2orf71-s.name: Karlskov-Mortensen et al. (2018) — Identification of the mutation causing progressive retinal atrophy in Old Danish Pointing Dog
old-danish-pointing-dog-pra-c17h2orf71-s.note: Peer-reviewed genomic study (Anim Genet. 2018 Jun;49(3):237-241, PMID 29624701) identifying the autosomal recessive single-base insertion c.3149_3150insC in exon 1 of C17H2orf71 (C2orf71 / PCARE, rcd4-PRA) as the cause of late-onset progressive retinal atrophy diagnosed in the Old Danish Pointing Dog since the late 1990s.

old-danish-pointing-dog-cms-chat-study.name: Proschowsky et al. (2007) — Identification of a mutation in the CHAT gene of Old Danish Pointing Dogs affected with congenital myasthenic syndrome
old-danish-pointing-dog-cms-chat-study.note: Peer-reviewed study (J Hered. 2007;98(5):539-543, PMID 17586598) identifying an autosomal recessive G-to-A missense mutation (valine-to-methionine substitution) in exon 6 of the choline acetyltransferase (CHAT) gene causing congenital myasthenic syndrome ('muskeltræthed') in Old Danish Pointing Dogs and establishing a breed-specific DNA test.

old-danish-pointing-dog-cms-clinical-stu.name: Flagstad et al. (1989) — Congenital Myasthenic Syndrome in the Dog Breed Gammel Dansk Hønsehund
old-danish-pointing-dog-cms-clinical-stu.note: Peer-reviewed clinical, electrophysiological, pharmacological, and immunological study (Acta Vet Scand. 1989;30(1):89-102, PMID 2782236 / PMCID PMC8142211) demonstrating a presynaptic congenital myasthenic syndrome without acetylcholine-receptor antibodies in the Gammel Dansk Hønsehund.

danish-dog-breeds-genetic-profile-study.name: Pertoldi et al. (2013) — Characterization of the genetic profile of five Danish dog breeds
danish-dog-breeds-genetic-profile-study.note: Peer-reviewed population genetics study (J Anim Sci. 2013 Nov;91(11):5122-5127, PMID 23989866) quantifying within-breed expected heterozygosity and genetic differentiation across five native Danish dog breeds including the Old Danish Pointing Dog.

wikimedia-old-danish-pointer-canarian.name: Wikimedia Commons — File:Old Danish Pointer.jpg
wikimedia-old-danish-pointer-canarian.note: Wikimedia Commons file page for 'File:Old Danish Pointer.jpg' (496 × 319 px), photographed by Canarian on 2008-10-31 and uploaded on 2013-10-23 under CC BY-SA 3.0.

fci-aidi-official-standard.name: FCI — Atlas Mountain Dog (Aidi), Standard No. 247
fci-aidi-official-standard.note: Official FCI Standard No. 247 (Group 2 Pinscher and Schnauzer, Molossoid and Swiss Mountain and Cattledogs; Section 2.2 Molossian, Mountain type; origin Morocco; height 52-62 cm; thick, weather-resistant coat with protective mane; not subject to working trial).

united-kennel-club-aidi-standard.name: United Kennel Club — Aidi (Atlas Mountain Dog) Official Breed Standard
united-kennel-club-aidi-standard.note: Official UKC Guardian Dog breed standard revised January 1, 2008, detailing body proportions (10:9 ratio), protective double coat, semi-prick ears, and guardian traits.

royal-canin-aidi-profile.name: Royal Canin — Aidi Breed Profile
royal-canin-aidi-profile.note: Breed overview providing a published 10-12 year average life expectancy estimate.

pubmed-aidi-leishmaniasis-study.name: Diagnosis and Prevalence of Canine Leishmaniasis in the Atlas Shepherd Dog
pubmed-aidi-leishmaniasis-study.publisher: PubMed / Veterinary Parasitology: Regional Studies and Reports
pubmed-aidi-leishmaniasis-study.note: Scientific study of 161 Atlas shepherd dogs in the Tiaret region of Algeria; findings reflect vector-borne infection rates specific to that geographic sample.

fci-puli-official-standard.name: FCI — Puli, Standard No. 55
fci-puli-official-standard.note: Official FCI Standard No. 55 (Group 1 Sheepdogs and Cattledogs, Section 1 Sheepdogs; origin Hungary; male height 39-45 cm, female height 36-42 cm; corded double coat with recognized colors pearl-white, black, black shaded with rust-red or grey, fawn with black mask, and grey).

american-kennel-club-puli.name: American Kennel Club — Puli Breed Profile
american-kennel-club-puli.note: Breed overview covering Herding Group classification, typical size, 10-15 year life expectancy, corded coat care, exercise, and recommended health testing.

puli-club-of-america-health-statement.name: Puli Club of America — Health Statement
puli-club-of-america-health-statement.note: Breed-club health testing recommendations for breeding stock covering hip dysplasia, patellar luxation, eye examination (CAER/CERF), and degenerative myelopathy (DM) DNA testing.

puli-club-of-america-faq.name: Puli Club of America — Frequently Asked Questions
puli-club-of-america-faq.note: Parent club informational FAQ discussing 10-15 year lifespan, cord formation, coat maintenance, and herding temperament.

enci-cane-da-pastore-abruzzese-maremmano.name: ENCI - Cane da Pastore Abruzzese Maremmano (FCI 201)
enci-cane-da-pastore-abruzzese-maremmano.note: Italian national kennel club breed monograph and Riproduzione Selezionata requirements: minimum age 18 months, minimum conformation qualification Molto Buono at a breed specialty or gathering, CPMA morphological-character test (TEST T.M.C. CPMA), hip dysplasia grade HD A or B, and elbow dysplasia grade ED 0 or 1; also documents Roman and medieval historical sources, the 1952 Brescia specialty, the 1958-01-01 unified standard, foundational kennels, and puppy weaning/development.

ukc-maremma-sheepdog-standard.name: United Kennel Club - Maremma Sheepdog Official Breed Standard
ukc-maremma-sheepdog-standard.note: UKC breed standard (recognized 2006-07-01, revised 2017-05-01) placing the breed in the Guardian Dog Group and recording the traditional pre-2025 size ranges (males 25.5–28.75 in / 77–100 lb; females 23.5–26.5 in / 66–88 lb) and tolerance of cropped ears only in working herd-guarding dogs.

rkc-maremma-sheepdog-breed-information.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Maremma Sheepdog Breed Information & Health Standard
rkc-maremma-sheepdog-breed-information.note: UK kennel club breed guide placing the Maremma Sheepdog in the Pastoral Group (Breed Watch Category 2), listing large size, over 2 hours of daily exercise, lifespan over 10 years, and Best Practice pre-breeding hip screening under the BVA/KC Hip Dysplasia Scheme.

warrnambool-middle-island-maremma-projec.name: Warrnambool Penguins - Maremma Dogs and the Middle Island Project
warrnambool-middle-island-maremma-projec.note: Official Warrnambool City Council conservation project documentation confirming that Maremma guardian dogs (beginning in 2006 with Eudy and Tula, named after Eudyptula minor) have protected Middle Island's Little Penguin colony from red foxes.

talenti-2023-italian-lgd-herding-selecti.name: Selection Signatures in Italian Livestock Guardian and Herding Shepherd Dogs (Veterinary Sciences, 2023)
talenti-2023-italian-lgd-herding-selecti.note: Open-access genomic study (170K canine SNP array across 158 dogs from 4 Italian livestock guardian and 5 herding shepherd breeds, including 20 Maremma and Abruzzi Sheepdogs) identifying selection signatures differentiating flock guardians from herding dogs around genes linked to body size/muscle development (MAP2K5, RYR3), drop vs. prick ear morphology (WIF1, MSRB3), behaviour (LLPH), and eye development.

donner-2023-canine-mendelian-disease-var.name: Genetic prevalence and clinical relevance of canine Mendelian disease variants in over one million dogs (PLOS Genetics, 2023)
donner-2023-canine-mendelian-disease-var.note: Open-access study (Donner et al., 2023, Table 2) reporting the Collie Eye Anomaly (CEA, OMIA Variant ID 632 / NHEJ1 intronic deletion) disease-associated allele at a 2.7% variant frequency in screened Maremma Sheepdogs (N = 37 dogs).

rombola-2021-leishmania-lazio-dogs.name: Seroprevalence and risk factors associated with exposure to Leishmania infantum in dogs, in an endemic Mediterranean region (PLOS ONE, 2021)
rombola-2021-leishmania-lazio-dogs.note: Open-access epidemiological study of 13,292 canine sera collected in Lazio, central Italy (2010–2014), finding that autochthonous Maremma Sheepdogs and long-coated dogs had significantly lower odds of Leishmania infantum seropositivity compared with non-autochthonous breeds (OR = 1.9 for other breeds vs. Maremma Sheepdog, p < 0.001).

fci-portuguese-water-dog-standard.name: FCI — Standard No. 37: Portuguese Water Dog
fci-portuguese-water-dog-standard.note: Official FCI Standard No. 37 (Group 8 Retrievers, Flushing Dogs and Water Dogs; Section 3 Water Dogs; origin Portugal; male height 50-57 cm, weight 19-25 kg; female height 43-52 cm, weight 16-22 kg; single coat in curly or wavy varieties).

portuguese-kennel-club-portuguese-water-.name: Clube Português de Canicultura — Portuguese Water Dog
portuguese-kennel-club-portuguese-water-.note: Official Portuguese national kennel club breed profile covering historical maritime background, working trials, and conformation measurements.

american-kennel-club-portuguese-water-do.name: American Kennel Club — Portuguese Water Dog
american-kennel-club-portuguese-water-do.note: Breed overview covering Working Group classification, coat varieties, grooming styles (lion clip and retriever clip), exercise, and parent-club health recommendations.

portuguese-water-dog-club-of-america-hea.name: Portuguese Water Dog Club of America — Health Overview
portuguese-water-dog-club-of-america-hea.publisher: Portuguese Water Dog Club of America
portuguese-water-dog-club-of-america-hea.note: Breed-club health testing recommendations covering hip dysplasia, ophthalmologist examination, and genetic testing for GM-1 gangliosidosis, prcd-PRA, EOPRA, microphthalmia, and juvenile dilated cardiomyopathy.

portuguese-water-dog-club-of-america-car.name: Portuguese Water Dog Club of America — Breed and Owner Guidance
portuguese-water-dog-club-of-america-car.publisher: Portuguese Water Dog Club of America
portuguese-water-dog-club-of-america-car.note: Owner guidance covering exercise needs, training, family life, grooming commitments, shedding characteristics, and allergy realities.

american-kennel-club-hovawart.name: American Kennel Club — Hovawart Breed Information
american-kennel-club-hovawart.note: AKC Foundation Stock Service breed profile (recorded in FSS since October 2010, assigned to the Working Group) listing height (23–28 in), weight (65–90 lbs), lifespan (10–14 years), low drooling level, exercise needs (at least a 1-hour walk plus 3–4 shorter daily walks), and hip dysplasia rates under 5%.

hovawart-club-of-great-britain-origins.name: Hovawart Club of Great Britain — Origins of the Hovawart (Dr. Jens Kerl Studbook Research)
hovawart-club-of-great-britain-origins.note: Summary of archival studbook research by Dr. Jens Kerl presented at the International Hovawart Federation (IHF) centenary, showing that Kurt König founded the Hovawart-Verein für Deutsche Schutzhunde in Thale in January 1924, that all modern lines trace to the 1932 sire Castor Meyer-Busch, and that modern bloodlines comprise ~65% regional farm 'Typenhunde', 20.2% German Shepherd Dog, and 14.8% Newfoundland (with Kuvasz used only in pre-WWI trials lost in the war).

mandrioli-2021-hovawart-degenerative-mye.name: Degenerative Myelopathy in Hovawart Dogs: Molecular Characterization, Pathological Features and Accumulation of Mutant Superoxide Dismutase 1 Protein (Journal of Comparative Pathology, 2021)
mandrioli-2021-hovawart-degenerative-mye.note: Mandrioli et al. (2021, doi:10.1016/j.jcpa.2020.11.006) molecular and neuropathological study of Hovawart dogs aged 9–12 years with progressive pelvic-limb ataxia and paraparesis, confirming homozygosity for SOD1:c.118G>A (p.E40K) and mutant SOD1 accumulation in spinal cord neurons and astrocytes without the SP110 risk haplotype.

ahlgren-uimari-2016-hovawart-hypothyroid.name: Heritability of hypothyroidism in the Finnish Hovawart population (Acta Veterinaria Scandinavica, 2016)
ahlgren-uimari-2016-hovawart-hypothyroid.publisher: Acta Veterinaria Scandinavica / PubMed Central (PMCID: PMC4897810; PMID: 27267591)
ahlgren-uimari-2016-hovawart-hypothyroid.note: Open-access genetic study (Åhlgren & Uimari, 2016, CC BY 4.0) of 4,953 Finnish Hovawarts born 1990–2010 estimating moderate-to-high heritability for hypothyroidism (h² = 0.47 via REML to 0.62 via Bayesian Gibbs sampling) and noting a 13% prevalence of autoimmune lymphocytic thyroiditis markers in Swedish Hovawarts (Ferm et al., 2009).

royal-kennel-club-english-toy-terrier-st.name: Royal Kennel Club - English Toy Terrier (Black & Tan) Breed Standard
royal-kennel-club-english-toy-terrier-st.note: Official breed standard published by The Royal Kennel Club; withers height: 25-30 cm (10-12 in), weight: 2.7-3.6 kg (6-8 lbs); defines head structure, candle-flame ears, jet black coat with rich chestnut tan markings, and light movement.

royal-kennel-club-english-toy-terrier-pr.name: Royal Kennel Club - English Toy Terrier (Black & Tan) Breed Profile
royal-kennel-club-english-toy-terrier-pr.note: Breed history, characteristics, exercise guidance (up to 30 minutes/day), grooming, lifespan (12-13 years), and vulnerable native breed status.

english-toy-terrier-club-health-testing.publisher: The English Toy Terrier (Black & Tan) Club
english-toy-terrier-club-health-testing.note: Parent breed club guidance on pre-breeding health testing, detailing patellar luxation, juvenile dilated cardiomyopathy (JDCM), xanthinuria, and ocular health.

wikimedia-english-toy-terrier-sannse.note: Photograph of an English Toy Terrier by Sannse with contrast adjustment by Pleple2000, captured 2003-08-29, uploaded 2006-07-24, dimensions 600 × 600 pixels, licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0.

the-dog-api.name: The Dog API
the-dog-api.note: Structured reference dataset used to cross-reference alternate names, metric measurements, weight estimates, lifespan, and temperament traits.

fci-pyrenean-mastiff-standard.name: FCI-Standard N° 92 — Mastín del Pirineo (Pyrenean Mastiff)
fci-pyrenean-mastiff-standard.note: Official English translation of FCI Standard No. 92 (published 26 May 1982, English translation 30 August 1992); specifies Spain as country of origin, minimum height of 77 cm for dogs and 72 cm for bitches (desirable >81 cm and >75 cm) with no upper limit, 6–9 cm bristly coat, mandatory dark mask, and disqualifications.

rsce-mastin-del-pirineo-standard.name: Real Sociedad Canina de España — Mastín del Pirineo (Estándar FCI Nº 92)
rsce-mastin-del-pirineo-standard.note: Official Spanish national kennel club breed page and authentic Spanish text of FCI Standard No. 92 for the Mastín del Pirineo.

ukc-pyrenean-mastiff-standard.name: United Kennel Club — Pyrenean Mastiff Official Breed Standard
ukc-pyrenean-mastiff-standard.note: Official UKC breed standard (recognized 1 July 2006 in the Guardian Dog Group); specifies lowest allowable height limits of 30 inches for males and 28 inches for females (desirable at least 32 inches and 29.5 inches) with no upper height limit.

pmaa-pyrenean-mastiff-health-testing.name: Pyrenean Mastiff Association of America — Health Testing & Official Health Statement
pmaa-pyrenean-mastiff-health-testing.note: Official PMAA Health Statement (approved 24 November 2024); specifies mandatory CHIC pre-breeding screenings at ≥24 months (OFA Hips, OFA Elbows, OFA Basic/Advanced Cardiac, and Degenerative Myelopathy SOD1 DNA test) and optional screenings (Spine radiographs at ≥24 months and CAER Eye exam at >12 months).

akc-tibetan-terrier-profile.name: American Kennel Club — Tibetan Terrier Dog Breed Information
akc-tibetan-terrier-profile.note: Breed profile covering Non-Sporting group placement, height (14–17 in), weight (18–30 lb), life expectancy (15–16 years), grooming, exercise, and national breed club health testing recommendations.

fci-tibetan-terrier-standard.name: Fédération Cynologique Internationale — FCI-Standard N° 209: Tibetan Terrier
fci-tibetan-terrier-standard.note: Official FCI Standard No. 209 (Group 9 Companion and Toy Dogs, Section 5 Tibetan breeds, without working trial; origin Tibet [China], patronage Great Britain). Specifies male height at withers 36–41 cm (females slightly smaller) and permits any coat colour except chocolate, liver, or merle.

fci-tibetan-terrier-nomenclature.name: Fédération Cynologique Internationale — Tibetan Terrier (209) Nomenclature
fci-tibetan-terrier-nomenclature.note: FCI nomenclature entry recording definitive recognition on 18 December 1957 under Group 9, Section 5 (Tibetan breeds).

rkc-tibetan-terrier-standard.name: The Royal Kennel Club — Tibetan Terrier Breed Standard
rkc-tibetan-terrier-standard.note: Official UK Utility Group breed standard (updated April 2025); specifies male height 36–41 cm (14–16 in) with females slightly smaller, scissor or reverse scissor bite with slightly curved incisor arcade, flat round snowshoe feet without arch, and any colour permissible except chocolate, liver, or merle.

ttca-tibetan-terrier-standard-guide.name: Tibetan Terrier Club of America — Illustrated Guide to the Tibetan Terrier Standard
ttca-tibetan-terrier-standard-guide.note: Parent-club illustrated commentary on the Tibetan Terrier standard explaining high-altitude adaptations, flat un-arched snowshoe foot anatomy vs. cat/hare feet, optional dewclaw removal and permissible double dewclaws, natural un-sculpted coat presentation, and acceptable scissor, reverse scissor, level, or slightly undershot bites.

ttca-tibetan-terrier-history.name: Tibetan Terrier Club of America — Breed History
ttca-tibetan-terrier-history.note: Parent-club historical account detailing Dr. Agnes R. H. Greig's 1922 gift of the gold-and-white female puppy Bunti in India, the 1924 Christmas Day first litter sired by Rajah, the Lamleh kennel prefix, 1930 renaming from Lhasa Terrier to Tibetan Terrier by the Kennel Club of India, 1937 UK recognition, 1956 US importation by Dr. Henry and Alice Murphy, and 1973 AKC recognition.

ofa-tibetan-terrier-ncl.name: Orthopedic Foundation for Animals — Neuronal Ceroid Lipofuscinosis (NCL-TT)
ofa-tibetan-terrier-ncl.note: Clinical and genetic overview of Tibetan Terrier late-onset neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis (NCL-TT), detailing progressive behavioral/anxiety changes, ataxia and difficulty with stairs/jumping, dim-light visual impairment, and late-stage seizures.

petmd-tibetan-terrier.name: PetMD — Tibetan Terrier Dog Breed Health and Care
petmd-tibetan-terrier.note: Veterinary-reviewed breed guide covering height (14–17 in), weight (up to 30 lb), lifespan (15–16 years), exercise needs (at least 1 hour daily), grooming, separation anxiety sensitivity, and inherited conditions.

pubmed-tibetan-terrier-ncl-atp13a2.name: Wöhlke et al. (2011) — A One Base Pair Deletion in the Canine ATP13A2 Gene Causes Exon Skipping and Late-Onset Neuronal Ceroid Lipofuscinosis in the Tibetan Terrier
pubmed-tibetan-terrier-ncl-atp13a2.note: Identifies the autosomal recessive c.1620delG single-base deletion in exon 16 of ATP13A2 on CFA2 causing exon skipping (69-amino-acid loss) and adult/late-onset neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis in Tibetan Terriers.

pubmed-tibetan-terrier-ccl-selection.name: prim-vet / KTR Study (2014) — Selection Response to DNA Testing for Canine Ceroid Lipofuscinosis in Tibetan Terriers
pubmed-tibetan-terrier-ccl-selection.note: Genotyped 1,120 Tibetan Terriers (1987–2012), showing the ATP13A2 mutant allele frequency declined from 0.20–0.28 before 2010 DNA testing to 0.09–0.14 after DNA screening implementation.

pubmed-tibetan-terrier-pra3-fam161a.name: Downs & Mellersh (2014) — An Intronic SINE Insertion in FAM161A That Causes Exon-Skipping Is Associated with Progressive Retinal Atrophy in Tibetan Spaniels and Tibetan Terriers
pubmed-tibetan-terrier-pra3-fam161a.note: Identifies the intronic SINE insertion in FAM161A on CFA10 causing exon skipping and progressive retinal atrophy type 3 (PRA3) in Tibetan Spaniels and Tibetan Terriers.

wikimedia-tibetan-terrier-8yo-male.name: Wikimedia Commons — File:8 year old male Tibetan Terrier.jpg
wikimedia-tibetan-terrier-8yo-male.note: Photograph of an 8-year-old male Tibetan Terrier in a practical pet trim ('puppy cut') by Getsnarky, captured 14 December 2019 (iPhone XS Max) and uploaded 8 December 2020 (2,049 × 1,537 px), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0.

wikimedia-tibet-terrier-bennie.name: Wikimedia Commons — File:Tibet Terrier Bennie.jpg
wikimedia-tibet-terrier-bennie.note: Photograph of a black Tibetan Terrier standing in snow by Mr407SW, captured 8 March 2006 (Canon EOS 350D EXIF) and uploaded 19 March 2008 (1,728 × 1,152 px), released into the public domain ({{PD-self}}).

fci-clumber-spaniel-standard.name: FCI Standard No. 109 - Clumber Spaniel
fci-clumber-spaniel-standard.note: Official valid FCI Standard No. 109. Origin Great Britain; Group 8 Retrievers, Flushing Dogs and Water Dogs, Section 2 Flushing Dogs; defines head, body substance, coat texture, coloration, and working characteristics.

royal-kennel-club-clumber-spaniel-standa.name: Royal Kennel Club - Spaniel (Clumber) Breed Standard
royal-kennel-club-clumber-spaniel-standa.note: Official UK breed standard covering general appearance, characteristics, temperament, coat feathering, and movement.

royal-kennel-club-clumber-spaniel-profil.name: Royal Kennel Club - Spaniel (Clumber) Breed Profile
royal-kennel-club-clumber-spaniel-profil.note: Breed history at Clumber Park, characteristics, exercise guidance (up to 1 hour per day), grooming, lifespan, and vulnerable native breed status.

american-kennel-club-clumber-spaniel-sta.name: American Kennel Club - Official Standard for the Clumber Spaniel
american-kennel-club-clumber-spaniel-sta.note: Official breed standard specifying height (dogs 18-20 in, bitches 17-19 in) and weight (dogs 70-85 lbs, bitches 55-70 lbs).

american-kennel-club-clumber-spaniel-pro.name: American Kennel Club - Clumber Spaniel Dog Breed Information
american-kennel-club-clumber-spaniel-pro.note: Breed profile covering sporting background, drooling, shedding, grooming, temperament, and health.

royal-kennel-club-clumber-spaniel-health.name: Royal Kennel Club - Clumber Spaniel Breed Health Information
royal-kennel-club-clumber-spaniel-health.note: Breed health guidance outlining pre-breeding testing priorities including EIC, PDP1 deficiency, and hip/elbow screening.

ecvo-clumber-spaniel-eye-conditions.name: ECVO Manual: Breeds - Clumber Spaniel Eye Diseases
ecvo-clumber-spaniel-eye-conditions.note: Veterinary ophthalmology manual documenting known and presumed inherited eye conditions in the Clumber Spaniel.

wikimedia-clumber-spaniel-audrey-sel-201.name: Wikimedia Commons - ClumberSpaniel.jpg
wikimedia-clumber-spaniel-audrey-sel-201.note: Photograph of a Clumber Spaniel by audrey_sel, uploaded 2017-10-19, dimensions 3888 × 2592 pixels, licensed under CC BY-SA 2.0.

wikimedia-clumber-spaniel-audrey-sel-200.name: Wikimedia Commons - Clumber Spaniel.jpg
wikimedia-clumber-spaniel-audrey-sel-200.note: Photograph of a Clumber Spaniel by audrey_sel, uploaded 2009-05-24, dimensions 2984 × 1989 pixels, licensed under CC BY-SA 2.0.

wikimedia-clumber-spaniel-canarian-2017.note: Photograph of a Clumber Spaniel outdoors by Canarian, captured 2017-12-09, uploaded 2018-01-29, dimensions 2297 × 1646 pixels, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0.

fci-broholmer-standard-2025.name: FCI Standard No. 315 - Broholmer
fci-broholmer-standard-2025.note: Official valid standard published on 3 May 2025; English version dated 16 May 2025. Origin Denmark; Group 2 Pinscher and Schnauzer, Molossoid and Swiss Mountain Dogs, Section 2.1 Molossian, Mastiff type; withers height: males approx. 75 cm, females approx. 70 cm; weight: males 50-70 kg, females 40-60 kg; covers historical background, estate guarding purpose, temperament, coat, and morphological characteristics.

dkk-broholmer-profile.name: Danish Kennel Club - Broholmer
dkk-broholmer-profile.note: Breed profile covering size, temperament, coat care, activity, and everyday handling from the Danish national kennel club.

american-kennel-club-broholmer.name: American Kennel Club - Broholmer
american-kennel-club-broholmer.note: Breed profile listing height, weight, and an 8-10 year life expectancy range.

royal-canin-broholmer.name: Royal Canin India - Broholmer
royal-canin-broholmer.note: Breed profile covering historical background and life expectancy estimates.

broholmerselskabet-health.name: Broholmerselskabet - Health
broholmerselskabet-health.note: Danish parent breed club health overview and monitoring protocols for hip dysplasia, elbow dysplasia, osteochondrosis dissecans (OCD), spondylosis, and subaortic stenosis (SAS).

wikimedia-broholmer-634.note: Photograph of a Broholmer by Pleple2000, captured 2006-11-11 and uploaded 2006-11-22, dimensions 2916 × 2112 pixels, licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0.

fci-manchester-terrier-standard.name: FCI Standard No. 71 - Manchester Terrier
fci-manchester-terrier-standard.note: Official valid FCI Standard No. 71; English PDF dated 10 January 2011. Origin Great Britain; Group 3 Terriers, Section 1 Medium and Large-Sized Terriers; ideal height at withers: dogs 41 cm (16 in), bitches 38 cm (15 in); covers head, dentition, coat, coloration, and working characteristics.

akc-manchester-terrier-standard.name: American Kennel Club - Official Standard of the Manchester Terrier
akc-manchester-terrier-standard.note: Official breed standard covering Standard and Toy size varieties; specifies weight for the Standard variety as over 12 pounds and not exceeding 22 pounds.

akc-manchester-terrier-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Manchester Terrier (Standard)
akc-manchester-terrier-profile.note: Breed profile covering historical background, lifespan (15-17 years), exercise, training, grooming, and recommended health testing.

royal-kennel-club-manchester-terrier-pro.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Manchester Terrier Breed Profile
royal-kennel-club-manchester-terrier-pro.note: Breed profile covering size, exercise recommendations, grooming, lifespan (over 12 years), English origins, and home suitability.

american-manchester-terrier-health.name: American Manchester Terrier Club - Health and Research
american-manchester-terrier-health.note: Parent club health testing protocol for Standard and Toy Manchester Terriers, outlining screenings for von Willebrand disease type 1, autoimmune thyroiditis, cardiac health, eye examinations, and congenital deafness.

wikimedia-manchester-terrier-photo.name: Wikimedia Commons - Manchester Terrier.jpg
wikimedia-manchester-terrier-photo.note: Photograph of a Manchester Terrier by Jon Ovington, captured 2008-12-02, uploaded 2012-07-18, dimensions 900 × 1200 pixels, licensed under CC BY-SA 2.0.

continental-kennel-club-black-mouth-cur-.name: Continental Kennel Club — Breed Spotlight: The Black Mouth Cur
continental-kennel-club-black-mouth-cur-.note: Historical and functional breed spotlight discussing Irish, Scottish, English, and French settler dog ancestry, brownish-pink to dark grey gum/lip pigmentation, and modern hog-catching, herding, and hunting roles.

embark-black-mouth-cur.name: Embark Veterinary — Black Mouth Cur Breed & Genetic Profile
embark-black-mouth-cur.note: Canine genetics and veterinary breed guide reporting male height (18–25 in) and weight (50–95 lb), female height (16–23 in) and weight (45–90 lb), multi-generational Southern family breeding lines (Alabama, Tennessee, Florida), child and pet compatibility, and high outdoor exercise requirements.

fci-deutsch-stichelhaar-nomenclature.name: Fédération Cynologique Internationale — Deutsch Stichelhaar (232) Nomenclature
fci-deutsch-stichelhaar-nomenclature.note: FCI breed nomenclature entry recording definitive recognition on 24 August 1961 (historical pre-1964 date recorded in note), Group 7 Section 1.1 (Continental Pointing Dogs, Braque type, with working trial), and official multilingual breed names.

verein-deutsch-stichelhaar-ev.name: Verein Deutsch Stichelhaar e.V. — Offizielle Vereinswebseite & Rasseporträt
verein-deutsch-stichelhaar-ev.note: Official German parent club (founded 1892 as Club Stichelhaar, renamed 1976) documenting pure breeding without English pointer crosses, versatile work in field, forest, and water (VJP, HZP, VGP), digital health monitoring, and family/handler bond.

verein-deutsch-stichelhaar-hd-ed-ocd.name: Verein Deutsch Stichelhaar e.V. — Verfahrensweise für die Begutachtung der HD, OC(D) und ED Röntgenaufnahmen & Zuchtordnung
verein-deutsch-stichelhaar-hd-ed-ocd.note: Official parent-club veterinary radiographic procedure and breeding-regulation documentation requiring pre-breeding evaluation for hip dysplasia (HD), shoulder osteochondrosis (OC/OCD), and elbow dysplasia (ED).

ukc-german-rough-haired-pointer-standard.name: United Kennel Club — Official Breed Standard: German Rough Haired Pointer
ukc-german-rough-haired-pointer-standard.note: Official UKC breed standard (recognised 2006, Gun Dog Group) specifying history, conformation, coat (~1.5 in), colours, height (23.5–27.5 in males, 23–27 in females), and disqualifications.

fci-spinone-italiano-standard.name: FCI Standard No. 165 - Spinone Italiano
fci-spinone-italiano-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 165. Origin Italy; Group 7 Pointing Dogs, Section 1.3 Continental Pointing Dogs, Griffon type; withers height: males 60-70 cm, females 58-65 cm; weight: males 34-39 kg, females 29-34 kg; covers historical background, versatile hunting utilization, wiry coat, coloration, and morphological characteristics.

the-kennel-club-italian-spinone-standard.name: The Kennel Club - Italian Spinone Breed Standard
the-kennel-club-italian-spinone-standard.note: Breed standard including measurements, coat texture, accepted colours, working characteristics, and temperament.

american-kennel-club-spinone-italiano.name: American Kennel Club - Spinone Italiano
american-kennel-club-spinone-italiano.note: Breed profile covering life expectancy (10-12 years), size parameters, hunting heritage, and breed traits.

spinone-club-of-america-about-spinoni.name: Spinone Club of America - About Spinoni
spinone-club-of-america-about-spinoni.note: National breed club overview covering history, working roles on land and in water, coat care, exercise, and longevity.

spinone-club-of-america-health.name: Spinone Club of America - Health
spinone-club-of-america-health.note: Breed club health guidance detailing hip dysplasia, elbow dysplasia, eye conditions, thyroid screening, and cerebellar ataxia testing.

wikimedia-spinone-italiano-photo.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Spinone Italiano.jpg
wikimedia-spinone-italiano-photo.note: Photograph of a Spinone Italiano by Caroline Granycome, captured 2012-06-09, uploaded 2012-09-13, dimensions 4288 × 2848 pixels, licensed under CC BY-SA 2.0.

fci-mudi-standard-2023.name: FCI Standard No. 238 - Mudi
fci-mudi-standard-2023.note: Official valid standard published 25 September 2023; English standard document dated 27 October 2023. Covers classification (Group 1, Section 1), origin (Hungary), physical proportions, coat texture, coloration, and size parameters (males 41–47 cm and 11–13 kg; females 38–44 cm and 8–11 kg).

american-kennel-club-mudi.name: American Kennel Club - Mudi
american-kennel-club-mudi.note: Breed profile covering life expectancy (12–14 years), traits, exercise needs, and national breed club health screening recommendations.

canadian-kennel-club-mudi.name: Canadian Kennel Club - Mudi
canadian-kennel-club-mudi.note: Breed profile with sex-specific height and weight in its original published units.

mudi-club-of-america-health-testing.name: Mudi Club of America - Understanding Health Testing
mudi-club-of-america-health-testing.note: National parent club health screening guidance covering hip, elbow, patella, ophthalmologist, and cardiac evaluations.

mudi-club-of-america-faq.name: Mudi Club of America - Frequently Asked Questions
mudi-club-of-america-faq.note: Parent club FAQ addressing breed history, temperament, exercise needs, vocal tendencies, and longevity.

petmd-mudi-breed.name: PetMD - Mudi Dog Breed Health and Care
petmd-mudi-breed.note: Veterinary-reviewed care and exercise overview; provides general activity and wellness context.

wikimedia-commons-mudi-jpg.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Mudi.jpg
wikimedia-commons-mudi-jpg.note: Photograph of a black Mudi by Canarian, captured 2006-03-03, uploaded 2013-10-23, dimensions 294 × 355 pixels, licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0.

klub-tirolerbracke-welpen.name: Klub Tirolerbracke (Österreich) — Welpenbestellung & Vergaberichtlinien
klub-tirolerbracke-welpen.note: Official Austrian parent club puppy placement guidelines confirming that puppies are placed exclusively with licensed hunters who hold a valid hunting permit (Jagdkarte) and hunting grounds, with priority given to professional hunters (Berufsjäger).

klub-tirolerbracke-de-rasse.name: Klub Tirolerbracke Deutschland e.V. — Rasse & Jagdliche Verwendung
klub-tirolerbracke-de-rasse.note: Official German parent club breed overview describing descent from the Keltenbracke/Alpenbracke, solo hunting style (Solojäger, 200–800 m Brackieren loops), driven ungulate hunting (Bewegungsjagden), blood tracking (Totverweisen and Totverbellen), unsuitability for pack or pure kennel keeping, and hunter-only puppy placement.

klub-tirolerbracke-de-standard.name: Klub Tirolerbracke Deutschland e.V. — Rassestandard der Tiroler Bracke
klub-tirolerbracke-de-standard.note: Official German parent club standard summary specifying withers height (44–50 cm males, 42–48 cm females) and typical adult weight of approximately 15–22 kg ('Gewicht: ca. 15 – 22 kg (Das Gewicht ist im Standard nicht festgelegt.)').

klub-tirolerbracke-de-zucht.name: Klub Tirolerbracke Deutschland e.V. — Zuchtvoraussetzungen & HD-Beurteilung
klub-tirolerbracke-de-zucht.note: Official German parent club breeding regulations requiring minimum conformation grade 'sehr gut' (SG), field trial qualification (gun-steadiness and minimum 'gut' in Spurlaut), minimum breeding age (20 months females, 24 months males), and mandatory hip dysplasia (HD) radiographic evaluation (HD A, B, and C allowed; HD D and E barred; HD C paired only with HD A).

klub-tirolerbracke-de-klub.name: Klub Tirolerbracke Deutschland e.V. — Geschichte der Rasse und des Klubs
klub-tirolerbracke-de-klub.note: Detailed historical account covering the medieval Eastern Alpine Wildbodenhund, 1786–1809 population decline, 1860 pure breeding, 1896 Innsbruck dog show standard, 9–10 May 1908 Innsbruck recognition, 1931 conservation under Richard Sauerwein, post-1945 recovery, and 1950 founding of Klub Tirolerbracke in Innsbruck.

ukc-tyrolean-hound-standard.name: United Kennel Club — Official Breed Standard: Tyrolean Hound
ukc-tyrolean-hound-standard.note: Official UKC breed standard (recognised 2006, Scenthound Group) confirming history, conformation, complete scissors bite (up to two premolars absent permitted), height (17–19.5 in males, 16.5–19 in females), colours, and disqualifications.

royal-canin-at-tyrolean-hound.name: Royal Canin Österreich — Tiroler Bracke Rasseporträt
royal-canin-at-tyrolean-hound.note: Austrian breed profile reporting an average lifespan of 12–14 years ('Durchschnittliche Lebenserwartung: 12-14 Jahre'), low grooming needs, watchful nature, and requirement for outdoor space.

pubmed-tyrolean-hound-inbreeding-2009.name: Voges & Distl (2009) — Inbreeding trends and pedigree analysis of Bavarian mountain hounds, Hanoverian hounds and Tyrolean hounds
pubmed-tyrolean-hound-inbreeding-2009.publisher: Journal of Animal Breeding and Genetics / PubMed (PMID: 19765162)
pubmed-tyrolean-hound-inbreeding-2009.note: Peer-reviewed pedigree analysis of 1,167 Tyrolean Hounds registered between 1992 and 2004 (with pedigree records from the 1960s onward), reporting a 5.0-year generation interval, 9.5% mean inbreeding coefficient, 4.3 effective founder genomes, effective population size Ne = 26.5, and 77.9% genetic contribution from the top 10 ancestors.

fci-bernese-mountain-dog-nomenclature.name: FCI Breeds Nomenclature — Berner Sennenhund (45)
fci-bernese-mountain-dog-nomenclature.note: Official FCI nomenclature entry confirming definitive recognition on 26 July 1954, Group 2 Section 3 classification without working trial, and official multilingual breed names (Berner Sennenhund, Bernese Mountain Dog, Bouvier Bernois, Boyero de Montaña Bernés).

akc-bernese-mountain-dog-standard.name: American Kennel Club — Official Standard of the Bernese Mountain Dog
akc-bernese-mountain-dog-standard.note: Official AKC breed standard (approved 10 February 1990, effective 28 March 1990) verifying height in inches (25–27.5 in males, 23–26 in females), dry-mouthed lip structure with only slightly developed flews, slow trot natural working gait, tricolour markings including the inverted white chest cross, and disqualifications for blue eye colour or any ground colour other than black.

bmdca-diseases-and-conditions.name: Bernese Mountain Dog Club of America — Diseases and Conditions
bmdca-diseases-and-conditions.publisher: Bernese Mountain Dog Club of America (BMDCA)
bmdca-diseases-and-conditions.note: Comprehensive breed health reference detailing histiocytic sarcoma (and the 2005 BMDCA Health Study finding that 67% of surveyed deaths were attributable to cancer), mast cell tumours, lymphoma, hemangiosarcoma, degenerative myelopathy (two SOD1 mutations), hip and elbow dysplasia, osteochondritis dissecans, panosteitis, progressive retinal atrophy, cataracts, entropion/ectropion, sub-aortic stenosis, von Willebrand disease, hypothyroidism, aseptic meningitis, food allergies/IBD, and gastric dilatation-volvulus (bloat).

kbs-berner-sennenhund-rassenstandard.name: Schweizerischer Klub für Berner Sennenhunde (KBS) — Rassenstandard
kbs-berner-sennenhund-rassenstandard.note: Official Swiss parent club breed standard in the original German language confirming historical development in the Canton of Bern, anatomical proportions, tricolour markings, and height ranges.

pubmed-39335301.name: Ghilardi S. et al. (2024) — Genotypic and Allelic Frequencies of Degenerative Myelopathy in an Italian Canine Population (Animals 14(18):2712, PMID: 39335301)
pubmed-39335301.note: Peer-reviewed genetic epidemiology study (DOI: 10.3390/ani14182712) evaluating SOD1 c.118G>A (Exon 2) and breed-specific c.52A>T (Exon 1) mutations across 1,667 canine DNA tests, establishing a 7.61% allelic frequency for the SOD1 c.52A>T variant in Bernese Mountain Dogs.

pubmed-36292578.name: Thai T. et al. (2022) — Identification of a Hypomorphic FANCG Variant in Bernese Mountain Dogs (Genes 13(10):1693, PMID: 36292578)
pubmed-36292578.note: Peer-reviewed molecular genetics study (DOI: 10.3390/genes13101693) investigating heritable predisposition to histiocytic sarcoma and DNA repair variants near the MTAP/CDKN2A locus on canine chromosome 11 in Bernese Mountain Dogs.

fci-brittany-spaniel-nomenclature.name: FCI — Épagneul Breton (95) Nomenclature Entry
fci-brittany-spaniel-nomenclature.note: Official FCI nomenclature entry confirming breed number 95, Group 7 (Pointing Dogs), Section 1.2 (Continental Pointing Dogs, Spaniel type), and working-trial requirement.

american-brittany-club-code-of-ethics.name: American Brittany Club — Breeders Code of Ethics
american-brittany-club-code-of-ethics.note: Parent-club code of ethics (adopted November 30, 1996) documenting breeder standards, minimum breeding age of two years, and the club's commitment to preserving the Brittany as a dual field-and-show dog.

pubmed-brittany-natural-bobtail-ltv-2026.name: Association between the natural bobtail phenotype and lumbosacral transitional vertebra in Brittany dogs and Danish-Swedish Farmdogs
pubmed-brittany-natural-bobtail-ltv-2026.note: Peer-reviewed radiographic study by Berg et al. (Can Vet J 2026;67(8):882–888) evaluating 744 Brittany dogs. Reports a 26.7% prevalence of the natural bobtail phenotype (stump + short, linked to the T-box transcription factor T-gene) and a 47.8% prevalence of lumbosacral transitional vertebrae (LTV), with bobtailed Brittanys showing significantly higher odds of LTV (OR = 2.04, P < 0.001).

pubmed-brittany-complement-c3-deficiency.name: Genetically determined deficiency of the third component of complement in the dog
pubmed-brittany-complement-c3-deficiency.note: Seminal peer-reviewed study by Winkelstein et al. (Science 1981;212(4499):1169–1170) identifying an autosomal recessive deficiency of complement component C3 in Brittany spaniels.

akc-great-dane-standard.name: American Kennel Club — Official Standard of the Great Dane
akc-great-dane-standard.note: AKC Official Standard of the Great Dane (approved July 9, 2018; effective January 1, 2019). pubmed-great-dane-gdv-risk-factors-2000.name: Non-dietary risk factors for gastric dilatation-volvulus in large and giant breed dogs (J Am Vet Med Assoc 2000; PMID 11128539)
pubmed-great-dane-gdv-risk-factors-2000.publisher: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association (PubMed)
pubmed-great-dane-gdv-risk-factors-2000.note: Prospective cohort study by Glickman et al. (2000) identifying advancing age, a first-degree relative with gastric dilatation-volvulus history, rapid eating speed, and raised food bowls as significant non-dietary risk factors in large and giant breeds including the Great Dane.

pubmed-great-dane-prophylactic-gastropex.name: Benefits of prophylactic gastropexy for dogs at risk of gastric dilatation-volvulus (Prev Vet Med 2003; PMID 12941556)
pubmed-great-dane-prophylactic-gastropex.note: Peer-reviewed decision-tree analysis by Ward et al. (2003) estimating a 36.7% (95% CI: 25.2–44.6%) lifetime risk of gastric dilatation-volvulus in the Great Dane and demonstrating a 29.6-fold reduction in GDV-related mortality following prophylactic gastropexy.

pubmed-great-dane-dcm-expression-2009.name: Decreased triadin and increased calstabin2 expression in Great Danes with dilated cardiomyopathy (J Vet Intern Med 2009; PMID 19674278)
pubmed-great-dane-dcm-expression-2009.note: Prospective molecular study by Oyama et al. (2009) investigating dilated cardiomyopathy in Great Danes and demonstrating altered cardiac expression of calstabin2 and triadin affecting myocyte calcium regulation.
