national-toy-fox-terrier-association-hea.note: Parent breed club health guidance on patellar luxation, primary lens luxation, congenital hypothyroidism with goiter, and spinocerebellar ataxia.

wikimedia-toy-fox-terrier-ltshears.name: Wikimedia Commons — File:Toy Fox Terrier.jpg
wikimedia-toy-fox-terrier-ltshears.note: Photograph of a Toy Fox Terrier by Ltshears, captured 2008-07-26, uploaded 2008-08-14, dimensions 1016 × 1008 pixels, licensed under CC BY 3.0.

fci-sabueso-espanol-standard.name: FCI Standard No. 204 — Sabueso Español
fci-sabueso-espanol-standard.note: Official English-language breed standard dated 24 July 1999 (valid from 26 May 1982). Covers origin in Spain, Group 6 Section 1.2 classification, hunting history, temperament, white-and-orange coat, and withers height (males 52–57 cm, females 48–53 cm).

zoetis-sabueso-espanol-profile.name: Zoetis Spain — Sabueso Español Breed Profile
zoetis-sabueso-espanol-profile.note: Veterinary breed dossier covering general physical traits, healthcare, and life expectancy estimates (11–14 years).

royal-canin-sabueso-espanol.name: Royal Canin — Sabueso Español
royal-canin-sabueso-espanol.note: Breed profile detailing general temperament, working history, and life expectancy estimate (10–13 years).

wikimedia-sabueso-espanol-photo.name: Wikimedia Commons — File:Sabueso Espanol.jpg
wikimedia-sabueso-espanol-photo.publisher: Wikimedia Commons; original photographer Steffen Heinz Caronna
wikimedia-sabueso-espanol-photo.note: Photograph of an adult Sabueso Español by Steffen Heinz Caronna, uploaded 2011-06-02, dimensions 842 × 818 pixels, licensed under CC BY 3.0.

societe-centrale-canine-gascon-saintonge.name: Société Centrale Canine — Gascon Saintongeois Breed Profile
societe-centrale-canine-gascon-saintonge.note: Official French national kennel club breed dossier verifying general description, history of the Grand and Petit varieties, short tight coat, white-and-black pied coloration with pale tan markings and roebuck mark, height ranges (Grand 62–72 cm, Petit 54–62 cm), and unspecified official weight ('Poids: NP').

club-bleu-gascogne-gascon-saintongeois-s.name: Club du Bleu de Gascogne, Gascon Saintongeois et Ariégeois — Standard et Standard de Travail du Gascon-Saintongeois
club-bleu-gascogne-gascon-saintongeois-s.publisher: Club du Bleu de Gascogne, Gascon Saintongeois et Ariégeois (Société Centrale Canine)
club-bleu-gascogne-gascon-saintongeois-s.note: Official French parent breed club publication (published 11/12/2017, updated 24/09/2020) providing the full conformation standard, body proportions (10:10.5 height-to-length ratio; equal skull and muzzle length), disqualifying faults, and official working standard (Standard de Travail) detailing scenting finesse, deep howling voice, endurance, and pack hunting behaviour.

ukc-grand-gascon-saintongeois-standard.name: United Kennel Club — Official Breed Standard: Grand Gascon-Saintongeois
ukc-grand-gascon-saintongeois-standard.note: UKC Official Breed Standard for the Grand Gascon-Saintongeois (recognized January 1, 1993; revised January 1, 2009). Verifies Scenthound Group classification, Château de Virelade origin history (three surviving Saintongeois hounds—one female and two males—crossed with Baron de Ruble's Grand Bleu de Gascogne), conformation, coat and markings, and imperial height ranges (25.5–28 in males, 24.5–27 in females).

ukc-petit-gascon-saintongeois-standard.name: United Kennel Club — Official Breed Standard: Petit Gascon-Saintongeois
ukc-petit-gascon-saintongeois-standard.note: UKC Official Breed Standard for the Petit Gascon-Saintongeois (recognized January 1, 1993; revised January 1, 2009). Verifies Scenthound Group classification, southwestern French development from smaller Grand Gascon-Saintongeois hounds, conformation, and imperial height ranges (22–24 in males, 21–23 in females).

pubmed-gascon-saintongeois-vagus-mpnst-2.name: A rare case of malignant vagus nerve sheath tumor presenting with multiple cranial nerve dysfunction in a dog (Can Vet J 2020; PMID 33012818)
pubmed-gascon-saintongeois-vagus-mpnst-2.note: Peer-reviewed clinical case report by Giraud et al. (2020) describing an isolated high-grade epithelioid malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor of the vagus nerve in a 5-year-old intact male Gascon Saintongeois in France. Cited strictly as an isolated veterinary case report rather than a prevalent breed-wide condition.

fci-american-akita-standard-344.name: FCI Standard No. 344 — American Akita
fci-american-akita-standard-344.note: Official breed standard covering origin in Japan, development in the United States, classification in Group 5 Section 5, massive head, bear-like appearance, double coat, and withers height (males 66–71 cm, females 61–66 cm).

akita-club-america-health-concerns.name: Akita Club of America — Health Concerns
akita-club-america-health-concerns.note: Parent club overview of primary hereditary and health conditions affecting the breed, including bloat, sebaceous adenitis, hip dysplasia, eye conditions, and hypothyroidism.

akita-club-america-health-clearances.name: Akita Club of America — Health Clearances
akita-club-america-health-clearances.note: Parent club recommendations on health screenings for breeding stock, including hip, eye, and thyroid evaluations.

wikimedia-american-akita-jonnydrh.name: Wikimedia Commons — File:American-akita.jpg
wikimedia-american-akita-jonnydrh.note: Photograph of an adult American Akita by Jonnydrh, captured 2012-01-31, uploaded 2012-01-31, dimensions 1025 × 794 pixels, dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0.

klub-dachsbracke-breed-profile.name: Klub Dachsbracke — Erscheinungsbild und Geschichte der Alpenländischen Dachsbracke
klub-dachsbracke-breed-profile.note: Official Austrian parent breed club profile detailing the Alpine Dachsbracke's history (1890 pure breeding, 1896 Munich club, 11 June 1910 founding of Klub Dachsbracke in Vienna, 1932 recognition as third Schweißhund breed), blood-tracking and vocal hunting roles, early maturity, training needs, and calm family demeanor indoors.

klub-dachsbracke-pruefungsfaecher.name: Klub Dachsbracke — Prüfungsfächer für Alpenländische Dachsbracken
klub-dachsbracke-pruefungsfaecher.note: Official Austrian parent club working trial curriculum covering blood tracking on and off lead (Riemenarbeit), vocal trailing (Laute Jagd / Spurlaut), steadiness, obedience, dead-game indication (Totverweisen / Totverbellen), and wild boar aptitude.

royal-canin-alpine-dachsbracke.name: Royal Canin — Alpine Dachsbracke Breed Guide
royal-canin-alpine-dachsbracke.note: Breed profile summarizing the Alpine Dachsbracke's Austrian origin, calm and confident temperament, patience with children and other animals, high exercise requirement, and minimal coat grooming needs.

pubmed-hirz-2017-cln8-ncl-alpine-dachsbr.name: Neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis (NCL) is caused by the entire deletion of CLN8 in the Alpenländische Dachsbracke dog
pubmed-hirz-2017-cln8-ncl-alpine-dachsbr.publisher: Molecular Genetics and Metabolism (via PubMed / NCBI)
pubmed-hirz-2017-cln8-ncl-alpine-dachsbr.note: Peer-reviewed study (Hirz et al., Mol Genet Metab. 2017 Mar;120(3):269-277, PMID: 28024876) identifying a homozygous whole-gene deletion of CLN8 as the autosomal recessive cause of neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis (NCL8) in the Alpine Dachsbracke.

pubmed-letko-2019-scn8a-ataxia-alpine-da.name: A Missense Variant in SCN8A in Alpine Dachsbracke Dogs Affected by Spinocerebellar Ataxia
pubmed-letko-2019-scn8a-ataxia-alpine-da.note: Peer-reviewed genetic study (Letko et al., Genes 2019 May 10;10(5):362, PMID: 31083464) identifying a recessive missense mutation (c.4898G>T; p.Gly1633Val) in the SCN8A gene on chromosome 27 causing hereditary spinocerebellar ataxia in Alpine Dachsbracke dogs.

pubmed-karpiuk-2021-boarhound-hunt-trial.name: Hunt Trials as a Measure to Assess Level of Training in Boarhounds
pubmed-karpiuk-2021-boarhound-hunt-trial.note: Peer-reviewed evaluation of 1,867 hunting dogs across 39 breeds in boarhound trials (2005–2015) (PMID: 34199674), finding that the Alpine Dachsbracke achieved the highest overall trial performance.

rkc-parson-russell-terrier-standard.name: The Royal Kennel Club — Parson Russell Terrier Breed Standard
rkc-parson-russell-terrier-standard.note: Official UK breed standard for the Parson Russell Terrier, listing ideal wither heights of 36 cm (14 in) for males and 33 cm (13 in) for females, rough/broken/smooth weather-resistant coat, and white or predominantly white colour with tan, lemon, or black markings.

prtaa-breed-history-standard.name: Parson Russell Terrier Association of America — Breed History and Official Breed Standard
prtaa-breed-history-standard.publisher: Parson Russell Terrier Association of America
prtaa-breed-history-standard.note: Official parent-club historical account (Reverend John Russell in Swimbridge, Devon; Arthur Heinemann's 1904 standard and 1914 club; 1985 JRTAA/PRTAA founding; 1990 UK and 1997/2003 US recognition) and complete text of the AKC/PRTAA Official Breed Standard.

prtaa-health-and-genetics.name: Parson Russell Terrier Association of America — Health and Genetics
prtaa-health-and-genetics.publisher: Parson Russell Terrier Association of America
prtaa-health-and-genetics.note: Official PRTAA Health and Genetics guidance detailing CHIC/OFA clinical evaluations (ACVO ophthalmologist eye exam, patellar luxation evaluation, BAER congenital deafness testing) and pre-breeding DNA tests for primary lens luxation (PLL), late-onset ataxia (LOA), and spinocerebellar ataxia (SCA).

pubmed-forman-2013-capn1-ataxia-parson-r.name: Forman et al. (2013) — Missense Mutation in CAPN1 Associated with Late-Onset Ataxia
pubmed-forman-2013-capn1-ataxia-parson-r.note: Peer-reviewed genetic study identifying a missense mutation (c.344G>A; p.Cys115Tyr) in the CAPN1 gene responsible for late-onset spinocerebellar ataxia in Jack Russell and Parson Russell Terriers.

pubmed-bianchi-2016-gwas-ataxia-parson-r.name: Genome-Wide Association Study for Hereditary Ataxia in the Parson Russell Terrier and Genetic Testing for CAPN1 and KCNJ10 Mutations
pubmed-bianchi-2016-gwas-ataxia-parson-r.note: Peer-reviewed GWAS and genotyping study in Parson Russell Terriers (PMID: 27724896) demonstrating segregation of KCNJ10:c.627C>G and CAPN1:c.344G>A variants in hereditary ataxia.

pubmed-rohdin-2015-kcnj10-ataxia-russell.name: A KCNJ10 Mutation Previously Identified in the Russell Group of Terriers Also Occurs in Smooth-Haired Fox Terriers with Hereditary Ataxia and in Related Breeds
pubmed-rohdin-2015-kcnj10-ataxia-russell.note: Peer-reviewed study (Rohdin et al., Acta Vet Scand 2015 May 23;57(1):26, PMID: 25998802) confirming the autosomal-recessive KCNJ10 mutation associated with spinocerebellar ataxia with myokymia, seizures, or both in Parson Russell Terriers and related Russell-group terriers.

pubmed-gould-2011-adamts17-lens-luxation.name: Gould et al. (2011) — ADAMTS17 Mutation Associated with Primary Lens Luxation
pubmed-gould-2011-adamts17-lens-luxation.note: Peer-reviewed study documenting the c.1473+1G>A splice-site mutation in ADAMTS17 causing autosomal recessive primary lens luxation (PLL) across terrier breeds including the Jack Russell Terrier.

pubmed-hytonen-2019-enam-amelogenesis-im.name: Canine Models of Human Amelogenesis Imperfecta: Identification of Novel Recessive ENAM and ACP4 Variants
pubmed-hytonen-2019-enam-amelogenesis-im.note: Peer-reviewed genetic study (Hytönen et al., Hum Genet 2019 May;138(5):525-533, PMID: 30877375) identifying a breed-specific autosomal-recessive missense variant (c.716C>T; p.Pro239Leu) in exon 8 of ENAM causing clinical dental enamel hypomineralization (amelogenesis imperfecta) in Parson Russell Terriers.

akc-golden-retriever-official-standard.name: Official Standard of the Golden Retriever
akc-golden-retriever-official-standard.note: Official breed standard covering general appearance, head, neck, body, coat, color, size, proportion, and substance (males 23–24 in, 65–75 lb; females 21.5–22.5 in, 55–65 lb).

akc-golden-retriever-profile.name: American Kennel Club — Golden Retriever
akc-golden-retriever-profile.note: Breed profile covering sporting group classification, Scottish origins, trainability, exercise needs, coat colors, shedding, and life expectancy (10–12 years).

grca-golden-retriever-health-screening.name: Golden Retriever Club of America — Health Screenings for the Parents of a Litter
grca-golden-retriever-health-screening.note: Official parent club health screening recommendations for breeding stock, covering hips, elbows, eyes, heart, and genetic testing including NCL5.

wikimedia-golden-retriever-karen-arnold.name: Wikimedia Commons — File:Golden-retriever-dog.jpg
wikimedia-golden-retriever-karen-arnold.publisher: Wikimedia Commons; original photographer Karen Arnold
wikimedia-golden-retriever-karen-arnold.note: Photograph of a Golden Retriever by Karen Arnold, uploaded by Brooks patty, dimensions 1920 × 1440 pixels, dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0.

akc-bull-terrier-profile.name: American Kennel Club — Bull Terrier
akc-bull-terrier-profile.note: Breed profile covering terrier group classification, typical height (21–22 in) and weight (50–70 lb), lifespan (12–13 years), training, and grooming.

akc-bull-terrier-official-standard.name: Official Standard of the Bull Terrier
akc-bull-terrier-official-standard.note: Official breed standard covering general appearance, head, eyes, ears, body, legs, coat, color (white and colored varieties), and movement. Height and weight are not prescribed in the standard.

ukc-bull-terrier-standard.name: United Kennel Club — Bull Terrier Official Breed Standard
ukc-bull-terrier-standard.note: Official breed standard describing conformation, distinctive oval head, temperament, coat, and color varieties.

ckc-bull-terrier-profile.name: Canadian Kennel Club — Bull Terrier
ckc-bull-terrier-profile.note: Breed overview covering historical background as a gentleman's companion, playful clownish personality, and absence of fixed height or weight limits.

bull-terrier-club-america-health-stateme.name: Bull Terrier Club of America — Health Statement
bull-terrier-club-america-health-stateme.note: Official parent club health statement detailing recommended health testing: BAER hearing testing, kidney screening (urine protein-to-creatinine ratio), cardiac evaluation, and patellar assessment.

commons-bullterrier-3453301920.name: Wikimedia Commons — File:Bullterrier-3453301920.jpg
commons-bullterrier-3453301920.publisher: Wikimedia Commons; original photographer TC-TORRES via Pixabay
commons-bullterrier-3453301920.note: Photograph of a female Bull Terrier by TC-TORRES via Pixabay, uploaded by Adventurous36, dimensions 1920 × 1280 pixels, dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0.

continental-kennel-club-bull-terrier.name: Continental Kennel Club — Bull Terrier Breed Profile
continental-kennel-club-bull-terrier.note: Breed reference documentation covering breed history and alternate names including English Bull Terrier.

german-shepherd-dog-club-of-america-bree.name: German Shepherd Dog Club of America - Breed History
german-shepherd-dog-club-of-america-bree.publisher: German Shepherd Dog Club of America
german-shepherd-dog-club-of-america-bree.note: Parent club historical documentation verifying Captain Max von Stephanitz's purchase of Hektor Linksrhein (renamed Horand von Grafrath, SZ 1) at Karlsruhe in April 1899, founding of the Verein für Deutsche Schäferhunde (SV) on 22 April 1899 with Artur Meyer, early Schutzhund trials (1901), 1913 formation of the GSDCA, World War I renaming to Shepherd Dog in the US and Alsatian in Britain, and pioneering Seeing Eye guide dog work.

akc-dna-testing-breed-recommendations.name: American Kennel Club - Breed-Specific DNA Testing Recommendations (German Shepherd Dog)
akc-dna-testing-breed-recommendations.note: AKC DNA Resource Center chart verifying breed-specific genetic tests for the German Shepherd Dog: Canine Scott Syndrome, Chondrodysplasia (CDPA), Cone Degeneration (German Shepherd Dog Type), Degenerative Myelopathy (Common Variant), Ectodermal Dysplasia X-Linked (Shepherd Type), Hemophilia A (German Shepherd Dog Type 1 & Type 2), Hyperuricosuria (HUU), Intervertebral Disc Disease Risk Factor and Chondrodystrophy (CDDY with IVDD), Leukocyte Adhesion Deficiency Type III, Mucopolysaccharidosis VII (Shepherd Type), Multidrug Resistance 1 (MDR1), Pituitary Dwarfism (Shepherd Type), and Renal Cystadenocarcinoma and Nodular Dermatofibrosis (RCND).

pubmed-26401327-gsd-dm-sod1.name: PubMed - Prevalence of the Canine Degenerative Myelopathy Associated SOD1:c.118G>A Mutation in a UK Referral Population of German Shepherd Dogs (PMID 26401327)
pubmed-26401327-gsd-dm-sod1.publisher: National Library of Medicine / Canine Genetics and Epidemiology
pubmed-26401327-gsd-dm-sod1.note: Peer-reviewed study by Holder et al. (2014) demonstrating high prevalence and clinical penetrance of the superoxide dismutase 1 (SOD1:c.118G>A) mutation associated with adult-onset canine degenerative myelopathy in German Shepherd Dogs.

pubmed-22132174-gsd-pituitary-dwarfism-l.name: PubMed - A Contracted DNA Repeat in LHX3 Intron 5 Is Associated with Aberrant Splicing and Pituitary Dwarfism in German Shepherd Dogs (PMID 22132174)
pubmed-22132174-gsd-pituitary-dwarfism-l.publisher: National Library of Medicine / PLoS One
pubmed-22132174-gsd-pituitary-dwarfism-l.note: Peer-reviewed molecular genetics study by Voorbij et al. (2011) identifying a 7-bp repeat deletion in intron 5 of the LHX3 gene on chromosome 9 causing autosomal recessive combined pituitary hormone deficiency (pituitary dwarfism) in German Shepherd Dogs.

drentsche-patrijshond-club-rasstandaard.name: Vereniging 'De Drentsche Patrijshond' — Rasstandaard & Geschiedenis
drentsche-patrijshond-club-rasstandaard.note: Dutch parent breed club publication of the official breed standard and historical background, detailing the Schuiling/Nimrod foundation lines around Eext in Drenthe, recognition on 15 May 1943, club establishment on 5 June 1948, and working traits before and after the shot.

akc-drentsche-patrijshond-breed-info.name: American Kennel Club — Drentsche Patrijshond Dog Breed Information
akc-drentsche-patrijshond-breed-info.note: AKC breed profile documenting Foundation Stock Service / Sporting Group status, 11–14 year life expectancy, imperial height (23–25 in males, 21.5–23.5 in females) and weight (70–73 lb males, 55–60 lb females), low drooling tendency, biannual shedding, ear and coat care, and health notes on epilepsy, von Willebrand disease type 1, eye conditions, hip/elbow dysplasia, hypothyroidism, cryptorchidism, and hyperuricosuria.

akc-dna-testing-recommendations.name: American Kennel Club — Breed Health Testing Requirements & DNA Testing Recommendations
akc-dna-testing-recommendations.note: Lists GM2 Gangliosidosis (Japanese Chin Type) DNA testing as recommended/required for the Japanese Chin.

licg-drentsche-patrijshond.name: LICG — Huisdierenbijsluiter Drentsche Patrijshond
licg-drentsche-patrijshond.note: Dutch national companion-animal veterinary reference guide detailing temperament, socialization, exercise, coat and ear care, ~12-year average lifespan, 58–63 cm / 55–60 cm height, 30–35 kg / 25–30 kg weight, and hereditary conditions (idiopathic epilepsy, von Willebrand disease type 1, hip dysplasia, distichiasis, persistent pupillary membranes, PRA, cataract, and cryptorchidism).

pubmed-drentsche-patrijshond-epilepsy-20.name: Identification of a Novel Idiopathic Epilepsy Risk Locus and a Variant in the CCDC85A Gene in the Dutch Partridge Dog (Animals, 2023, PMID 36899667)
pubmed-drentsche-patrijshond-epilepsy-20.note: Peer-reviewed genome-wide association and whole-exome sequencing study by Ghent University and Utrecht University characterizing idiopathic epilepsy in the Dutch Partridge Dog (most cases showing focal seizures evolving into generalized seizures) and identifying a chromosome 12 risk locus and a chromosome 10 CCDC85A variant.

pubmed-drentsche-patrijshond-fshg-1991.name: Familial stomatocytosis-hypertrophic gastritis (FSHG), a newly recognised disease in the dog (Drentse patrijshond) (Vet Q, 1991, PMID 2021052)
pubmed-drentsche-patrijshond-fshg-1991.note: Peer-reviewed clinical and pathological study from Utrecht University describing autosomal-recessive familial stomatocytosis-hypertrophic gastritis (FSHG) in Drentsche Patrijshond families.

fci-austrian-pinscher-standard.name: FCI Standard No. 64 — Österreichischer Pinscher (Austrian Pinscher)
fci-austrian-pinscher-standard.note: Official breed standard covering origin in Austria, Group 2 Section 1.1 classification, pear-shaped head, double coat, colors, and withers height (males 44–50 cm, females 42–48 cm). Weight is not specified.

ukc-austrian-pinscher-standard.name: United Kennel Club — Austrian Pinscher Official Breed Standard
ukc-austrian-pinscher-standard.note: Official breed standard covering breed history, characteristics, general appearance, coat, and color varieties.

royal-canin-austrian-pinscher.name: Royal Canin — Austrian Pinscher
royal-canin-austrian-pinscher.note: Breed library profile detailing temperament, working background, life expectancy (12–14 years), and grooming.

commons-austrian-pinscher-canarian-2023.name: Wikimedia Commons — File:Austrianpinscherosterreich1.jpg
commons-austrian-pinscher-canarian-2023.note: Photograph of an Austrian Pinscher by Canarian, captured 2023-08-26, uploaded 2023-08-27, dimensions 2493 × 1950 pixels, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0.

fci-swedish-lapphund-standard.name: FCI Standard No. 135 — Svensk Lapphund (Swedish Lapphund)
fci-swedish-lapphund-standard.note: Official breed standard covering origin in Sweden, Group 5 Section 3 classification, spitz conformation, stand-off double coat, black coloration with bronzing, and withers height (males 45–51 cm, females 40–46 cm).

swedish-kennel-club-swedish-lapphund-en.name: Svenska Kennelklubben — Swedish Lapphund (English)
swedish-kennel-club-swedish-lapphund-en.note: Official national kennel club breed overview in English detailing Sami reindeer-herding history, working character, coat care, and versatility in canine activities.

swedish-kennel-club-swedish-lapphund.name: Svenska Kennelklubben — Svensk Lapphund
swedish-kennel-club-swedish-lapphund.note: Primary Swedish kennel club breed dossier documenting typical weight (males 16–20 kg, females 14–16 kg), longevity (12–14 years), and health monitoring (hip dysplasia and prcd-PRA DNA screening).

ukc-swedish-lapphund-standard.name: United Kennel Club — Swedish Lapphund Official Breed Standard
ukc-swedish-lapphund-standard.note: Official breed standard covering Northern breed characteristics, rectangular proportions, dense double coat, and temperament.

commons-swedish-lapphund-canarian-2017.name: Wikimedia Commons — File:Swedish Lapphund.jpg
commons-swedish-lapphund-canarian-2017.note: Photograph of a male Swedish Lapphund by Canarian, captured 2017-12-08, uploaded 2017-12-08, dimensions 2115 × 1769 pixels, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0.

fci-lhasa-apso-standard.name: FCI Standard No. 227 — Lhasa Apso
fci-lhasa-apso-standard.note: Official breed standard covering origin in Tibet (China), Group 9 Section 5 classification, long hard-textured double coat, permissible colors (excluding merle), and ideal withers height (males 25 cm, females slightly smaller).

american-kennel-club-lhasa-apso.name: American Kennel Club — Lhasa Apso
american-kennel-club-lhasa-apso.note: Breed profile covering Non-Sporting classification, height (10–11 in for males, slightly smaller for females), weight (12–18 lb), life expectancy (12–15 years), grooming, and health concerns.

american-lhasa-apso-club-faqs.name: American Lhasa Apso Club — Frequently Asked Questions
american-lhasa-apso-club-faqs.note: Parent club FAQ addressing watchdog barking, independent temperament, coat maintenance schedules, and hereditary renal dysplasia.

american-lhasa-apso-club-health-statemen.name: American Lhasa Apso Club — Lhasa Apso Health
american-lhasa-apso-club-health-statemen.note: Parent club health statement detailing commonly observed conditions including patellar luxation, umbilical/inguinal hernias, corneal ulcers, and bladder calculi, while noting no mandatory breeder testing requirements.

commons-lhasaapso-photo-2011.name: Wikimedia Commons — File:Lhasaapso.jpg
commons-lhasaapso-photo-2011.note: Photograph of an adult Lhasa Apso by Lhasaapso, captured 2011-12-26, uploaded 2011-12-26, dimensions 1200 × 800 pixels, licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0.

fci-continental-toy-spaniel-standard.name: FCI Standard No. 77 — Épagneul Nain Continental (Continental Toy Spaniel)
fci-continental-toy-spaniel-standard.note: Official breed standard covering Belgium and France origin, Group 9 Section 9 classification, Papillon and Phalène ear varieties, white-dominant parti-color coat, and weight categories (1.5 kg minimum; <2.5 kg and 2.5–4.5 kg males / 2.5–5 kg females).

american-kennel-club-papillon-standard.name: Official Standard of the Papillon
american-kennel-club-papillon-standard.note: Official breed standard detailing fine-boned toy conformation, height (8–11 inches, disqualifying over 12 inches), single silky coat, color symmetry, and happy, alert temperament.

american-kennel-club-papillon.name: American Kennel Club — Papillon
american-kennel-club-papillon.note: Breed profile covering Toy group classification, life expectancy (14–16 years), weight (5–10 lb), grooming, and agility/obedience aptitude.

papillon-club-of-america-health-statemen.name: Papillon Club of America — Health Statement
papillon-club-of-america-health-statemen.note: Official parent club health statement detailing recommended evaluations for eyes, patellas, and heart, alongside DNA testing for PRA-1 and neuroaxonal dystrophy (NAD).

vca-papillon-breed-profile.name: VCA Animal Hospitals — Papillon
vca-papillon-breed-profile.note: Veterinary breed guide covering lifespan estimate (12–15 years), nutrition, puppy hypoglycemia precautions, grooming, and exercise needs.

commons-phalen-papillon-with-drop-ears.name: Wikimedia Commons — File:Papillon with drop ears.jpg
commons-phalen-papillon-with-drop-ears.note: Photograph of a Phalène (drop-eared Continental Toy Spaniel) by Dzhermanotta-royals, captured 2015-08-01, uploaded 2015-09-01, dimensions 960 × 639 pixels, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0.

fci-francais-tricolore-standard-2023.name: FCI Standard No. 219 — Français Tricolore (French Tricolour Hound)
fci-francais-tricolore-standard-2023.note: Official breed standard covering origin in France, Group 6 Section 1.1 classification with working trial, pack-hound conformation, short fine hair, tricolour/grizzled coat, and withers height (males 62–72 cm, females 60–68 cm). Weight is not specified.

fci-francais-tricolore-nomenclature.name: FCI Breed Nomenclature — Français Tricolore (219)
fci-francais-tricolore-nomenclature.note: Official breed nomenclature listing Group 6 classification, working trial status, and definitive recognition date (15 December 1959).

akc-finnish-spitz-breed-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile covering ancient Suomenpystykorva history, national dog of Finland designation in 1979, barking bird dog traits, published weight (25-33 lbs males, 20-28 lbs females), lifespan (13-15 years), and exercise needs.

the-kennel-club-finnish-spitz-breed-stan.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Finnish Spitz Breed Standard
the-kennel-club-finnish-spitz-breed-stan.note: Official Royal Kennel Club breed standard (Hound Group, updated April 2025) confirming height (dogs 43-50 cm / 17-20 in; bitches 39-45 cm / 15.5-18 in), weight (14-16 kg / 31-35 lbs), coat characteristics, and hunting temperament.

finnish-spitz-epilepsy-adam23-study-2015.name: Identification of a Common Risk Haplotype for Canine Idiopathic Epilepsy in the ADAM23 Gene (BMC Genomics 2015)
finnish-spitz-epilepsy-adam23-study-2015.note: Peer-reviewed scientific study (Koskinen et al., BMC Genomics 2015;16:465, PMID 26084559) identifying a shared risk haplotype on chromosome 37 in the ADAM23 gene associated with idiopathic epilepsy across four breeds including the Finnish Spitz.

finnish-spitz-epilepsy-phenotype-study-2.name: Phenotype, Inheritance Characteristics, and Risk Factors for Idiopathic Epilepsy in Finnish Spitz Dogs (JVIM 2006)
finnish-spitz-epilepsy-phenotype-study-2.note: Peer-reviewed study (Viitmaa et al., J Vet Intern Med 2006;20(2):305-310, PMID 16538965) analyzing idiopathic epilepsy in Finnish Spitz dogs, demonstrating a high proportion of focal-onset seizures and estimated heritability.
finnish-spitz-epilepsy-phenotype-study-2.publisher: Journal of Veterinary Internal Medicine / PubMed

fci-transylvanian-hound-official-standar.name: FCI - Transylvanian Hound Official Breed Standard No. 241
fci-transylvanian-hound-official-standar.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 241 (valid standard dated 2000-04-06, published 2000-09-13). Covers Hungarian origin, Group 6 Section 1.2 Medium-sized Hounds classification with working trial, historical big game and small game hunting roles, rectangular build, black and tan coloration with eyebrow spots, withers height (55 to 65 cm, ideal 58 to 62 cm), and minimum weight (25 kg).

fci-transylvanian-hound-nomenclature.name: FCI - Transylvanian Hound Breed Nomenclature (No. 241)
fci-transylvanian-hound-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming Hungary as country of origin, Group 6 Section 1.2 classification with working trial, official multilingual names (Erdélyi Kopó, Chien Courant Transylvanien, Transylvanischer Laufhund, Sabueso de Transilvania), and definitive recognition date (1963-03-30).

meoesz-erdelyi-kopo-breed-profile.name: Magyar Ebtenyésztők Országos Egyesülete - Erdélyi Kopó Fajtaleírás
meoesz-erdelyi-kopo-breed-profile.note: Official Hungarian Kennel Club (MEOESZ) breed profile and history for the Erdélyi Kopó, detailing its historical role under the Hungarian royalty, 1968 rescue in Transylvania, working trial standards, height (55-65 cm), weight (25-35 kg), and health screening requirements.

ukc-transylvanian-hound-breed-standard.name: United Kennel Club - Transylvanian Hound Breed Standard
ukc-transylvanian-hound-breed-standard.note: Official UKC breed standard (Scenthound Group, recognized 2006) covering conformation, rectangular proportions, black and tan coloration, height (21.5 to 25.5 inches / 55 to 65 cm), minimum weight (55 lbs / 25 kg, typically 25 to 35 kg), and hunting behavior.

akc-transylvanian-hound-breed-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Transylvanian Hound Breed Information
akc-transylvanian-hound-breed-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile (Foundation Stock Service, Hound Group) covering historical background, height (21.5 to 25.5 inches), weight (55 to 77 pounds), lifespan (10 to 12 years), temperament, grooming, and exercise needs.

fci-hamiltonstovare-official-standard.name: FCI - Hamiltonstövare Official Breed Standard No. 132
fci-hamiltonstovare-official-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 132 (valid standard dated 2017-09-25, publication date 2017-10-30). Covers Swedish origin, Group 6 Section 1.2 Medium-sized Hounds classification with working trial, rectangular proportions, tricolour coat pattern (black mantle, golden-tan ground, white markings), withers height (males 53-61 cm, ideal 57 cm; females 49-57 cm, ideal 53 cm), and hunting utility on hare and fox.

fci-hamiltonstovare-nomenclature.name: FCI - Hamiltonstövare Breed Nomenclature (No. 132)
fci-hamiltonstovare-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming Sweden as country of origin, Group 6 Section 1.2 classification with working trial, official multilingual names (Chien Courant Hamilton, Hamilton-Bracke, Sabueso de Hamilton), and definitive recognition date (1954-11-25).

skk-hamiltonstovare-breed-standard.name: Svenska Kennelklubben - Rasstandard för Hamiltonstövare (FCI 132)
skk-hamiltonstovare-breed-standard.note: Official Swedish Kennel Club (SKK) breed standard and profile for Hamiltonstövare, confirming Swedish origin, Count Adolf Patrik Hamilton heritage, hunting traits on hare and fox, height limits, weight range (approx. 23-27 kg), and health screening.

svenska-hamiltonstovareklubben-breed-pro.name: Svenska Hamiltonstövareklubben - Om Hamiltonstövaren
svenska-hamiltonstovareklubben-breed-pro.note: Official Swedish Hamiltonstövare breed club portal documenting the 1886 Stockholm show foundation (Pang and Stella), 1889 SKK founding by Count A.P. Hamilton, weight ranges (25-27 kg males, 23-25 kg females), lifespan (12-14 years), hunting traits, and hip dysplasia health screening.

the-kennel-club-hamiltonstovare-breed-st.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Hamiltonstovare Breed Standard
the-kennel-club-hamiltonstovare-breed-st.note: Official Royal Kennel Club breed standard (Hound Group, updated April 2025) confirming height (dogs 53-61 cm / 21-24 in; bitches 49-57 cm / 19.5-22.5 in), rectangular proportions, tricolour coat, and hunting temperament.

ukc-hamiltonstovare-breed-standard.name: United Kennel Club - Hamiltonstovare Breed Standard
ukc-hamiltonstovare-breed-standard.note: Official UKC breed standard (Scenthound Group, recognized 2006) covering conformation, rectangular proportions, tricolour markings, height (males 21-24 in / 53-61 cm; females 19.5-22.5 in / 49-57 cm), weight (males 55-60 lbs / approx. 25-27 kg; females 50-55 lbs / approx. 23-25 kg), and hunting behavior.

wikimedia-hamiltonstovare-lilly-m.note: Photograph of an adult Hamiltonstövare standing in profile outdoors by Lilly M (captured 2007-06-16, uploaded 2007-06-25, 2604 x 1952 px). Licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0.

fci-basset-hound-official-standard.name: FCI - Basset Hound Official Breed Standard No. 163
fci-basset-hound-official-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 163 (valid standard dated 2010-10-13, publication date 2011-01-24). Covers Great Britain origin, Group 6 Section 1.3 Small-sized Hounds classification with working trial, general appearance, low-slung achondroplastic build, loose skin, coat, colours (tricolour, lemon and white), and withers height (33-38 cm).

fci-basset-hound-nomenclature.name: FCI - Basset Hound Breed Nomenclature (No. 163)
fci-basset-hound-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming Great Britain as country of origin, Group 6 Section 1.3 classification with working trial, and definitive recognition date (1955-01-18).

the-kennel-club-basset-hound-breed-stand.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Basset Hound Breed Standard
the-kennel-club-basset-hound-breed-stand.note: Official Royal Kennel Club breed standard (Hound Group) confirming withers height (33-38 cm / 13-15 in), weight guide (dogs 25-30 kg / 55-66 lbs, bitches 20-25 kg / 44-55 lbs), head structure, and hunting characteristics.

akc-basset-hound-breed-standard.name: American Kennel Club - Official Standard of the Basset Hound
akc-basset-hound-breed-standard.note: Official AKC breed standard establishing height not to exceed 14 inches at withers (over 15 inches disqualified), heavy bone, chest, ears, loose skin, and tricolor/bicolor coat patterns.

akc-basset-hound-breed-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Basset Hound Dog Breed Information
akc-basset-hound-breed-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile covering French St. Hubert ancestry, Lord Galway and Everett Millais development in Britain, weight (40-65 lbs), lifespan (12-13 years), drooling, shedding, and health.

basset-hound-club-of-america-health.name: Basset Hound Club of America - Health & Research
basset-hound-club-of-america-health.note: Official national parent club health portal covering thrombopathia (CTP), primary glaucoma, intervertebral disc disease (IVDD), bloat, elbow dysplasia, and CHIC screening protocols.

ofa-basset-hound-chic-requirements.name: Orthopedic Foundation for Animals - Basset Hound CHIC Requirements
ofa-basset-hound-chic-requirements.note: Official OFA Canine Health Information Center (CHIC) testing requirements for the Basset Hound, mandating thrombopathia DNA test, primary glaucoma DNA test or gonioscopy eye exam, and optional hip, elbow, and cardiac evaluations.

basset-hound-thrombopathia-rasgrp1-study.name: A Mutation in the RASGRP1 Gene Causes Thrombopathia in Basset Hounds (AJVR / Blood 2006)
basset-hound-thrombopathia-rasgrp1-study.note: Peer-reviewed scientific study (Boudreaux et al., 2006) identifying the causal RASGRP1 gene mutation responsible for inherited canine thrombopathia, a severe platelet aggregation defect in Basset Hounds.
basset-hound-thrombopathia-rasgrp1-study.publisher: American Journal of Veterinary Research / PubMed

basset-hound-glaucoma-adamts17-study-201.name: An ADAMTS17 Mutation Is Associated with Primary Glaucoma in the Basset Hound (PLoS ONE 2015)
basset-hound-glaucoma-adamts17-study-201.note: Peer-reviewed study (Oliver et al., PLoS ONE 2015;10(8):e0133939, PMID 26262981) identifying a 19-bp deletion in the ADAMTS17 gene associated with primary closed-angle glaucoma in Basset Hounds.

fci-greenland-dog-official-standard.name: FCI - Greenland Dog (Grønlandshund) Official Breed Standard No. 274
fci-greenland-dog-official-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 274 (valid standard dated 2003-03-25, publication date 2015-05-05). Covers Greenland origin, Denmark patronage, Group 5 Spitz and primitive types, Section 1 Nordic Sledge Dogs classification without working trial, wedge-shaped head, dense double coat, all colors except albinos, and withers height (males 60 cm and upwards, females 55 cm and upwards).

fci-greenland-dog-nomenclature.name: FCI - Greenland Dog Breed Nomenclature (No. 274)
fci-greenland-dog-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming Greenland as country of origin, Denmark as country of patronage, Group 5 Section 1 classification without working trial, official multilingual names (Grønlandshund, Chien du Groenland, Grönlandhund, Perro de Groenlandia), and definitive recognition date (1967-08-01).

dansk-kennel-klub-groenlandshund-breed-s.name: Dansk Kennel Klub - Racebeskrivelse for Grønlandshund
dansk-kennel-klub-groenlandshund-breed-s.note: Official Danish Kennel Club (Dansk Kennel Klub / DKK) breed profile and standard for Grønlandshund, detailing Greenland heritage, legal protection north of the Arctic circle, sledge dog function, height (males 60+ cm, females 55+ cm), weight ranges (approx. 30-40 kg for males, 25-35 kg for females), and pack behavior.

the-kennel-club-greenland-dog-breed-stan.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Greenland Dog Breed Standard
the-kennel-club-greenland-dog-breed-stan.note: Official Royal Kennel Club breed standard (Working Group) confirming height (dogs 60 cm / 23.5 in minimum; bitches 55 cm / 21.5 in minimum), weight guide (approx. 34-47.5 kg / 75-105 lbs for dogs; 27-41 kg / 60-90 lbs for bitches), coat characteristics, and working sledge temperament.

ukc-greenland-dog-breed-standard.name: United Kennel Club - Greenland Dog Breed Standard
ukc-greenland-dog-breed-standard.note: Official UKC breed standard (Northern Breed Group, recognized 1996) covering Arctic conformation, height (males 23.5 in / 60 cm and up; females 21.5 in / 55 cm and up), sledging endurance, and pack behavior.

greenland-dog-holocene-origins-study-202.name: Arctic-Adapted Dogs Emerged at the Beginning of the Holocene (Science 2020)
greenland-dog-holocene-origins-study-202.note: Peer-reviewed landmark scientific study (Sinding et al., Science 2020;368(6498):1495-1499, PMID 32587019) demonstrating genetic continuity between 9,500-year-old Siberian sled dogs from Zhokhov Island and modern Greenland Dogs, identifying specific adaptations to a high-fat diet, oxygen uptake, and cold-climate endurance.
greenland-dog-holocene-origins-study-202.publisher: Science / American Association for the Advancement of Science

fci-estrela-mountain-dog-official-standa.name: FCI - Cão da Serra da Estrela Official Breed Standard No. 173
fci-estrela-mountain-dog-official-standa.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 173 (valid standard dated 2008-11-04, publication date 2009-03-30). Covers Portuguese origin in Serra da Estrela, Group 2 Section 2.2 Mountain type Molossoids classification without working trial, historical background, both long and short coat varieties, black mask, hooked tail tip, withers height (males 65-73 cm, females 62-69 cm, +2 cm tolerance), and weight (males 45-60 kg, females 35-45 kg).

fci-estrela-mountain-dog-nomenclature.name: FCI - Cão da Serra da Estrela Breed Nomenclature (No. 173)
fci-estrela-mountain-dog-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming Portugal as country of origin, Group 2 Section 2.2 classification without working trial, definitive recognition date (1955-01-18), and official multilingual names (Chien de la Serra da Estrela, Estrela-Berghund, Perro de la Sierra de la Estrela).

cpc-cao-da-serra-da-estrela-standard.name: Clube Português de Canicultura - Estalão do Cão da Serra da Estrela
cpc-cao-da-serra-da-estrela-standard.note: Official Portuguese Kennel Club (CPC) breed standard and profile for Cão da Serra da Estrela, detailing historical origin in the Serra da Estrela, 1922 and 1934 historical standards, morphological proportions, height, weight, long and short coat varieties, and health screening.

apcse-cao-da-serra-da-estrela-profile.name: Associação Portuguesa do Cão da Serra da Estrela - A Raça e História
apcse-cao-da-serra-da-estrela-profile.note: Official Portuguese parent breed club portal documenting the 1983 club founding, pastoral transhumance history, spiked collar protection against wolves, long and short hair varieties, and pre-breeding health testing.
apcse-cao-da-serra-da-estrela-profile.publisher: Associação Portuguesa do Cão da Serra da Estrela

ukc-estrela-mountain-dog-standard.name: United Kennel Club - Estrela Mountain Dog Breed Standard
ukc-estrela-mountain-dog-standard.note: Official UKC breed standard (Guardian Dog Group, recognized 1996, revised 2006) covering conformation, height (males 25.5-29 inches / 65-73 cm; females 24.5-27 inches / 62-69 cm), weight (males 99-132 lbs / 45-60 kg; females 77-99 lbs / 35-45 kg), long and short coats, and guardian behavior.

akc-estrela-mountain-dog-breed-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Estrela Mountain Dog Breed Information
akc-estrela-mountain-dog-breed-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile (Foundation Stock Service, Working Group) covering Portuguese mountain origin, height, weight, lifespan (10-14 years), temperament, and care.

estrela-mountain-dog-cardiac-health-stud.name: Echocardiographic Reference Values and Screening in Portuguese Mountain Breeds (Veterinary Cardiology)
estrela-mountain-dog-cardiac-health-stud.note: Peer-reviewed veterinary cardiology study evaluating echocardiographic parameters and screening for dilated cardiomyopathy in Portuguese mountain guardian dogs including the Cão da Serra da Estrela.

wikimedia-cao-da-serra-da-estrela-600-to.note: Photograph of an adult long-haired Estrela Mountain Dog by Tomasz Sienicki (captured 2006-05-20, uploaded 2006-05-21, 600 x 489 px). Licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0 on Wikimedia Commons.

fci-west-highland-white-terrier-official.name: FCI - West Highland White Terrier Official Breed Standard No. 85
fci-west-highland-white-terrier-official.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 85 (valid standard dated 2010-10-13, publication date 2011-01-24). Covers Great Britain origin, Group 3 Terriers, Section 2 Small-sized Terriers classification without working trial, general appearance, pure white double coat, carrot tail, black pigment, and withers height (approximately 28 cm / 11 ins).

fci-west-highland-white-terrier-nomencla.name: FCI - West Highland White Terrier Breed Nomenclature (No. 85)
fci-west-highland-white-terrier-nomencla.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming Great Britain as country of origin, Group 3 Section 2 classification without working trial, official multilingual names (Chien Terrier Blanc des Highlands de l'Ouest, Weißer Hochland-Terrier), and definitive recognition date (1954-10-29).

the-kennel-club-west-highland-white-terr.name: The Royal Kennel Club - West Highland White Terrier Breed Standard
the-kennel-club-west-highland-white-terr.note: Official Royal Kennel Club breed standard (Terrier Group, country of origin standard) establishing withers height (approximately 28 cm / 11 ins), weight (7-10 kg / 15-22 lbs), harsh straight white double coat, carrot-shaped tail, and game working temperament.

akc-west-highland-white-terrier-breed-st.name: American Kennel Club - Official Standard of the West Highland White Terrier
akc-west-highland-white-terrier-breed-st.note: Official AKC breed standard establishing ideal height of 11 inches for dogs and 10 inches for bitches, hard white coat, dark almond eyes, black pigmentation, and alert terrier carriage.

akc-west-highland-white-terrier-breed-pr.name: American Kennel Club - West Highland White Terrier Dog Breed Information
akc-west-highland-white-terrier-breed-pr.note: Official AKC breed profile covering Scottish history (Clan Malcolm of Poltalloch, Colonel Edward Donald Malcolm, Roseneath Terrier), height, weight (15-20 lbs), lifespan (13-15 years), temperament, and grooming.

west-highland-white-terrier-club-of-amer.name: West Highland White Terrier Club of America - Health and Research
west-highland-white-terrier-club-of-amer.note: National parent breed club health resource detailing craniomandibular osteopathy (CMO / Westie Jaw), atopic dermatitis, globoid cell leukodystrophy (GCL), idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (Westie Lung), and CHIC health screening recommendations.
west-highland-white-terrier-club-of-amer.publisher: West Highland White Terrier Club of America

ofa-west-highland-white-terrier-chic-req.name: Orthopedic Foundation for Animals - West Highland White Terrier CHIC Requirements
ofa-west-highland-white-terrier-chic-req.note: Official OFA Canine Health Information Center (CHIC) testing requirements for the West Highland White Terrier, mandating DNA testing for Craniomandibular Osteopathy (CMO), patellar luxation evaluation, and CAER eye examination, alongside optional hip and GCL evaluations.

west-highland-white-terrier-cmo-slc37a2-.name: Novel Carboxylesterase 1 (CES1) and Solute Carrier Family 37 Member 2 (SLC37A2) Mutations Associated with Craniomandibular Osteopathy in Terriers (PLoS ONE 2014)
west-highland-white-terrier-cmo-slc37a2-.note: Peer-reviewed scientific study (Hytönen et al., PLoS ONE 2014;9(11):e112468, PMID 25402008) identifying a missense mutation in the SLC37A2 gene on chromosome 5 causing craniomandibular osteopathy in West Highland White Terriers, Cairn Terriers, and Scottish Terriers.

wikimedia-west-highland-white-terrier-pl.note: Photograph (2400 x 1800 px) of a West Highland White Terrier at a dog show by Pleple2000 (captured 2008-10-05, uploaded 2008-10-18). Licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0.

ukc-patterdale-terrier-official-standard.name: United Kennel Club - Patterdale Terrier Breed Standard
ukc-patterdale-terrier-official-standard.note: Official UKC breed standard (Terrier Group, recognized January 1, 1995) covering conformation, spannable chest, smooth/broken/rough coat varieties, height (10 to 15 inches), weight (11 to 13 pounds for a 12-inch dog; in proportion), and working earthdog temperament.

patterdale-terrier-club-of-america-breed.name: Patterdale Terrier Club of America - Breed Standard and Information
patterdale-terrier-club-of-america-breed.note: Official parent breed club standard detailing Lake District history, working earthdog traits, height (10-15 inches), working weight (11-15 lbs), coat varieties, and health management.

patterdale-terrier-pll-adamts17-study-20.name: Mutations in ADAMTS17 Associated with Primary Lens Luxation in Terriers (Genetics 2011)

fci-whippet-official-standard.name: FCI - Whippet Official Breed Standard No. 162
fci-whippet-official-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 162 (valid standard dated 2019-09-04). Covers Great Britain origin, Group 10 Sighthounds, Section 3 Short-haired Sighthounds classification without working trial, aerodynamic symmetry, arch over loin, rose ears, and withers height (males 47-51 cm, females 44-47 cm).

fci-whippet-nomenclature.name: FCI - Whippet Breed Nomenclature (No. 162)
fci-whippet-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming Great Britain as country of origin, Group 10 Section 3 classification without working trial, definitive recognition date (1955-04-27), and multilingual names (Lévrier Whippet).

the-kennel-club-whippet-breed-standard.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Whippet Breed Standard
the-kennel-club-whippet-breed-standard.note: Official Royal Kennel Club breed standard (Hound Group, country of origin standard) establishing withers height (dogs 47-51 cm / 18.5-20 in; bitches 44-47 cm / 17.5-18.5 in), typical weight (approx. 12.5-13.5 kg / 11-18 kg), fine close coat, and sighthound temperament.

akc-whippet-breed-standard.name: American Kennel Club - Official Standard of the Whippet
akc-whippet-breed-standard.note: Official AKC breed standard (Hound Group) establishing height (dogs 19 to 22 inches, bitches 18 to 21 inches), proportions, rose ears, scissor bite, and color specifications.

akc-whippet-breed-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Whippet Dog Breed Information
akc-whippet-breed-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile covering English mining history, snap dog and rag racing roots, speed (up to 35 mph), published weight (25-40 lbs), lifespan (12-15 years), temperament, and grooming.

american-whippet-club-health.name: American Whippet Club - Health and Genetics
american-whippet-club-health.note: Official national parent club health portal covering sighthound anesthesia sensitivity, cardiac health (mitral valve disease, athletic heart), myostatin mutation testing, and pre-breeding health screening guidelines.

ofa-whippet-chic-requirements.name: Orthopedic Foundation for Animals - Whippet CHIC Requirements
ofa-whippet-chic-requirements.note: Official OFA Canine Health Information Center (CHIC) testing requirements for the Whippet, mandating CAER eye examination, congenital cardiac evaluation by a specialist, and autoimmune thyroiditis blood panel.

whippet-myostatin-mutation-study-2007.name: A Mutation in the Myostatin Gene Increases Muscle Mass and Enhances Racing Performance in Heterozygote Dogs (PLoS Genetics 2007)
whippet-myostatin-mutation-study-2007.note: Peer-reviewed scientific study (Mosher et al., PLoS Genet 2007;3(5):e79, PMID 17530926) identifying a 2-bp deletion in the myostatin (MSTN) gene that enhances racing performance in heterozygous Whippets and causes severe muscular hypertrophy ('bully whippets') in homozygotes.

societe-centrale-canine-ariegeois.name: Société Centrale Canine — Ariegeois Breed Profile
societe-centrale-canine-ariegeois.note: National French kennel club breed profile covering history, Pyrenean origin, hunting application, calm temperament, care, height (50–58 cm), and unrecorded formal weight ('Poids: NP').

fci-fox-terrier-smooth-official-standard.name: FCI - Fox Terrier (Smooth) Official Breed Standard No. 12
fci-fox-terrier-smooth-official-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 12 (valid standard dated 2026-09-08, published 2026-10-06). Covers Great Britain origin, Group 3 Terriers, Section 1 Large and medium-sized Terriers classification without working trial, general appearance, flat hard smooth coat, white-predominated coloration, withers height not exceeding 39 cm in males, and weight (dogs 7.5-8 kg, bitches 7-7.5 kg).

fci-fox-terrier-smooth-nomenclature.name: FCI - Fox Terrier (Smooth) Breed Nomenclature (No. 12)
fci-fox-terrier-smooth-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming Great Britain as country of origin, Group 3 Section 1 classification without working trial, definitive recognition date (1955-05-26), and multilingual names (Fox-Terrier à poil lisse, Glatthaar-Foxterrier, Fox Terrier de pelo liso).

the-kennel-club-fox-terrier-smooth-breed.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Fox Terrier (Smooth) Breed Standard
the-kennel-club-fox-terrier-smooth-breed.note: Official Royal Kennel Club breed standard (Terrier Group, country of origin standard) establishing withers height not exceeding 39 cm (15.5 in) in dogs, bitches slightly less, weight (dogs 7.5-8 kg / 16-18 lbs, bitches 7-7.5 kg / 15-17 lbs), straight flat smooth coat, V-shaped drop ears, and fearless sporting temperament.

akc-smooth-fox-terrier-breed-standard.name: American Kennel Club - Official Standard of the Smooth Fox Terrier
akc-smooth-fox-terrier-breed-standard.note: Official AKC breed standard (Terrier Group) establishing height not to exceed 15.5 inches for males, proportions, smooth flat coat, V-shaped drop ears, scissor bite, and alert terrier carriage.

akc-smooth-fox-terrier-breed-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Smooth Fox Terrier Dog Breed Information
akc-smooth-fox-terrier-breed-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile covering English fox-hunting history, three-time Westminster winner Ch. Warren Remedy, Herbert Hoover dogs, weight (15-18 lbs), lifespan (12-15 years), temperament, and care.

ukc-smooth-fox-terrier-breed-standard.name: United Kennel Club - Smooth Fox Terrier Breed Standard
ukc-smooth-fox-terrier-breed-standard.note: Official UKC breed standard (Terrier Group, recognized 1912) covering conformation, rectangular proportions, smooth coat, height, weight, and working earthdog behavior.

ofa-smooth-fox-terrier-chic-requirements.name: Orthopedic Foundation for Animals - Smooth Fox Terrier CHIC Requirements
ofa-smooth-fox-terrier-chic-requirements.note: Official OFA Canine Health Information Center (CHIC) testing requirements for the Smooth Fox Terrier, mandating clinical patellar luxation evaluation, CAER eye examination, congenital cardiac evaluation, and DNA testing for Primary Lens Luxation (PLL) and Spinocerebellar Ataxia (SCA).

smooth-fox-terrier-sca-kcnj10-study-2014.name: A KCNJ10 Mutation Causes Spinocerebellar Ataxia with Myokymia and Seizures (SAMS) in Terriers (PLoS ONE 2014)
smooth-fox-terrier-sca-kcnj10-study-2014.note: Peer-reviewed scientific study (Rohdin et al., PLoS ONE 2014;9(6):e98968, PMID 24911478) establishing that a missense mutation in the KCNJ10 gene causes hereditary spinocerebellar ataxia with myokymia and seizures in Fox Terriers and Russell Terriers.

fci-bolognese-official-standard.name: FCI - Bolognese Official Breed Standard No. 196
fci-bolognese-official-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 196 (valid standard dated 2015-11-13, published 2015-12-17). Covers Italian origin in Bologna, Group 9 Companion and Toy Dogs, Section 1 Bichons and related breeds classification without working trial, square proportions (height equals length), pure white flocky coat in tufts without fringes, withers height (males 27-30 cm, females 25-28 cm), and weight (2.5 to 4 kg).

fci-bolognese-nomenclature.name: FCI - Bolognese Breed Nomenclature (No. 196)
fci-bolognese-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature record confirming Italy as country of origin, Group 9 Section 1 classification without working trial, definitive recognition date (1956-03-05), and multilingual names (Bolognese, Bologneser).

enci-bolognese-breed-standard.name: Ente Nazionale della Cinofilia Italiana - Standard del Bolognese
enci-bolognese-breed-standard.note: Official Italian kennel club (ENCI / Ente Nazionale della Cinofilia Italiana) standard and breed profile for the Bolognese, detailing historical Italian origins, Renaissance nobility, square build, flocky coat, height, weight (2.5-4 kg), and health.

akc-bolognese-breed-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Bolognese Dog Breed Information
akc-bolognese-breed-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile (Foundation Stock Service, Toy Group) covering Italian Renaissance history, Medici court gifts, Catherine the Great, weight (5.5-9 lbs / 2.5-4 kg), lifespan (12-14 years), temperament, and grooming.

the-kennel-club-bolognese-breed-standard.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Bolognese Breed Standard
the-kennel-club-bolognese-breed-standard.note: Official Royal Kennel Club breed standard (Toy Group) confirming height (dogs 27-30 cm / 10.5-12 in; bitches 25-28 cm / 10-11 in), weight (2.5-4 kg / 5.5-9 lbs), square build, pure white flocky coat, and serene companion temperament.

ukc-bolognese-breed-standard.name: United Kennel Club - Bolognese Breed Standard
ukc-bolognese-breed-standard.note: Official UKC breed standard (Companion Dog Group, recognized 1995, revised 2012) covering conformation, square proportions, flocky white coat, height, weight, and companion behavior.

ofa-bolognese-health-screenings.name: Orthopedic Foundation for Animals - Bolognese Health Screening Guidelines
ofa-bolognese-health-screenings.note: Orthopedic Foundation for Animals health database and veterinary screening guidelines for the Bolognese, documenting evaluations for patellar luxation, eye examinations (CAER), cardiac health, and Legg-Calve-Perthes disease.

srhk-belgian-shepherd-breed-standard.name: Société Royale Saint-Hubert - Standard du Chien de Berger Belge
srhk-belgian-shepherd-breed-standard.note: Official Belgian kennel club (SRSH / Société Royale Saint-Hubert) standard and breed profile for the Belgian Shepherd, detailing Château de Groenendael foundation history, Professor Reul 1891 breed separation, height limits, weight parameters, and working sheepdog trials.

akc-belgian-sheepdog-breed-standard.name: American Kennel Club - Official Standard of the Belgian Sheepdog
akc-belgian-sheepdog-breed-standard.note: Official AKC breed standard (effective June 11, 1990, Herding Group) establishing height (males 24 to 26 inches / 61-66 cm, females 22 to 24 inches / 56-61 cm), square proportions, solid black long double coat, scissor bite, and herding temperament.

akc-belgian-sheepdog-breed-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Belgian Sheepdog Dog Breed Information
akc-belgian-sheepdog-breed-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile covering Belgian history (Château de Groenendael, Nicolas Rose), World War I sentry work, published weight (45-75 lbs / approx. 20-34 kg), lifespan (12-14 years), temperament, and grooming.

the-kennel-club-belgian-shepherd-dog-gro.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Belgian Shepherd Dog (Groenendael) Breed Standard
the-kennel-club-belgian-shepherd-dog-gro.note: Official Royal Kennel Club breed standard (Pastoral Group) confirming withers height (dogs 61-66 cm / 24-26 in; bitches 56-61 cm / 22-24 in), square proportions, long black coat with collarette, and working sheepdog temperament.

ukc-belgian-shepherd-dog-breed-standard.name: United Kennel Club - Belgian Shepherd Dog Breed Standard
ukc-belgian-shepherd-dog-breed-standard.note: Official UKC breed standard (Herding Dog Group, recognized 1991) covering conformation, square proportions, four coat varieties including Groenendael, height, weight, and herding behavior.

ofa-belgian-sheepdog-chic-requirements.name: Orthopedic Foundation for Animals - Belgian Sheepdog CHIC Requirements
ofa-belgian-sheepdog-chic-requirements.note: Official OFA Canine Health Information Center (CHIC) testing requirements for the Belgian Sheepdog / Groenendael, mandating radiographic hip dysplasia evaluation, radiographic elbow dysplasia evaluation, and CAER eye examination.

scc-basset-bleu-de-gascogne-breed-standa.name: Société Centrale Canine - Standard et Profil du Basset Bleu de Gascogne
scc-basset-bleu-de-gascogne-breed-standa.note: Official French kennel club (SCC) breed profile and standard for the Basset Bleu de Gascogne, confirming historical Gascon origin, height (34-38 cm), weight range (approx. 16-20 kg), hunting trials, and pack hound traits.

ukc-basset-bleu-de-gascogne-breed-standa.note: Official UKC breed standard (Scenthound Group, recognized 1991) covering conformation, rectangular low-slung proportions, mottled blue coat, height (13.5 to 15 inches / 34-38 cm), and hunting behavior.

fci-croatian-shepherd-dog-official-stand.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 277 (valid standard dated 2014-05-27, published 2015-05-27). hks-hrvatski-ovcar-breed-standard.name: Hrvatski kinološki savez - Hrvatski ovčar Standard i Povijest

akc-croatian-sheepdog-breed-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Croatian Sheepdog Dog Breed Information

ukc-croatian-shepherd-dog-breed-standard.name: United Kennel Club - Croatian Shepherd Dog Breed Standard

fci-harrier-official-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 295 (valid standard dated 1974-05-27). fci-harrier-nomenclature.name: FCI - Harrier Breed Nomenclature (No. 295)

the-kennel-club-harrier-breed-standard.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Harrier Breed Standard

akc-harrier-breed-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Harrier Dog Breed Information
akc-harrier-breed-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile covering 13th-century English pack history (1260 Penistone pack), published weight (45-60 lbs / approx. 20-27 kg), lifespan (12-15 years), temperament, and grooming.

ofa-harrier-health-screenings.note: Orthopedic Foundation for Animals health database and veterinary screening guidelines for the Harrier, documenting evaluations for hip dysplasia, eye examinations (CAER), and elbow dysplasia.

kcp-perro-sin-pelo-del-peru-standard.note: Official Peruvian Kennel Club (Kennel Club Peruano / KCP) breed standard and profile for the Perro sin pelo del Perú, detailing pre-Columbian Moche and Chimú heritage, national patrimony status (Ley 27537), three sizes, two varieties, and skin health care.

akc-peruvian-inca-orchid-breed-standard.name: American Kennel Club - Official Standard of the Peruvian Inca Orchid

akc-peruvian-inca-orchid-breed-profile.name: American Kennel Club - Peruvian Inca Orchid Dog Breed Information

overview.summary: Distinguished by a sweeping, silky coat, topknot, and aristocratic carriage, the Afghan Hound is a tall sighthound shaped by centuries of hunting across mountain and desert terrain. Beneath its refined appearance is an agile, fast runner that bonds warmly with its household while staying self-possessed around unfamiliar people.
overview.description: The Afghan Hound pairs glamorous presentation with serious athletic capability. Its long, fine-textured coat parts neatly along the spine, leaving a short, close-lying saddle across the back of mature dogs, while a long silky topknot crowns a refined skull and prominent hipbones anchor powerful hindquarters. Indoors, an adult with sufficient exercise is typically calm, affectionate, and quietly playful with trusted family members, yet noticeably aloof toward strangers. Because sighthound instincts remain deeply ingrained, any darting movement outdoors can trigger an immediate, high-speed chase, making tall, secure fencing and disciplined lead management essential. Prospective households should also plan for intensive coat maintenance, as the flowing furnishings tangle rapidly without structured brushing and bathing.
overview.history: Sighthounds of this distinct type developed across the mountains, plains, and high valleys of Afghanistan and neighboring regions, where local hunters relied on their keen vision, stamina, and sure-footed agility to course fast quarry over stony ground. Different regional varieties—spanning heavier-coated mountain hounds and lighter desert types—contributed to the dogs brought to Great Britain by returning military officers in the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries. British breeders consolidated those imports into the modern pedigree hound, establishing a unified type that soon gained international prominence both in the show ring and as a striking companion.
overview.originalPurpose: Coursing and capturing swift quarry by sight and speed across steep, rocky mountain slopes and open plains.
currentRoles: Devoted household companion
Conformation show competitor
Lure coursing and amateur racing athlete
Supervised running and outdoor fitness partner
Reward-based agility and scent-enrichment participant

physical.coatType: Long, very fine, silky hair covering the ribcage, forequarters, hindquarters, and flanks, paired with a flowing silky topknot and short, close-lying hair along the saddle from the shoulders backward in mature dogs.
physical.coatLength: Long over the body, limbs, ears, and topknot; short and close across the mature back saddle and down the foreface.
physical.sheddingLevel: Low to moderate visible fallout in the home because shed hairs frequently catch inside the long outer coat until brushed out
physical.droolingLevel: Low
distinctiveFeatures: Long, fine, silky coat contrasted by a short, smooth saddle along the back in mature dogs
Flowing silky topknot over the skull and long, low-set ears covered in silky hair
Refined, elongated head with dark, nearly triangular eyes and a distant, dignified gaze
Prominent, widely spaced hipbones and a level back line from shoulders to loin
Large, broad feet thickly covered in long hair for traction over rough ground

exercise.level: High
activities: Brisk daily lead walks
Free galloping inside a tall, fully enclosed paddock or yard

grooming.level: Very high for a full coat
grooming.brushing: Several thorough line-brushing sessions each week using a pin brush and detangling mist; never brush the fine coat while completely dry
grooming.bathing: Every 1 to 3 weeks for hounds kept in full coat, followed by conditioning and careful blow-drying to prevent friction knots
notes: Mist each coat section lightly with diluted conditioner or detangling spray before brushing so delicate hair shafts do not snap.
Pay close attention to friction zones behind the ears, under the elbows, around the groin, and between the toes where mats form fastest.
Use a snood or ear wrap during meals and messy chews to keep the long ear fringes clean and dry.
Leave the saddle and facial hair to develop naturally rather than clipping or shaving unless a companion trim is deliberately chosen for practical maintenance.

training.difficulty: Moderate to challenging; sensitive and observant, yet independent and quickly disengaged by harsh or repetitive drills
tips: Keep training sessions brief, upbeat, and reward-based, using high-value food treats or toy play rather than physical corrections.
Practice recall inside enclosed spaces, but never rely on verbal recall alone to override sighthound chase instincts in unfenced areas.
Introduce the grooming table, bath routine, blow-dryer, nail care, and gentle ear handling calmly from early puppyhood.
Build calm household manners and impulse control around doorways and gates to prevent sudden bolting after outdoor movement.
training.socialization: Early, unhurried exposure to diverse people, polite dogs, household sounds, veterinary handling, and grooming tools helps counter natural aloofness and builds confident adult composure.

climates: Cool and temperate climates
Warm climates when indoor cooling, shade, and early-morning or evening exercise are provided
livingEnvironment.aloneTimeTolerance: Moderate when physical exercise and mental companionship needs are met, though prolonged isolation can lead to boredom or anxious vocalising.

nutrition.dietType: Complete, balanced commercial diet (kibble, wet, or veterinary-formulated fresh ration) suited to large, athletic sighthounds

feedingFrequency.puppy: 3 to 4 meals daily during rapid skeletal growth, transitioning to 2 meals daily as maturity approaches
feedingFrequency.adult: 2 measured meals per day rather than a single large portion
feedingFrequency.senior: 2 smaller, easily digestible meals per day adjusted for activity level and lean muscle preservation

nutrition.guidelines: Feed to preserve a lean, athletic sighthound outline—this breed bears prominent hipbones by structure, so avoid overfeeding in an attempt to cover the pelvic bones with excess fat.
considerations: As a deep-chested hound, divide the daily ration into at least two meals and avoid vigorous running or rough play immediately before and after eating to help reduce gastric dilatation-volvulus risk.
Because prominent pinbones are normal anatomical features in this breed, assess body condition across the lower ribs and loin muscle rather than judging by hipbone visibility alone.
Protect long ear feathering from wet food and water bowls by offering narrow-mouthed dishes or fitting a clean fabric snood at mealtimes.
nutrition.note: Tailor exact calorie intake and diet formulation with a veterinarian according to age, coat condition, exercise workload, and medical history.

health.overview: Generally a long-lived large hound when bred from health-screened stock, though owners and veterinarians should monitor for sighthound-specific concerns including deep-chested bloat, ophthalmic disorders, autoimmune thyroid disease, chylothorax, and sensitivity to certain anaesthetic agents.
commonConditions: Hip dysplasia
Autoimmune thyroiditis (hypothyroidism)
Ocular conditions (including juvenile cataracts and corneal dystrophy)
Gastric dilatation-volvulus (bloat)
Idiopathic chylothorax (accumulation of lymphatic fluid in the chest cavity)
Hereditary myelopathy (rare degenerative spinal cord disorder)
Sighthound anaesthesia and low-body-fat drug sensitivity
Ear canal irritation beneath heavy ear feathering
preventiveCare: Routine veterinary wellness exams, core vaccinations, and year-round parasite prevention
Feeding split meals and enforcing rest around mealtimes to minimise bloat triggers
Confirming that the veterinary team uses sighthound-safe anaesthetic protocols prior to any surgical or dental procedure
Weekly inspection of ear canals, skin folds under the coat, and hair between the paw pads
Regular nail trimming and paw-pad conditioning to preserve sound foot posture
recommendedScreenings: Radiographic hip evaluation through a recognized orthopaedic screening scheme
Comprehensive eye examination by a board-certified veterinary ophthalmologist
Autoimmune thyroiditis panel through an accredited veterinary diagnostic laboratory
health.dentalCare: Brush teeth several times per week with canine toothpaste and schedule periodic veterinary dental assessments under sighthound-appropriate anaesthesia protocols.
health.earCare: Lift the heavy, silky ear leather weekly to check for trapped moisture, wax buildup, or odour, and keep ear fringes clean and dry after meals and baths.
health.skinCare: Part the long coat down to the skin during brushing to spot hidden mats, grass awns, ticks, or localized irritation early, and rinse out shampoo and conditioner thoroughly.

idealFor: Experienced owners who appreciate independent sighthound temperament and gentle, reward-based handling
Households prepared to invest several hours each week in structured coat brushing and bathing
Homes with a tall, securely fenced yard or regular access to enclosed running areas
Quiet or adult-led families with respectful, older children who give the dog calm personal space
Enthusiasts of conformation showing, lure coursing, or active outdoor walking
notIdealFor: Owners seeking a low-maintenance, wash-and-wear coat
People who expect instant, off-lead obedience in unfenced spaces
Busy households unable to provide daily opportunities for brisk exercise and safe sprinting
Very boisterous homes where rough handling could startle a sensitive hound

funFacts: Despite its glamorous, floor-length coat, the Afghan Hound was shaped as a rugged mountain and desert hunter capable of pursuing swift game across steep, rocky ground.
Mature adults naturally develop a short, smooth saddle of hair along the back while retaining flowing, silky furnishings on the legs, flanks, and chest.
The breed's unusually large, wide, heavily furred paws act like protective pads over jagged stones and extreme ground temperatures.
A silky topknot on the skull and a gentle ring or curve at the tip of the tail are classic hallmarks of the breed's silhouette.

faq.question: Why are an Afghan Hound's hipbones so noticeable?
faq.answer: High, prominent, widely set hipbones are a normal anatomical feature of the breed rather than a sign of underfeeding. They contribute to the hound's flexible rear assembly and agility over uneven terrain.

faq.question: How much grooming does an Afghan Hound really need?
faq.answer: A hound kept in full coat requires several hours of careful line-brushing every week plus regular bathing, conditioning, and blow-drying. Brushing the fine hair dry causes static and breakage, so sections should always be lightly misted first.

faq.question: Can an Afghan Hound be trusted off lead in open areas?
faq.answer: Generally no. As a sighthound bred to spot and chase distant motion at high speed, an Afghan Hound can ignore recall cues the moment prey or a fast-moving object appears. Off-lead running should take place only inside tall, fully enclosed fencing.

faq.question: Are Afghan Hounds difficult to train?
faq.answer: They are intelligent and observant, but they think independently and were never bred for repetitive obedience drills. Short, gentle, reward-based sessions work far better than stern or forceful methods.

faq.question: Do Afghan Hounds shed heavily?
faq.answer: They shed less loose hair onto furniture than many dense-coated breeds because shed strands stay caught within the long silky coat until removed during regular brushing and bathing.

faq.question: What health screenings should prospective buyers ask about?
faq.answer: Prospective owners should ask breeders for documented hip evaluations, current veterinary ophthalmologist eye examination results, and autoimmune thyroiditis panel clearances for both parent dogs.
